words.en: A barbecue is a meal or gathering at which meat, fish, or other food is cooked out of doors on a rack over an open fire or on a special appliance.

words.ex: The tree has bare branches in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天有光秃秃的树枝。
words.en: If part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.ex: I found a great bargain at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场上找到了一件便宜货。
words.en: A bargain is an agreement between two people or groups in which each promises to do something in exchange for something else. It can also refer to something bought or offered for sale much more cheaply than is usual or expected.

words.ex: Barium is a chemical element with the symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
words.ex_cn: 钡是一种化学元素，符号为Ba，原子序数为56。
words.en: Barium is a chemical element with the symbol Ba and atomic number 56. It is a soft, silvery alkaline earth metal.

words.tr:
n. 树皮；
v. 狗吠；
words.ex: The dog climbed the tree and touched the bark.
words.ex_cn: 狗爬上了树，摸了摸树皮。
words.en: The sound a dog makes; the outer covering of a tree.

words.ex: The farmer stores hay in the barn.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把干草存放在谷仓里。
words.en: A barn is a large building on a farm in which crops or animals are kept.

words.tr: n. [无脊椎] 藤壶；茗荷介；难以摆脱的人；黑雁
words.ex: The barnacle sticks to the bottom of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 藤壶粘在船底。
words.en: A barnacle is a type of arthropod constituting the infraclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea, and is hence related to crabs and lobsters. Barnacles are exclusively marine, and tend to live in shallow and tidal waters, typically in erosive settings.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.ex: He poured water into a wooden barrel.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进一个木桶里。
words.en: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food, typically made of wood or metal.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.ex: The castle is a bastion of safety.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是安全的堡垒。
words.en: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification built at an angle to the line of a wall, so as to allow defensive fire in several directions.

words.ex: The bather walked into the sea slowly.
words.ex_cn: 游泳者慢慢走进海里。
words.en: A bather is a person who is swimming or washing in a body of water.

words.ex: The castle was surrounded by a wall with battlement.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被带有城垛的墙包围着。
words.en: A battlement is a parapet at the top of a wall, especially of a fort or castle, that has regularly spaced squared openings for shooting through.

words.ex: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星向地球发射信号。
words.en: A beam is a long, thick piece of wood, metal, or concrete that is used to support the roof of a building. It can also refer to a line of light that shines from a bright object, or a smile that shows someone is very happy.

words.tr: n. 兽性，淫猥，令人恶心的食物
words.ex: The beastliness of the scene made her sick.
words.ex_cn: 这令人作呕的场面让她感到恶心。
words.en: The quality of being like a beast; cruelty or savagery.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.ex: He is bedridden after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后卧床不起。
words.en: If someone is bedridden, they are so ill or disabled that they cannot get out of bed.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: The beggar sat on the street with a cup.
words.ex_cn: 那个乞丐坐在街上，手里拿着一个杯子。
words.en: A beggar is a person who lives by asking people for money or food.

words.ex: The walls are beige.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁是米黄色的。
words.en: A pale sandy yellowish-brown color.

words.tr:
v. 打嗝；冒出
n. 嗝
words.ex: He belched after eating the big meal.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完这顿大餐后打了个嗝。
words.en: To expel gas noisily from the stomach through the mouth; to emit or discharge something forcefully.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: He packed his belongings before moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他在搬去新城市前收拾好了自己的所有物。
words.en: Your belongings are the things that you own, especially things that are small enough to be carried.

words.ex: He sat on the bench in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在公园的长凳上。
words.en: A bench is a long seat for several people, typically made of wood or metal.

words.ex: This test is a benchmark for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试是所有学生的标准。
words.en: A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲处；
v. （使）弯曲；
words.ex: The car turned at the bend in the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在道路的拐弯处转弯了。
words.en: To bend something means to change its shape so that it is no longer straight but curved.

words.tr: n. 恩人；捐助者；赠送者
words.ex: The benefactor gave money to the school.
words.ex_cn: 资助人捐钱给学校。
words.en: A benefactor is a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.ex: The new policy will affect the company beneficially.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将对公司产生有益的影响。
words.en: In a way that is helpful or advantageous.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The storm benighted us, leaving us stranded on the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨使我们陷入黑暗，让我们被困在山上。
words.en: To overtake with darkness or night; to involve in intellectual or moral darkness.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: He picked a red berry from the bush.
words.ex_cn: 他从灌木丛中摘了一颗红色浆果。
words.en: A berry is a small, round fruit that grows on a bush or a tree. Some berries are edible and can be eaten raw or used in cooking.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He felt deep pain from his friend's betrayal.
words.ex_cn: 他因朋友的背叛感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: The action of betraying one's country, a group, or a person; treachery.

words.ex: A bevy of birds flew over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过湖面。
words.en: A bevy of people or things is a group of them, especially a group of women or girls.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.ex: The bidder won the auction with the highest offer.
words.ex_cn: 这位出价者以最高出价赢得了拍卖。
words.en: A bidder is a person or organization that offers to pay a particular amount of money for something that is being sold.

words.ex: The two countries signed a bilateral agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项双边协议。
words.en: Involving or affecting two parties, countries, etc.

words.ex: The ad is on a big billboard near the road.
words.ex_cn: 广告牌在路边的大广告牌上。
words.en: A billboard is a large outdoor board for displaying advertisements.

words.tr: n. 兵舍，工作职位 v. 给（部队）安排住处
words.ex: The soldiers were billeted in the local school during the training period.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在训练期间被安置在当地学校。
words.en: A billet is a place for soldiers to live temporarily, or a job or position that someone has been given.

words.tr: n. 演员表；演员次序；营业额
words.ex: The billing at the end of the movie listed all the actors.
words.ex_cn: 电影结尾的演员表列出了所有演员。
words.en: The process of preparing and sending invoices to customers for goods or services provided.

words.ex: He bind the books with string.
words.ex_cn: 他用绳子把书捆起来。
words.en: To tie something or someone tightly or to fasten something.

words.ex: The car runs on biofuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车使用生物燃料行驶。
words.en: Biofuel is a type of energy derived from renewable biological sources, such as plants or animal waste, used as an alternative to fossil fuels.

words.ex: The biographer wrote about the artist's life.
words.ex_cn: 传记作家写了这位艺术家的一生。
words.en: A biographer is a person who writes an account of someone's life.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: This is a biological experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个生物学实验。
words.en: Relating to biology or living organisms.

words.ex: The biopic chronicles the life of a famous scientist.
words.ex_cn: 这部传记片记录了一位著名科学家的生平。
words.en: A biopic is a film that tells the story of the life of a real person, often a well-known historical figure or celebrity.

words.ex: Bioscience is a rapidly advancing field with many applications in medicine.
words.ex_cn: 生物科学是一个在医学中有许多应用的快速发展领域。
words.en: Bioscience is any of the life sciences, such as biology, biochemistry, or biophysics, especially when applied to practical problems in areas such as medicine, agriculture, or the environment.

words.ex: The birch trees have white bark.
words.ex_cn: 桦树有白色的树皮。
words.en: A birch is a type of tree with thin branches and a smooth trunk, which is often white or silver in color.

words.ex: He lives in Birmingham with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人住在伯明翰。
words.en: A city in central England, known for its industrial heritage, vibrant cultural scene, and diverse communities.

words.ex: The road was paved with bituminous asphalt.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是用沥青混凝土铺成的。
words.en: Containing or resembling bitumen.

words.tr:
n. 黑名单
v. 将…列入黑名单
words.ex: He was added to the blacklist for his fraudulent activities.
words.ex_cn: 他因欺诈行为被列入了黑名单。
words.en: A list of people, organizations, or countries that are being shunned or excluded by others because they are considered to be untrustworthy or undesirable.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.ex: He feels pain in his bladder.
words.ex_cn: 他感到膀胱疼痛。
words.en: A bladder is a part of your body that is shaped like a bag and holds urine until it is passed out of the body.

words.tr: adj. 无可责难的；清白无辜的
words.ex: He was blameless in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中是无罪的。
words.en: If you say that someone is blameless, you mean that they have not done anything wrong.

words.tr:
n. 毛毯；厚的覆盖物；
adj. 包括所有的；
words.ex: He wrapped himself in a warm blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己裹在一条温暖的毛毯里。
words.en: A blanket is a large piece of woolen or similar material used as a covering on a bed or elsewhere for warmth.

words.ex: He blatantly broke the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他公然违反了规则。
words.en: If you describe something as blatant, you mean that it is very obvious and you think that it is done to shock or offend people.

words.tr:
n. 烈火；火焰；闪耀
v. 闪耀；熊熊燃烧；发亮光
words.ex: The fire began to blaze in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 火在森林里开始猛烈燃烧。
words.en: A blaze is a very large or fiercely burning fire that is difficult to control.

words.tr: n. 幸事； v. “bless”的现在分词；
words.ex: Finding a good job after graduation was a blessing.
words.ex_cn: 毕业后找到一份好工作是一件幸事。
words.en: A blessing is a prayer asking for God's favor and protection, or a beneficial thing for which one is grateful.

words.ex: The blight destroyed the potato crops.
words.ex_cn: 这种枯萎病摧毁了马铃薯作物。
words.en: A blight is something that spoils or damages something, or a disease that affects plants.

words.ex: The roses are in bloom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 玫瑰在春天开花。
words.en: When a plant or tree blooms, it produces flowers. The period during which a plant or tree produces flowers is also known as its bloom.

words.tr:
n. （果树的）花朵；
v. 开花；
words.ex: The apple tree is full of blossom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，苹果树上开满了花。
words.en: When a tree or plant blossoms, it produces flowers before producing fruit that can be eaten.

words.tr: n. 宽松的女短衫；女衬衫
words.ex: She wears a white blouse to work.
words.ex_cn: 她上班穿一件白色上衣。
words.en: A blouse is a piece of clothing for women, which covers their body from the neck to the waist or slightly below, and which usually has long sleeves and buttons down the front.

words.ex: The architect showed us the blueprint of the new house.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师给我们看了新房子的蓝图。
words.en: A blueprint is a detailed plan or design of something, often used in the context of buildings or machinery, which shows how it is to be made or how it will work.

words.ex: He bluntly said he did not like the food.
words.ex_cn: 他直率地说他不喜欢这食物。
words.en: If you say something bluntly, you say it very directly, without trying to be polite or to hide unpleasant facts.

words.tr:
n. 脸红；羞愧
v. 泛红；羞愧
words.ex: He felt shy and got a blush when she praised him.
words.ex_cn: 当他被她夸奖时，他感到害羞，脸红了。
words.en: If you blush, your face turns red because you are embarrassed or ashamed.

words.tr:
n. 板；董事会；
v. 上船（或火车、飞机等）；
words.ex: He nailed the picture to the board.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片钉在板上。
words.en: A board is a flat, thin, rectangular piece of wood or other material used for a particular purpose, such as cutting food on or as a surface for writing or playing games. It can also refer to a group of people who manage or control a company or organization, or to the meals provided by an institution such as a school or hospital. As a verb, it means to get onto a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle, or to provide meals and lodging for someone.

words.ex: The boarder eats dinner with the family.
words.ex_cn: 这个寄宿生和家人一起吃晚饭。
words.en: A boarder is someone who pays to live and receive meals in someone else's house, or a student who lives at school during the term.

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.ex: The water begins to boil at 100 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 水在100度时开始沸腾。
words.en: When a liquid boils or when you boil it, it reaches the temperature at which it starts to turn into a gas.

words.tr: adj. 勇敢的； n. 明显的( bold的比较级 )；
words.ex: He made a bolder decision to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了更勇敢的决定，勇敢地说出了自己的想法。
words.en: Comparative form of 'bold', meaning more willing to take risks or more confident in facing challenges.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.tr:
n. 纽带；联系；债券；保释金；协定
v. （使）黏合；相互联结
words.ex: Family is the bond that keeps us together.
words.ex_cn: 家庭是我们团结的纽带。
words.en: A bond between people is a strong feeling of friendship, love, or shared beliefs and experiences that unites them.

words.tr: adj. 如骨的；多骨的；瘦骨嶙峋的
words.ex: He has a bony hand that looks thin and weak.
words.ex_cn: 他有一只骨瘦如柴的手，看起来又细又弱。
words.en: If you describe someone as bony, you mean that they are very thin so that their bones stick out.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr: n. 生育高峰中出生的人
words.ex: My dad is a boomer who loves classic rock.
words.ex_cn: 我爸爸是个婴儿潮一代，喜欢经典摇滚。
words.en: A boomer is a person born during the baby boom, especially in the US between 1946 and 1965, or something that makes a loud, deep sound.

words.tr:
n. 飞去来器；回旋镖；回力镖
v. 自食其果；害人反害己
words.ex: He threw the boomerang and it came back to him.
words.ex_cn: 他扔出了回旋镖，它又飞回到他身边。
words.en: A boomerang is a curved piece of wood which comes back to you if you throw it correctly. It is used by Australian Aborigines for hunting and for sport.

words.tr: v. 快速发展；“boom”的现在分词； adj. 急速发展的；暴涨的；繁荣发展的；
words.ex: The tech industry is booming.
words.ex_cn: 科技行业正在快速发展。
words.en: Experiencing a period of great prosperity or rapid economic growth.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.tr: n. 借用的言语（或思想等）； v. 借；借用；“borrow”的现在分词；
words.ex: His poem shows a lot of borrowing from old folk tales.
words.ex_cn: 他的诗大量借用民间故事的言语。
words.en: The act of taking and using something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it.

words.tr: n. 罐头食品中毒，肉毒中毒，肉毒杆菌中毒
words.ex: Botulism is a rare but serious illness caused by a toxin that attacks the body's nerves.
words.ex_cn: 肉毒中毒是一种由毒素攻击身体神经的罕见但严重的疾病。
words.en: Botulism is a rare but serious condition caused by toxins from bacteria called Clostridium botulinum. These toxins attack the nervous system and can cause paralysis, breathing difficulties, and even death.

words.tr:
n. 弹跳；跳动；
v. 弹跳；反弹；
words.ex: The ball had a high bounce on the concrete.
words.ex_cn: 球在混凝土上弹跳得很高。
words.en: If something bounces or if you bounce it, it moves away from a surface after hitting it.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.ex: He ate soup from a bowl.
words.ex_cn: 他从碗里吃汤。
words.en: A bowl is a round container with a wide uncovered top. Some kinds of bowl are used, for example, for serving or eating food from, or in cooking, while other larger kinds are often used for washing or other purposes.

words.ex: The boxer trained every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位拳击手每天早上训练。
words.en: A boxer is someone who takes part in the sport of boxing, or a breed of dog with a short coat and a square-shaped muzzle.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: He moved up to a higher bracket after his promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他升职后进入了更高的等级。
words.en: A bracket is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is fastened to a wall in order to support something such as a shelf. In writing, brackets are symbols that are used to separate words or numbers.

words.ex: We will brainstorm ideas for the project tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将为这个项目集思广益。
words.en: To brainstorm is to try to solve a problem or come up with new ideas by having a group of people discuss it and all suggest ideas.

words.tr:
n. 刹车；制动器
v. 刹车
words.ex: He pressed the brake to stop the car.
words.ex_cn: 他踩了刹车来停车。
words.en: A brake is a device in a vehicle that makes it go slower or stop.

words.tr: v. 污辱；打上...的烙印；“brand”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有品牌的；
words.ex: The scandal branded him as a liar.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻污辱了他，让他被视为骗子。
words.en: Marked with a brand or trademark; having a brand name.

words.ex: The brawl started over a simple misunderstanding.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误解。
words.en: A brawl is a rough or noisy fight or quarrel.

words.tr:
adj. 巴西的；
n. 巴西人；
words.ex: She loves Brazilian music.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢巴西音乐。
words.en: Brazilian means belonging or relating to Brazil, or to its people or culture.

words.ex: The course covers a wide breadth of topics.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程涵盖了广泛的主题。
words.en: The distance or measurement from side to side of something; width.

words.ex: He is the breadwinner in his family.
words.ex_cn: 他是家里的经济支柱。
words.en: A breadwinner is a person who earns money to support their family.

words.ex: The breakage of the glass was accidental.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃的破碎是意外造成的。
words.en: Breakage refers to the act of breaking something or the state of being broken, or an instance of this. It can also refer to the items that have been broken.

words.tr: n. 崩溃；故障；细目分类；
words.ex: The stress led to a breakdown.
words.ex_cn: 压力导致了崩溃。
words.en: A breakdown is a failure of a system, machine, or relationship, or a sudden collapse in someone's mental health.

words.tr: n. 断路器；破碎机；碎浪
words.ex: The breaker turned off when the power overloaded.
words.ex_cn: 当电力过载时，断路器跳闸了。
words.en: A breaker is a device that stops the flow of electricity in a circuit when the current becomes too strong, or a wave that breaks into foam on the shore.

words.ex: He drove at a breakneck speed down the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 他以惊险的速度沿着山路开车。
words.en: If you say that something happens or travels at breakneck speed, you mean that it happens or travels very fast.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.ex: The soldier loaded the bullet into the breech of the gun.
words.ex_cn: 士兵把子弹装入枪的后膛。
words.en: The lower part of the body in humans, between the legs; the part of a gun or cannon behind the bore.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: A gentle breeze blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵微风轻轻吹过树梢。
words.en: A breeze is a gentle wind.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.ex: The sun brightens the room in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早上使房间变亮。
words.en: To make something lighter or more colorful, or to make someone feel happier or more hopeful.

words.ex: The young pianist played with great brilliancy.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻钢琴家用极高的才华演奏。
words.en: The quality of being brilliant, especially in terms of intelligence or talent.

words.tr:
n. 盐水；卤水；咸水；海水
v. 用盐水处理
words.ex: She put the fish in brine to preserve it.
words.ex_cn: 她把鱼放在盐水中腌制以保存它。
words.en: Brine is water that contains a high concentration of salt, used especially for preserving food.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: n. 广播员；广播公司；节目主持人；电视台
words.ex: The broadcaster announced the news on TV.
words.ex_cn: 广播员在电视上宣布了新闻。
words.en: A broadcaster is a person or organization that transmits programs or information by radio or television.

words.ex: Reading books can broaden your mind.
words.ex_cn: 读书可以扩大你的视野。
words.en: If something broadens or if you broaden it, it increases in size or range.

words.ex: I eat broccoli with dinner every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天晚餐都吃西兰花。
words.en: Broccoli is a vegetable with a green flower head and a thick stalk, eaten as a vegetable.

words.tr: n. 溴（元素符号为 Br）
words.ex: Bromine is a chemical element with the symbol Br.
words.ex_cn: 溴是一种化学元素，符号为Br。
words.en: Bromine is a chemical element with the symbol Br and atomic number 35. It is a halogen, and is a fuming red-brown liquid at room temperature that evaporates readily to form a similarly coloured gas.

words.ex: She tried to browbeat him into submission.
words.ex_cn: 她试图恫吓他屈服。
words.en: To intimidate or bully someone into doing something, especially by using threats or aggressive behavior.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.tr: n. 不伦瑞克（德国东部城市）
words.ex: Brunswick is known for its historical architecture.
words.ex_cn: 不伦瑞克以其历史建筑而闻名。
words.en: A type of sausage or a style of clothing, or a city in Germany, depending on context.

words.tr: n. 滑稽；丑态；插科打诨
words.ex: The play was filled with buffoonery to entertain the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部戏充满了滑稽表演，以娱乐观众。
words.en: Buffoonery refers to behavior that is ridiculous but amusing, often involving silly jokes or actions.

words.ex: The builder constructed a new house last month.
words.ex_cn: 这位营造商上个月建造了一栋新房子。
words.en: A builder is a person whose job is to build or repair houses and other buildings.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: The bulldozer cleared the path for the new road.
words.ex_cn: 推土机为新道路清理了路径。
words.en: A bulldozer is a large tractor with a blade in front, used for moving earth and rocks in construction work.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.ex: They live in a small bungalow near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在公园附近的一座小平房里。
words.en: A bungalow is a small house, usually having one story.

words.ex: The buoyancy of the water helps the boat float.
words.ex_cn: 水的浮力帮助船漂浮。
words.en: Buoyancy is the ability of something to float in a liquid or to rise in air or gas.

words.ex: He eats a burger for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃一个汉堡。
words.en: A burger is a flat round mass of minced meat or vegetables, which is fried and often eaten in a bread roll.

words.tr: n. 城市居民；市民；公民
words.ex: The burgher voted in the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 市民在城镇会议上投票了。
words.en: A burgher is a citizen of a town or city, especially a member of the middle class.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.tr: adj. （女子外表、举止、穿着）男性化的，男人腔的；（男子）高大的; n. 充当男性角色的女同性恋...
words.ex: She wears short hair and suits, looking very butch.
words.ex_cn: 她留着短发，穿着西装，看起来非常男性化。
words.en: A butch person is someone, especially a woman, who behaves and dresses in a traditionally male way.

words.ex: She spread butter on her toast.
words.ex_cn: 她在吐司上抹了黄油。
words.en: Butter is a pale yellow edible fatty substance made by churning cream and used as a spread or in cooking.

words.ex: He hurt his buttock when he fell on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒在地板上时伤到了臀部。
words.en: One of the two rounded parts of the body that form the bottom.

words.tr: n. 流行行话；时髦词汇；
words.ex: The new app uses buzzwords like 'smart' and 'AI' to attract users.
words.ex_cn: 这款新应用使用了‘智能’和‘人工智能’等流行行话来吸引用户。
words.en: A buzzword is a word or phrase, often jargon, that becomes very popular for a period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 过去的
n. 过去的事
words.ex: He liked to talk about bygone days with his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢和祖父谈论过去的时光。
words.en: Belonging to an earlier time.

words.tr: n. （报刊文章顶部的）作者署名行
words.ex: The journalist's byline was prominently displayed at the top of the article.
words.ex_cn: 记者的署名显眼地显示在文章的顶部。
words.en: A byline is a line at the head of a newspaper or magazine article giving the author's name.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.ex: He calculates the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算出总成本。
words.en: To determine by mathematical methods; compute.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the calf every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂小牛。
words.en: A calf is a young cow or bull. It can also refer to the fleshy part of the back of the human leg below the knee.

words.ex: This food has high caloric content.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物热量很高。
words.en: relating to heat or calories

words.ex: The politician faced numerous calumniations during the campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家在竞选期间遭受了许多诽谤。
words.en: The act of making false and defamatory statements about someone; slander.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: The boat travels through the canal.
words.ex_cn: 船通过运河航行。
words.en: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.

words.tr: n. 取消；撤销；作废；中止；
words.ex: The flight cancellation made us wait for a new ticket.
words.ex_cn: 航班取消让我们不得不等待新的机票。
words.en: The act of cancelling something; a situation in which something that has been arranged is stopped from happening.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: He capitalized on the chance to start a business.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了这个创业的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to use something to your advantage, especially in a way that brings financial gain. It can also mean to write or print a word with its first letter as a capital letter.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.tr: adj. 资本主义的；资本家的
words.ex: He lives in a capitalistic society.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在一个资本主义社会。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by capitalism, an economic system based on private ownership of the means of production and their operation for profit.

words.ex: The captive man sat quietly in his cell.
words.ex_cn: 那个被监禁的人安静地坐在牢房里。
words.en: A captive is someone who is being kept as a prisoner or in a confined space, or something that is held or confined.

words.ex: Bread and rice are rich in carbohydrate.
words.ex_cn: 面包和米饭富含碳水化合物。
words.en: A carbohydrate is a substance found in foods such as bread, potatoes, and rice which provides your body with heat and energy and which consists of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

words.ex: He saw a cardiologist for his heart pain.
words.ex_cn: 他因为心痛去看了一位心脏病专家。
words.en: A cardiologist is a doctor who specializes in the study or treatment of heart diseases and heart abnormalities.

words.tr: n. 照顾者；护理者；看护者
words.ex: The caregiver helps the old man every day.
words.ex_cn: 这位照护者每天帮助这位老人。
words.en: A caregiver is someone who is responsible for looking after another person, especially a family member who is sick, elderly, or disabled.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.ex: He is a carrier of the flu virus.
words.ex_cn: 他是流感病毒的携带者。
words.en: A carrier is a person or thing that carries, holds, or conveys something.

words.ex: He put the milk in a carton.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶倒进了硬纸盒里。
words.en: A carton is a box or container usually made of cardboard or plastic, used for holding goods.

words.ex: The company's cashflow improved significantly after the new management took over.
words.ex_cn: 新管理层接手后，公司的现金流量显著改善。
words.en: The movement of money into and out of a business, especially as affecting liquidity.

words.tr: n. 首饰盒，匣子，<美>棺材
words.ex: She kept her most precious jewels in a small casket.
words.ex_cn: 她把她最珍贵的珠宝放在一个小匣子里。
words.en: A casket is a box used for holding the body of a dead person for burial, or a small box for keeping valuable items such as jewelry.

words.ex: The teacher gave castigation to the student who cheated.
words.ex_cn: 老师惩罚了作弊的学生。
words.en: Castigation is the act of criticizing or punishing someone severely.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.tr: v. 将…分类；把…加以归类
words.ex: We categorize books by genre.
words.ex_cn: 我们按类型对书籍进行分类。
words.en: To categorize means to put people or things into groups according to their type or characteristics.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr: v. 满足需要；“cater”的现在分词； n. 包办饮食；
words.ex: The new service is catering to the needs of students.
words.ex_cn: 这项新服务正在满足学生的需求。
words.en: The business of providing food and drink for events or occasions.

words.ex: The cathedral has tall towers and stained glass windows.
words.ex_cn: 这座大教堂有高高的塔楼和彩绘玻璃窗。
words.en: A cathedral is a very large and important church which has a bishop in charge of it.

words.tr: n. 高加索（亚洲和欧洲之间的山脉地区）
words.ex: The Caucasus is known for its diverse cultures and languages.
words.ex_cn: 高加索地区以其多元的文化和语言而闻名。
words.en: The Caucasus is a region at the border of Europe and Asia, situated between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, which includes the Caucasus Mountains and surrounding areas.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.ex: He gave a cautionary warning about the dangerous road.
words.ex_cn: 他针对这条危险的道路给出了一个警戒性的警告。
words.en: A cautionary story or warning is intended to make people aware of the possible dangers or problems of something.

words.tr: n. 警告；防止误解的说明；注意事项
words.ex: He gave me a warning, a caveat, before I signed the contract.
words.ex_cn: 我在签署合同之前，他给了我一个警告，一个注意事项。
words.en: A caveat is a warning of a specific limitation of something such as information or an agreement.

words.ex: The rain ceased after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，雨停了。
words.en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.

words.tr: n. （通常指永久性的）停火，停战; 停火命令
words.ex: The two countries agreed to a ceasefire after years of war.
words.ex_cn: 两国在多年战争后同意停火。
words.en: A ceasefire is an agreement in which countries or groups that are fighting each other agree to stop fighting.

words.tr: adj. 天空的；天体的；天国的；
words.ex: The celestial lights shone brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的光芒在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: Relating to the sky or the heavens; belonging or relating to heaven as the abode of the gods.

words.ex: He uses his cellphone to call his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机给妈妈打电话。
words.en: A cellphone is a telephone that does not have wires and works by radio, that you can carry with you and use anywhere.

words.ex: They used cement to build the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他们用水泥建造了这堵墙。
words.en: Cement is a powdery substance which is mixed with water and used for sticking things together or for making very hard surfaces.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.tr: n. （古希腊神话中的）半人半马怪
words.ex: The centaur has a human body and a horse's legs.
words.ex_cn: 半人马有人的身体和马的腿。
words.en: In Greek mythology, a centaur is a creature with the upper body of a human and the lower body and legs of a horse.

words.tr: v. 集中；形成中心；中央集权
words.ex: The company will centralize its offices in one city.
words.ex_cn: 公司将会把办公室集中到一个城市。
words.en: To centralize means to bring something under central control or to make something the center of attention or activity.

words.ex: The government is centrally located in the capital city.
words.ex_cn: 政府位于首都的中央。
words.en: In a central position or place; in or towards the centre.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

chapters.name: 第2周 高频词汇2500（上）星期三

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: He received a certification for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证明。
words.en: Certification is the act of certifying or the state of being certified, often involving the issuance of a certificate or official document attesting to a status or level of achievement.

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: The doctor checked her cervix during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查时查看了她的宫颈。
words.en: The cervix is the lower, narrow part of the uterus (womb). The cervix connects the main body of the uterus to the vagina (birth canal).

words.ex: The cessation of rain allowed us to go outside.
words.ex_cn: 雨停了，我们就能出去了。
words.en: The fact or process of ending or being brought to an end.

words.tr:
n. 圣歌；赞美诗；喊叫
v. 吟唱；诵扬；反复叫喊
words.ex: The monks sang a traditional chant during the morning prayer.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在晨祷时唱了一首传统圣歌。
words.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again. It can also refer to a simple song, especially one that is sung in a religious service.

words.ex: He characteristically arrived late to meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是特征性地迟到参加会议。
words.en: In a way that is typical of a particular person, thing, or group.

words.tr:
n. 收费；负责；指控；
v. 收费；充电；
words.ex: The hotel charge is $50 per night.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的收费是每晚50美元。
words.en: If you charge someone, you ask them to pay an amount of money for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.tr: v.制图，图表研究，图示行为法; 填图
words.ex: The team spent weeks charting the new coastline.
words.ex_cn: 团队花了几个星期绘制新的海岸线。
words.en: Charting refers to the process of making a map or detailed plan, especially of an area of land or sea, or a graphical representation of data.

words.tr: n. 话匣子；喋喋不休的人
words.ex: She was known as a chatterbox among her friends.
words.ex_cn: 她在朋友中以喋喋不休著称。
words.en: A chatterbox is someone who talks a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr: n. 清单；检查表；备忘录；目录册；
words.ex: He made a checklist for his trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为旅行列了一份清单。
words.en: A checklist is a list of items required, things to be done, or points to be considered, used as a reminder.

words.tr: n. 化疗；化学疗法；化学治疗
words.ex: He is receiving chemotherapy for cancer.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受化疗治疗癌症。
words.en: The treatment of disease by the use of chemical substances, especially the treatment of cancer by cytotoxic and other drugs.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.tr: adj. 挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: She is choosy about what she eats.
words.ex_cn: 她对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone as choosy, you mean they are very careful in choosing what they do or buy, and will only accept exactly what they want.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: He has been chronically ill since childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他从小长期患病。
words.en: In a way that continues for a long time or keeps happening, especially of a disease or problem.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

words.tr: n. （产于南美洲的）金鸡纳树，金鸡纳皮
words.ex: The bark of the cinchona tree is used to make quinine.
words.ex_cn: 金鸡纳树的树皮被用来制作奎宁。
words.en: Cinchona is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae containing at least 23 species of trees and shrubs, all native to the tropical Andes forests of western South America. They are known as sources of quinine and other alkaloids.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr: n. 全体市民；公民；市民
words.ex: The citizenry voted for new leaders.
words.ex_cn: 市民们投票选举了新领导人。
words.en: The citizenry refers to the body of citizens of a state or country.

words.ex: He applied for citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年申请了公民身份。
words.en: Citizenship is the status of being a citizen of a particular country.

words.ex: He asked for clarification about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他要求对规则进行澄清。
words.en: A clarification is a statement that makes something clear or easier to understand.

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.ex: The data is easily classifiable into different categories.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据很容易被分类到不同的类别中。
words.en: Able to be categorized or classified.

words.tr: n. 清洁；使清洁的人或物；清洁，使清洁的人或物 adj. 有去污作用的 v. 弄干净，清洗( cleanse的现在分词； v. 弄干净；清洗； adj. 有去污作用的；
words.ex: The cleansing of the river took many months.
words.ex_cn: 这条河的清洁花了好几个月。
words.en: The act of cleaning something, especially the skin.

words.ex: We need a clean-up after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后我们需要清理一下。
words.en: The act of making a place clean and tidy by removing dirt or unwanted items.

words.ex: The clearance of trash improved the park's appearance.
words.ex_cn: 清理垃圾改善了公园的外观。
words.en: Clearance refers to the process of removing or getting rid of something, or the space that is needed for one thing to move past another. It can also refer to the permission given for something to happen or be done.

words.tr: v. 清除；“clear”的现在分词； n. 空旷地；
words.ex: They are clearing the leaves from the yard.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在清除院子里的树叶。
words.en: A clearing is an open area in a forest where there are no trees or bushes.

words.ex: The glass showed a clear cleavage after it fell.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃掉落后出现了明显的裂纹。
words.en: Cleavage refers to the act of splitting or dividing something, especially along a natural line or grain. It can also refer to the space between a woman's breasts, especially as revealed by a low-cut garment.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.ex: He works in a clerical job at the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室做文书工作。
words.en: Clerical means relating to work that is done in an office, especially work that involves keeping records or accounts. It can also refer to the clergy or the religious leaders of a church.

words.ex: His cleverness helped him solve the puzzle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他的聪明帮助他快速解开了谜题。
words.en: The ability to understand and learn quickly and easily; intelligence.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the edge of the cliff.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边上。
words.en: A cliff is a high area of rock with a very steep side, often at the edge of the sea or a river.

words.tr:
v. 钉牢；用臂互抱；达成（协议等）；最终解决
n. 钉牢；扭抱
words.ex: He clinched the board to the wall with nails.
words.ex_cn: 他用钉子把木板钉在墙上。
words.en: To settle something conclusively; to secure or fasten something by flattening the ends of nails, screws, etc.

words.tr:
n. 斗篷；掩护物
v. 隐瞒；掩饰
words.ex: He wore a black cloak to hide his face.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件黑色斗篷来遮住脸。
words.en: A cloak is a long, loose outer garment which is worn over other clothes, especially in cold weather. It can also refer to something that hides or covers another thing.

words.ex: The old clock has a broken clockwork.
words.ex_cn: 这台老钟的钟表装置坏了。
words.en: A clockwork is a mechanism that operates in a very precise and regular way, often used in toys or small machines.

words.tr: n. 亲密；接近；密闭；狭窄
words.ex: The closeness of the two friends is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 这两位朋友之间的亲密显而易见。
words.en: The state of being close in space or time; intimacy or familiarity.

words.ex: We had a cloudless sky during our hike.
words.ex_cn: 我们在徒步旅行时天空晴朗无云。
words.en: If the sky is cloudless, there are no clouds in it.

words.tr: adj. 俱乐部的，喜交际的，资格要求严的
words.ex: The atmosphere at the party was very clubby.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上的气氛非常俱乐部化。
words.en: If you describe a group of people or their attitudes as clubby, you mean that they are friendly with each other but perhaps rather unwelcoming to people who are not in their group.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.tr: n. 年久失修的旧机器; 破旧不堪的汽车 ; 严重的错误; 大错
words.ex: The car is a real clunker, it breaks down every other day.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车真是破旧不堪，每隔一天就出故障。
words.en: A clunker is an old car that is in very bad condition.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.tr:
n. 杂乱；混乱
v. 弄乱
words.ex: The table is full of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上堆满了杂物。
words.en: If things or people clutter a place, they fill it in an untidy way.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: The boat travels along the coastline.
words.ex_cn: 船沿着海岸线航行。
words.en: The coastline is the outline of a coast, especially its shape and appearance.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: The cables are connected using a coaxial connector.
words.ex_cn: 电缆使用同轴连接器连接。
words.en: Coaxial refers to having a common axis, especially in the context of cables or components that share the same axis for efficient signal transmission.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: Pandas and bamboo coexist in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫和竹子在野外共存。
words.en: The state or fact of existing at the same time or in the same place.

words.ex: He saw a wooden coffin at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上看到一个木制棺材。
words.en: A coffin is a box in which a dead body is buried or cremated.

words.tr: n.  共同创办人；共同创始人
words.ex: He is a co-founder of the tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家科技公司的联合创始人。
words.en: A co-founder is one of a group of people who establish a company, organization, project, or system together.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: The story has good coherence, so it is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事很有连贯性，所以很容易理解。
words.en: Coherence is the quality of being logical and consistent.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.tr: n. 造币；货币；货币制度；新造的词语
words.ex: The new coinage was made of silver.
words.ex_cn: 新的硬币是用银制成的。
words.en: Coinage refers to the system of coins used in a country, or the process of making coins. It can also refer to the invention of new words or phrases.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: Coincidentally, we both arrived at the station at the same time.
words.ex_cn: 巧合的是，我们俩同时到达了车站。
words.en: In a way that happens by chance, especially in a surprising or interesting manner.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: The two companies worked together in collaboration.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司通过合作一起工作。
words.en: the act of working together with someone to produce or create something

words.ex: He is a collaborator in the science project.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个科学项目的协助者。
words.en: A collaborator is someone who works jointly on an activity or project; an associate.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: The collectivity worked together to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 集体一起努力打扫公园。
words.en: Collectivity refers to the quality or state of being collective, involving all members of a group rather than individuals.

words.ex: He is a collector of old coins.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位古钱币收藏家。
words.en: A collector is a person who collects things of a particular type as a hobby or for investment.

words.ex: The two cars collided at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 两辆车在十字路口相撞了。
words.en: If two or more moving people or objects collide, they crash into one another.

words.ex: The car crash was a serious collision.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次严重的碰撞。
words.en: A collision occurs when two or more objects come into contact with each other, often resulting in damage or a change in direction.

words.ex: The two companies were accused of collusion to fix prices.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司被指控串通操纵价格。
words.en: Collusion is secret or illegal cooperation or conspiracy, especially in order to cheat or deceive others.

words.ex: Europeans colonized many parts of Africa in the 1800s.
words.ex_cn: 欧洲人在19世纪开拓了非洲的许多地区。
words.en: To colonize means to send people to live in and govern another country.

words.ex: The argument was a colorable imitation of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 这个论点是对真相的似是而非的模仿。
words.en: If something is colorable, it can be colored or it is plausible but not necessarily true.

words.tr:
n. 颜料；染料；色素；（显示健康好坏的）脸色
v. 着色；“color”的现在分词
words.ex: The coloring for the painting came from natural plants.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜料来自天然植物。
words.en: The act or process of applying color.

words.ex: The ancient temple has a tall stone column.
words.ex_cn: 这座古庙有一根高大的石柱。
words.en: A column is a tall solid upright stone post used to support a building or as a monument.

words.ex: The lock uses a simple combination of three numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁使用三个数字的简单组合。
words.en: A combination is a mixture of things or people that are combined.

words.ex: He is a strong comer in the talent show.
words.ex_cn: 他在才艺比赛中是个有成功希望的人。
words.en: A comer is someone who arrives somewhere or someone who is likely to be successful in the future.

words.ex: He bought a commemorative coin for the event.
words.ex_cn: 他为这个活动买了一枚纪念币。
words.en: Something that is commemorative is intended to honor or remember someone or something.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: His commendable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞扬的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as commendable, you approve of it or are praising it.

words.ex: The teacher gave me a recommendation for the scholarship.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我写了一封奖学金推荐信。
words.en: A suggestion or proposal as to the best course of action, especially one put forward by an authoritative body.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.ex: The commentator explained the game clearly.
words.ex_cn: 评论员清晰地解释了比赛。
words.en: A commentator is someone who gives a commentary on something such as a sports event or a television program.

words.ex: They want to commercialize the new app.
words.ex_cn: 他们想将这个新应用商业化。
words.en: To commercialize something means to organize or develop it in such a way that it becomes intended to make a profit.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.tr: adj. 明白事理的，有基本常识的
words.ex: His commonsensical approach to problem-solving was highly appreciated.
words.ex_cn: 他解决问题的明白事理的方法很受赞赏。
words.en: Having or showing common sense; sensible.

words.tr: adj. 语言交际能力的（尤指用外语）；乐意沟通的；
words.ex: He is very communicative in English, even when he makes mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他用英语交流时很有能力，即使犯了错误。
words.en: Someone who is communicative talks to people, for example about their feelings, and tells people things.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.tr: adj. 伙伴的，同伴的；友爱的，友好的
words.ex: They shared a companionate relationship, built on mutual respect and understanding.
words.ex_cn: 他们分享了一种建立在相互尊重和理解基础上的伙伴关系。
words.en: Showing or characterized by affection and companionship.

words.ex: This is a comparative study of two languages.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个关于两种语言的比较研究。
words.en: You use comparative to show that you are judging something against a previous or different situation. For example, if you say that something is comparative luxury, you mean that it is luxurious compared to something else.

words.ex: The train has a sleeping compartment for passengers.
words.ex_cn: 火车上有一个供乘客休息的隔间。
words.en: A compartment is a separate section or part of something, especially a space in a vehicle that is separated from other spaces.

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: He met a compatriot at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场遇到了一位同胞。
words.en: A compatriot is a person from your own country.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: He received compensation for his injured leg.
words.ex_cn: 他因腿部受伤获得了赔偿。
words.en: Compensation is something, typically money, awarded to someone in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.ex: The book is a compilation of his best essays.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是他最佳文章的汇编物。
words.en: A compilation is a collection of different items, such as songs, pieces of writing, or data, that have been gathered together in one place or for one purpose.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: His complacency made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的自满让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: A feeling of smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.tr: n. 完整性; 完全; 完全性
words.ex: The completeness of the report impressed the board.
words.ex_cn: 报告的完整性给董事会留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: The state or condition of having all necessary or normal parts, components, or steps; the state of being whole and having no parts missing.

words.tr: n. 肤色；面色；情况；局面
words.ex: Her complexion is very fair.
words.ex_cn: 她的肤色非常白皙。
words.en: The natural color, texture, and appearance of a person's skin, especially of the face.

words.ex: The problem has too much complexity.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题太复杂了。
words.en: Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.

words.ex: The company showed compliance with safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 该公司遵守了安全规定。
words.en: The act of complying with a wish, request, or demand; obedience.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.tr: adj. 可压缩的；可压榨的
words.ex: The gas is compressible under high pressure.
words.ex_cn: 这种气体在高压下可以被压缩。
words.en: Capable of being compressed or made more compact.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.tr: adj. 无法控制行为的；禁不住的；
words.ex: He has a compulsive habit of checking the door lock.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种无法控制地检查门锁的习惯。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as compulsive, you mean that they cannot stop themselves doing or wanting something, even though it may be harmful or unreasonable.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: Computational methods are widely used in scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 计算方法在科学研究中被广泛使用。
words.en: Relating to the use of computers or involving computation.

words.ex: The company is undergoing computerization to improve efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在实施计算机化以提高效率。
words.en: The process of equipping a process, activity, or equipment with computers or of adapting something to the use of computers.

words.tr: v. 使计算机化；用计算机做
words.ex: The school will computerize its records next year.
words.ex_cn: 学校明年将把记录电脑化。
words.en: To computerize something means to use computers to control or operate it, or to change something so that it can be controlled or operated by computers.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 可想象得出的；可信的；可能的
words.ex: It is conceivable that he will arrive late.
words.ex_cn: 他可能会迟到，这是可以想象的。
words.en: Capable of being imagined or grasped mentally.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.ex: You must concentrate on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 你必须集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you concentrate on something, you give it your full attention and think about it carefully.

words.ex: His conception of the new app was simple but clever.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新应用的构想简单而巧妙。
words.en: A conception is an idea or a plan that someone has in their mind.

words.tr: v. 构思；使形成观念；使概念化
words.ex: He tries to conceptualize the problem before solving it.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决问题之前试图理解这个概念。
words.en: To conceptualize something means to form an idea or concept of it in your mind.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. “concern”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book is concerning climate change.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于气候变化的。
words.en: If something is concerning, it causes you to feel concerned about it.

words.ex: He plays a violin concerto at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐会上演奏一首小提琴协奏曲。
words.en: A concerto is a musical composition usually composed in three parts or movements, in which one solo instrument is accompanied by an orchestra.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: He wrote with concision to save time.
words.ex_cn: 他简洁地写作以节省时间。
words.en: Concision refers to the quality of being concise, that is, expressing much in few words.

words.ex: After the experiment, we reached a conclusion.
words.ex_cn: 实验结束后，我们得出了一个结论。
words.en: A conclusion is the last part of something, its end or result.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 该罚的，该受责备的
words.ex: His actions were condemnable, deserving severe punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是该受责备的，应受到严厉的惩罚。
words.en: Deserving condemnation; reprehensible.

words.ex: The public expressed condemnation for the violent act.
words.ex_cn: 公众对这一暴力行为表示谴责。
words.en: Condemnation is the act of saying that something or someone is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The condensation of the report made it easier to read.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告的浓缩版更容易阅读。
words.en: Condensation is the process by which a gas changes into a liquid, or the liquid that results from this process.

words.ex: She wrote a letter to condole with him on his loss.
words.ex_cn: 她写了一封信，对他的损失表示慰问。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a misfortune or loss.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.tr: n. （热或电等能量的）传导；导热；导电
words.ex: Metal is good for conduction of heat.
words.ex_cn: 金属善于导热。
words.en: The process by which heat or electricity is directly transmitted through a substance when there is a difference of temperature or of electrical potential between adjoining regions, without movement of the material.

words.tr: adj. 传导的；能传导（热、电）的
words.ex: Copper is conductive and used in wires.
words.ex_cn: 铜具有导电性，用于电线。
words.en: Having the property of conducting something (especially heat or electricity).

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: He made a confession about his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认了自己的错误。
words.en: A confession is a statement made by someone in which they admit that they have committed a particular crime or done something wrong.

words.ex: He is confident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很自信。
words.en: If you are confident, you are certain of your abilities or of your beliefs.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.tr: n. 结构；布局；配置；外形
words.ex: The configuration of the computer is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑的配置非常简单。
words.en: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form, figure, or combination.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.ex: The results of the test are confirmable and reliable.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果是可以确定的，且可靠。
words.en: Capable of being confirmed or verified.

words.ex: He received a confirmation email for his flight.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了航班的确认邮件。
words.en: Confirmation is the act of confirming something or making it more definite.

words.ex: The results of the experiment provided confirmative evidence.
words.ex_cn: 实验结果提供了确定的证据。
words.en: Serving to confirm or corroborate.

words.ex: The conflict between the two countries lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家之间的冲突持续了多年。
words.en: A conflict is a serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

words.ex: The meeting was highly conflictive, with both sides refusing to compromise.
words.ex_cn: 会议非常冲突，双方都拒绝妥协。
words.en: Involving or causing conflict; contradictory.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.ex: His actions were conformable to the company's policies.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为与公司的政策是一致的。
words.en: If something is conformable to something such as a law or someone's wishes, it is in accordance with that law or those wishes.

words.ex: The software is designed to ensure conformance with industry standards.
words.ex_cn: 该软件设计用于确保符合行业标准。
words.en: Conformance refers to the act of conforming or the state of being conformed, especially to a standard, specification, or regulation.

words.ex: He showed conformity with the group's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了小组的规定。
words.en: Conformity is the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or standards.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: The confrontation between the two teams was intense.
words.ex_cn: 两队之间的对抗非常激烈。
words.en: A confrontation is a situation in which there is a lot of disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: He looked at me with confusion.
words.ex_cn: 他困惑地看着我。
words.en: A state of uncertainty about what is happening, intended, or required.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.tr: n. 魔术师，变戏法的人
words.ex: The conjuror amazed the audience with his sleight of hand.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师用他的手法技巧让观众惊叹不已。
words.en: A conjuror is a person who performs magic tricks or who is believed to have magical powers.

words.ex: The teacher connived at the students' cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师纵容了学生的作弊行为。
words.en: If one person connives with another to do something wrong, they secretly allow or help them to do it.

words.ex: The word 'home' has a warm connotation.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词有温暖的含义。
words.en: An idea or feeling that a word invokes in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: The conquest of the mountain took three days.
words.ex_cn: 攻克这座山花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of conquering a place or people.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.tr: adj. 随之发生的；作为结果的；
words.ex: The rain was heavy, and the flood was consequent.
words.ex_cn: 雨下得很大，洪水随之发生。
words.en: Following as a result or effect.

words.tr: n. 保护；节约（自然资源）；
words.ex: The park is for the conservation of wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是为了保护野生动物。
words.en: The protection and preservation of the natural environment and wildlife.

words.tr: n. 自然环境保护主义者
words.ex: The conservationist protects wild animals.
words.ex_cn: 这位环保主义者保护野生动物。
words.en: A conservationist is someone who works to protect the environment, especially natural resources and wildlife.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He dressed conservatively for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他为面试穿着得体。
words.en: In a way that is traditional and does not like to change things quickly or take risks.

words.ex: The plants grow in the conservatory.
words.ex_cn: 植物在温室里生长。
words.en: A conservatory is a room with glass walls and a glass roof, which is built on the side of a house. It is used as a sun lounge or for growing plants. It can also refer to a school where people are trained in music or acting.

words.ex: We should conserve water in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们应在日常生活中节约用水。
words.en: To conserve something means to protect it from harm, loss, or change, especially in order to preserve it for the future.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.tr: v. 考虑；“consider”的现在分词； prep. 考虑到；就…而言；鉴于；
words.ex: I am considering going to the park.
words.ex_cn: 我正在考虑去公园。
words.en: Taking into account; in view of.

words.ex: The team consists of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名球员组成。
words.en: If something consists of particular things or people, it is made up of them.

words.tr: n. 始终一贯；前后一致；
words.ex: His consistency in studying every day helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他每天学习的一贯坚持帮助他通过了考试。
words.en: Consistency is the quality or condition of being consistent, especially in achieving a level of performance or behavior that does not vary greatly in quality over time.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The company's consolidation improved its market position.
words.ex_cn: 公司的巩固增强了其市场地位。
words.en: The act of combining two or more things into a single more effective or coherent whole.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.tr:
n. （统治者的）配偶；一组
v. 厮混；结交
words.ex: The king walked with his consort at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中与他的配偶一起行走。
words.en: A consort is a husband or wife, especially of a reigning monarch. As a verb, it means to habitually associate with someone, typically with the implication of a close or intimate relationship.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.ex: He is constantly checking his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他不断地查看他的手机。
words.en: If something happens constantly, it happens all the time or very often.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
