words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.tr:
n. 哑炮；无用的东西；废物
adj. 无用的；失灵的；出故障的
words.ex: The battery is a dud and won't turn on the phone.
words.ex_cn: 这节电池是坏的，无法让手机开机。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as a dud, you mean that they are completely useless, ineffective, or unsuccessful.

words.tr: adj. 应给的；预期的；到期的；
words.ex: The payment is due tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这笔款项明天应给。
words.en: If something is due at a particular time, it is expected to happen or be done at that time.

words.ex: The tailor used a dummy to fit the new coat.
words.ex_cn: 裁缝用人体模型来试穿新外套。
words.en: A dummy is a model of a person, often used for displaying clothes or for use in tests to see how something will work or fit.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: The duplication of the document cost five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件的复制花了五美元。
words.en: the act or process of making an exact copy of something

words.ex: The office uses a high-speed duplicator to produce large quantities of documents.
words.ex_cn: 办公室使用高速复印机大量复印文件。
words.en: A duplicator is a machine or person that copies something.

words.ex: The durability of this plastic makes it good for outdoor use.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料的持久性使它适合户外使用。
words.en: The ability of something to last a long time without significant deterioration.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The book was dusty on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书在架子上积满了灰尘。
words.en: Covered with or resembling dust; dry and powdery.

words.ex: He is an earnest student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真的学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you are earnest about something, you are serious about it and your intentions are honest and sincere.

words.tr: n. （科幻小说中外星球人谈话时使用的）地球人
words.ex: The alien communicated with the earthling in a strange language.
words.ex_cn: 外星人用一种奇怪的语言与地球人交流。
words.en: An earthling is a human being, especially when considered in relation to beings from other planets.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.ex: The edge of the table is sharp.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的边缘很锋利。
words.en: The edge of something is the place or line where it stops, or the part of it that is furthest from the middle.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.tr:
n. 社论；
adj. 编辑的；
words.ex: The newspaper published an editorial about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的社论。
words.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper which gives the opinion of the editor or publisher on a topic or item of news.

words.tr: adv. 怪异地；神秘地；引起害怕地
words.ex: The house was eerily quiet.
words.ex_cn: 这房子出奇地安静，令人感到神秘。
words.en: In a strange and frightening manner.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.ex: This medicine is effective against colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: Something that is effective works well and produces the results that were intended.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；利己的；
words.ex: He is egocentric and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他以自我为中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egocentric, you mean that they are only concerned with their own needs and desires, and not with those of other people.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: He felt sad after the rejection.
words.ex_cn: 在遭到拒绝后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The act of refusing to accept, believe in, or agree with something.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: adv. 精心地；苦心经营地
words.ex: The cake was decorated elaborately with flowers and ribbons.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕用花朵和丝带精心装饰。
words.en: In a detailed and complicated way, often involving a lot of effort or careful planning.

words.tr: n. 精心制作；详尽的细节；
words.ex: The chef gave an elaboration to the dish with fresh herbs.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用新鲜香草对这道菜进行了精心制作。
words.en: The process of developing or presenting a theory, policy, or system in detail.

words.tr: adj. 详尽的，精心制作的，煞费苦心的
words.ex: The report was elaborative, covering every detail of the project.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告非常详尽，涵盖了项目的每一个细节。
words.en: Involving many carefully arranged parts or details; detailed and complicated in design and planning.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.tr:
n. 肘部
v. 用肘推挤
words.ex: He hurt his elbow while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他在打篮球时伤了肘部。
words.en: The joint between the forearm and the upper arm; to push someone with your elbow.

words.ex: The wire is electrically connected to the battery.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线通过电与电池相连。
words.en: In a way that relates to electricity or is powered by electricity.

words.ex: Her dress showed great elegance.
words.ex_cn: 她的裙子展现了极大的优雅。
words.en: Elegance is the quality of being graceful and stylish in appearance or manner.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.ex: Water is made of two elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水由两种要素组成：氢和氧。
words.en: An element is a substance that cannot be separated into simpler substances by chemical means and is composed of atoms having the same number of protons.

words.ex: Water is an elemental part of life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本组成部分。
words.en: Something that is elemental is of a simple, basic kind.

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

chapters.name: 第2周 高频词汇2500（上）星期六

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The elevation of his skills helped him get a better job.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的提升帮助他找到了一份更好的工作。
words.en: The height to which something is elevated or to which it rises.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: The teacher used questions for elicitation of student ideas.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来引出学生的观点。
words.en: The act of drawing out or bringing forth something latent or potential.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: He spoke eloquently about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他雄辩地谈论了正义。
words.en: In a manner that is fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.ex: He felt embarrassment when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前绊倒时感到窘迫。
words.en: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.

words.ex: He is the embodiment of patience.
words.ex_cn: 他是耐心的化身。
words.en: The embodiment of a quality or idea is the concrete or physical form that it takes.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: The emergent technology is changing how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 这项新兴技术正在改变我们的交流方式。
words.en: An emergent situation or problem is one that has just started and often requires immediate action.

words.tr: adj. 新兴的； v. 浮现；显露；“emerge”的现在分词；
words.ex: China has many emerging tech companies.
words.ex_cn: 中国有许多新兴的科技公司。
words.en: An emerging market, country, or economy is one that is beginning to grow and develop its industries and infrastructure.

words.ex: The king sent an emissary to talk to the neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 国王派了一名使者去与邻国交谈。
words.en: An emissary is a person who is sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.

words.ex: He showed strong emotion when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，表现出了强烈的情绪。
words.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

words.ex: He gave an emotional speech about his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于他母亲的感人演讲。
words.en: Something that is emotional is connected with people's feelings. If someone is emotional, they show their feelings very openly, especially because they are upset.

words.tr: adj. 使感动的；感情的；动感情的
words.ex: The movie used emotive music to make people cry.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用了富有情感的音乐来让人流泪。
words.en: If you describe something as emotive, you mean that it is concerned with emotions and feelings, and often causes them.

words.tr: v. 移情；神会；有同感；产生共鸣
words.ex: She tries to empathize with her friend's feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她努力理解朋友的感受。
words.en: If you empathize with someone, you understand their situation, problems, and feelings, because you have been in a similar situation.

words.tr: adv. 强调地；断然地；显然地
words.ex: She emphatically denied the accusation.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决否认了这项指控。
words.en: In a forceful way that shows emphasis.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.ex: The fence encircles the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏围绕着花园。
words.en: To encircle something or someone means to surround them completely.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.ex: He will encode the message with a secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他将用密钥对这条信息进行编码。
words.en: To convert information into a particular form, especially for the purposes of secrecy or transmission.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: He looked up the word in an encyclopedia.
words.ex_cn: 他从百科全书中查找这个词。
words.en: An encyclopedia is a book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically.

words.tr:
adj. 惹人喜爱的
v. 使受喜爱；“endear”的现在分词
words.ex: Her smile is endearing.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as endearing, you mean that it causes you to feel very fond of them.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.ex: Endometrial cancer is a common type of gynecological cancer.
words.ex_cn: 子宫内膜癌是一种常见的妇科癌症。
words.en: Relating to the endometrium, which is the mucous membrane lining the uterus.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.ex: The pain was endurable, so she kept going.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛是可以忍受的，所以她继续前行。
words.en: If something is endurable, it is possible to be tolerated or endured.

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.tr: adj. 能耐劳的，能忍耐的
words.ex: He is known for his endurant nature, always persevering through tough times.
words.ex_cn: 他以能忍耐的性情著称，总是能挺过艰难时刻。
words.en: Having the ability to withstand hardship or stress; capable of enduring.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.tr: adj. 可执行的；可强制执行的
words.ex: The contract is enforceable by law.
words.ex_cn: 该合同在法律上是可实施的。
words.en: If something such as a law or agreement is enforceable, it can be enforced.

words.ex: The enforcement of traffic laws keeps roads safe.
words.ex_cn: 交通法规的执行使道路更安全。
words.en: The act of compelling observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation.

words.tr: n. 版画； v. 在（硬物）上雕刻；“engrave”的现在分词；
words.ex: He bought an old engraving at the art market.
words.ex_cn: 他在艺术市场买了一幅古老的版画。
words.en: An engraving is a picture or design that has been cut into a surface.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.tr: v. 增强；提高；“enhance”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 增强的；提高的；
words.ex: The new software enhanced the camera's quality.
words.ex_cn: 新软件增强了相机的画质。
words.en: If something is enhanced, it is made better or more effective.

words.tr: n. 增强；改善；增加；增进；
words.ex: The new software brings an enhancement to the system.
words.ex_cn: 新软件带来了系统的增强。
words.en: An enhancement is an improvement or addition that makes something better or more effective.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: The book brought him great enlightenment.
words.ex_cn: 这本书给了他极大的启迪。
words.en: Enlightenment is the act of enlightening or the state of being enlightened. It can refer to the acquisition of spiritual knowledge or understanding, especially in Buddhism.

words.tr: v. 使有生气；使活跃；使快活
words.ex: The music enlivened the party.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让派对更热闹了。
words.en: To make something more interesting, exciting, or cheerful.

words.ex: He enquired about the train schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了火车时刻表。
words.en: If you enquire about something, you ask for information about it.

words.ex: The unfair rule enrage him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的规则激怒了他。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.tr: n. 丰富；充实；浓缩；富集
words.ex: The school offers enrichment activities for gifted students.
words.ex_cn: 学校为天才学生提供拓展活动。
words.en: The act of improving or enhancing the quality or value of something.

words.ex: His enrolment at the university starts next month.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学的入学时间是下个月。
words.en: Enrolment refers to the process of signing up or registering for something, such as a school, course, or program.

words.ex: He ensconced himself in the armchair with a book.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己安顿在扶手椅里看书。
words.en: If you ensconce yourself somewhere, you settle yourself there in a safe, comfortable, or secret place.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: Please ensure the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 请确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make certain that something will occur or be the case.

words.tr: n. 表演者；艺人；款待的人
words.ex: The entertainer sang and danced for the children.
words.ex_cn: 这位表演者为孩子们唱歌跳舞。
words.en: An entertainer is a person whose job is to amuse or interest people, for example by telling jokes, singing, or dancing.

words.ex: She enthused about the new project for hours.
words.ex_cn: 她对新项目兴奋地讨论了几个小时。
words.en: If you enthuse about something, you talk about it in a way that shows how much you admire or like it.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: Every worker has an entitlement to fair pay.
words.ex_cn: 每位工人都有获得公平报酬的权利。
words.en: An entitlement is a right to have or do something, often granted by law or policy.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: The defense argued that the evidence was obtained through entrapment.
words.ex_cn: 辩护方认为证据是通过诱捕手段获得的。
words.en: Entrapment is the act of tricking someone into committing a crime so that they can be arrested for it.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.ex: She entrusted her keys to her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙托付给了朋友。
words.en: If you entrust something important to someone or entrust them with it, you give them the responsibility of looking after it or dealing with it.

words.tr: adv. 与环境有关地；在环境方面地；
words.ex: We should environmentally friendly products.
words.ex_cn: 我们应该购买与环境有关的产品。
words.en: In a way that relates to the natural world and the impact of human activity on its condition.

words.ex: The enzyme helps break down food in the stomach.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶帮助分解胃里的食物。
words.en: An enzyme is a protein that acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.ex: She is an epidemiologist who studies the spread of infectious diseases.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位研究传染病传播的流行病学家。
words.en: An epidemiologist is a medical scientist who studies the incidence, distribution, and control of diseases in populations.

words.ex: He studies epidemiology to understand how diseases spread.
words.ex_cn: 他研究流行病学以了解疾病如何传播。
words.en: Epidemiology is the study of how often diseases occur in different groups of people and why. It is a key component of public health, and shapes policy decisions and evidence-based practice by identifying risk factors for disease and targets for preventive healthcare.

words.ex: The saint had an epiphany while praying in the church.
words.ex_cn: 圣人在教堂祈祷时经历了显灵。
words.en: An epiphany is a moment of sudden and great revelation or realization.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.tr: v. 使平等；使均等；使相等
words.ex: The law aims to equalize opportunities for all people.
words.ex_cn: 法律旨在使所有人机会平等。
words.en: To make things equal in amount, size, or value.

words.tr: n. 均等；相等；相当；等价
words.ex: The equivalence of the two weights was proven by the scale.
words.ex_cn: 天平证明了这两个重量的均等。
words.en: Equivalence is the condition of being equal or equivalent in value, worth, function, etc.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr: n. 根除；连根拔除；消灭；
words.ex: The government aims at the eradication of poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府的目标是根除贫困。
words.en: The complete destruction of something so that it no longer exists.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: He erroneously thought the answer was 5.
words.ex_cn: 他错误地认为答案是5。
words.en: In a way that is incorrect or based on false information.

words.ex: She visited her erstwhile home town.
words.ex_cn: 她参观了她从前居住的小镇。
words.en: Former; in the past.

words.tr: adj. 暴发的，喷火的，疹的
words.ex: The eruptive volcano spewed lava and ash into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 喷发的火山向空中喷射出熔岩和灰烬。
words.en: Something that is eruptive is characterized by or relating to a sudden outbreak or discharge, especially of a volcano or a disease.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: The spy practiced espionage to get secret information.
words.ex_cn: 间谍从事间谍活动以获取秘密信息。
words.en: The practice of spying or of using spies, typically by governments to obtain political and military information.

words.tr: n. 精神；才智；机敏；朝气; n. （Esprit）（美、法、英、比、加、荷）埃斯普里（人名）
words.ex: The esprit de corps of the team was evident in their synchronized movements.
words.ex_cn: 团队的集体精神在他们整齐划一的动作中显而易见。
words.en: Liveliness of mind or spirit; a sense of belonging and loyalty to a group.

words.tr: n. 论说文（或小品文、散文）作家
words.ex: The essayist writes clearly and wisely.
words.ex_cn: 散文家写得清晰而睿智。
words.en: An essayist is a writer of essays, especially ones that are published and deal with serious subjects.

words.ex: The essence of love is caring for others.
words.ex_cn: 爱的本质是关心他人。
words.en: The essence of something is its basic and most important characteristic which gives it its individual identity.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.tr: n. 本质主义，本质先于存在论；要素主义教育
words.ex: Essentialism in education focuses on the core subjects.
words.ex_cn: 要素主义教育注重核心学科。
words.en: Essentialism is the belief that things have a set of characteristics that make them what they are, and that these characteristics are necessary to their identity.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr:
adj. 审美的；美学的
n. 美学
words.ex: She loves the esthetic of old paintings.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢旧画的美感。
words.en: Relating to the appreciation of beauty or good taste, especially in the arts.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.ex: He sought to eternalize his name by writing a great novel.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过写一部伟大的小说来使自己的名字永恒。
words.en: To make something last forever; to immortalize.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.tr: adj. 基督教福音派的；狂热的
words.ex: He is an evangelical Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名福音派基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: Relating to the Christian gospel or the Christian religion as presented in the Gospels.

words.tr: n. 逃避，推诿；模棱两可
words.ex: His evasiveness during the interview raised suspicions.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中的逃避态度引起了怀疑。
words.en: The quality of being evasive; avoidance of directness or clarity.

words.ex: The eventual winner was a young student.
words.ex_cn: 最后的赢家是一位年轻学生。
words.en: An eventual event or situation happens at the end of a process or period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 常绿的；常青的；
n. 常绿树；常绿植物；
words.ex: The evergreen trees stay green all year.
words.ex_cn: 常绿树一年四季都是绿色的。
words.en: An evergreen is a plant, tree, or bush that has green leaves all the year round.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: The evolution of birds from dinosaurs took millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类从恐龙进化而来花了数百万年。
words.en: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.

words.ex: This trait is evolutionarily advantageous.
words.ex_cn: 这种特性在进化上是有利的。
words.en: In a manner relating to the development and diversification of species over time.

words.ex: The bird evolved from a small dinosaur.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟由一种小型恐龙演变而来。
words.en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: His story was an exaggeration of the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事是对事实的夸张。
words.en: An exaggeration is a statement that represents something as better or worse than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 虚夸; 唐; 夸张的，夸大的
words.ex: Her exaggerative descriptions made the story seem more dramatic than it really was.
words.ex_cn: 她夸张的描述使得故事比实际情况更加戏剧化。
words.en: If you describe something as exaggerative, you mean that it is exaggerated or overemphasized.

words.tr:
adj. 高位的；高尚的；欣喜的
v. 赞扬；提升；加强；“exalt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The exalted king sat on a golden throne.
words.ex_cn: 这位高位的国王坐在一张金宝座上。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exalted, you mean they are at a high level of honor, rank, or quality.

words.ex: He slammed the door in exasperation.
words.ex_cn: 他因恼怒而砰地关上了门。
words.en: Exasperation is a feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.

words.ex: The excavation revealed ancient pottery.
words.ex_cn: 挖掘发现了古代陶器。
words.en: The process of digging up and removing earth, especially at an archaeological site.

words.tr: v. 超过；超出；“exceed”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is exceeding the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 他正在超过限速。
words.en: Going beyond the usual, necessary, or proper limit or degree; excessive.

words.ex: The weather is exceedingly cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气极其寒冷。
words.en: To a very great degree; extremely.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.tr:
n. 交换；兑换；交易所；
v. 交换；
words.ex: They made an exchange of books.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了书籍的交换。
words.en: If you exchange something, you give it to someone and receive something else in return.

words.tr: adj. 可兑换; 可交的，可兑交的，可替交的
words.ex: These coins are exchangeable for bills.
words.ex_cn: 这些硬币可以兑换成纸币。
words.en: If something is exchangeable, it can be exchanged for something else, especially of the same type or value.

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr: n. 排他性；独占性；独家经营权
words.ex: The club offers exclusivity to its members.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部只为会员提供专属权。
words.en: The state of being exclusive, especially the condition of being limited to a single person, group, or area.

words.tr: adv. 极痛苦地，难忍受的
words.ex: She found it excruciatingly painful to move after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，她发现一动就极其痛苦。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely painful or intense.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: The execution of the criminal was carried out last night.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯的处决昨晚执行了。
words.en: The carrying out or performance of a task, plan, or order.

words.tr: n. 死刑执行人；刽子手
words.ex: The executioner carried out the sentence quietly.
words.ex_cn: 刽子手安静地执行了判决。
words.en: An executioner is a person who carries out a death sentence on a legally condemned person.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.tr:
v. 豁免；
adj. 被免除的；
words.ex: The school exempted him from the test.
words.ex_cn: 学校免除了他的考试。
words.en: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

words.ex: The king was sent into exile after the revolution.
words.ex_cn: 革命后，国王被流放了。
words.en: Exile is the state of being sent away from one's home country or place of residence, often for political or punitive reasons.

words.ex: Her expansiveness made it difficult to have a serious conversation.
words.ex_cn: 她的夸张性使得进行严肃的对话变得困难。
words.en: The quality of being expansive; the capacity to extend or spread out widely.

words.ex: He has high expectancy for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来有很高的预期。
words.en: The feeling of excitement about something that is going to happen.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: He learned through experiential training.
words.ex_cn: 他通过基于经验的培训学习。
words.en: Relating to or derived from experience.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.ex: The milk's expiration date is tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶的保质期是明天。
words.en: The end of the period for which something is valid or the act of breathing out.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: The expiry of the contract will be next month.
words.ex_cn: 合同的满期将在下个月。
words.en: The end of the period for which something is valid.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.tr: adj. 开发资源的；剥削的；
words.ex: The company used exploitative labor practices to cut costs.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司使用剥削性的劳动做法来降低成本。
words.en: Exploitative refers to taking unfair advantage of someone or something, often for personal gain.

words.ex: He did an exploratory trip to find new places.
words.ex_cn: 他进行了一次探索性的旅行来寻找新地方。
words.en: relating to or involving exploration or investigation

words.ex: The population grows exponentially each year.
words.ex_cn: 人口每年呈指数增长。
words.en: Exponential means increasing very rapidly, often used to describe growth rates in mathematics, biology, and economics.

words.tr: n. 说明者，解释者，评注者
words.ex: He was known as an excellent expositor of complex theories.
words.ex_cn: 他以解释复杂理论的能力而闻名。
words.en: An expositor is someone who explains or interprets complex ideas or texts.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: He faced expulsion for breaking the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反校规而被开除。
words.en: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone to leave a place, especially a school or a country, as a punishment or because they are not wanted there.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr: v. 赋与形体；使…具体化；表露
words.ex: The architect externalized his vision into a concrete design.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师将他的愿景具体化为一个具体的设计。
words.en: To externalize something means to make it external or to give it an external form, especially to express it in a concrete or tangible way.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: The extinguishment of the fire was a relief to the residents.
words.ex_cn: 火灾的扑灭让居民们松了一口气。
words.en: The act of extinguishing or the state of being extinguished; the termination or cancellation of a right or obligation.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

words.ex: He extrapolates the trend from last year's data.
words.ex_cn: 他从去年的数据中推断出趋势。
words.en: To extrapolate is to estimate or conclude something by extending or projecting known information.

words.tr: adj. 地球外的；地外的；外星球的；
words.ex: The movie shows an extraterrestrial life form.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一种地球外的生命形式。
words.en: An extraterrestrial is a creature that comes from or exists outside the planet Earth.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: He shows extroversion at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上表现出外向。
words.en: Extroversion is the quality of being outgoing and socially confident.

words.ex: The flowers exude a sweet smell.
words.ex_cn: 花朵散发出甜美的香味。
words.en: If someone exudes a quality or feeling, or if it exudes, they show that they have it to a great extent.

words.ex: The eyewitness saw the accident happen.
words.ex_cn: 目击者看到了事故的发生。
words.en: An eyewitness is a person who has seen something happen and can give a first-hand description of it.

words.tr:
n. 寓言；神话传说；无稽之谈
v. 虚构
words.ex: The old man told a fable about a fox and a crow.
words.ex_cn: 老人讲了一个关于狐狸和乌鸦的寓言。
words.en: A fable is a short story that typically features animals as characters and conveys a moral lesson.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: The concert was fabulous!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

words.tr: adj. 姓名不祥的；无表情的；千篇一律的；无个性的
words.ex: The faceless bureaucrats made the decision without consulting the public.
words.ex_cn: 这些不露面的官僚未经公众咨询就做出了决定。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as faceless, you dislike them because they are uninteresting and have no character.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: The new software is for the facilitation of daily tasks.
words.ex_cn: 这个新软件是为了简化日常任务。
words.en: The act of making something easier or helping it to happen.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr:
n. 因素；要素；倍数；
v. 把…因素包括进去；
words.ex: Weather is a factor in the game's outcome.
words.ex_cn: 天气是比赛结果的一个因素。
words.en: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

words.tr: n. （太阳光球上的）光斑( facula的名词复数 )
words.ex: The faculae on the sun's surface are brighter than the surrounding areas.
words.ex_cn: 太阳表面上的光斑比周围区域更亮。
words.en: Bright patches on the sun's surface, visible in white light, usually associated with sunspots.

words.tr: n. 不贞; 不可信赖; 无信仰; 无信用
words.ex: His faithlessness led to the downfall of the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的不可信赖导致了公司的垮台。
words.en: The quality of being unfaithful or disloyal.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.tr: n. 欺骗; 蒙骗; 伪造; 赝品
words.ex: His fakement fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的伪装骗了派对上的每个人。
words.en: An act or instance of faking; a deception or fraud.

words.ex: His fanaticism for the team made him miss work.
words.ex_cn: 他对球队的狂热让他错过了工作。
words.en: Fanaticism is the quality of being fanatical, which means having very extreme and often unreasonable beliefs, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: The child told a fanciful story about flying dragons.
words.ex_cn: 孩子讲了一个关于会飞的龙的富于幻想的故事。
words.en: If you describe an idea as fanciful, you mean that it is imaginative rather than reasonable or practical.

words.ex: The trial was a farce.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是一场闹剧。
words.en: A farce is a comedy that aims at entertaining the audience through situations that are highly exaggerated, extravagant, and thus improbable.

words.ex: The old farmhouse stands near the field.
words.ex_cn: 那座古老的农舍坐落在田地附近。
words.en: A farmhouse is a house attached to a farm, especially the main house in which the farmer lives.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The movie is fascinating because it shows strange aliens.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极有吸引力，因为它展示了奇怪的外星人。
words.en: If you describe something as fascinating, you find it very interesting and attractive, and your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The magic show had a strange fascination for children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演对孩子们有一种奇特的迷惑力。
words.en: A fascination is a very strong interest or attraction for someone or something.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: The car accident caused one fatality.
words.ex_cn: 这场车祸导致一人死亡。
words.en: A fatality is a death caused by an accident or by violence, or is the fact of causing death.

words.ex: The fatness of the meat made it too oily to eat.
words.ex_cn: 肉的油腻让它太腻了，吃不下。
words.en: The quality or state of being fat; obesity.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the pigs to fatten them.
words.ex_cn: 农夫喂猪使它们长胖。
words.en: To make or become fat or fatter.

words.tr: adj. 无可指责的；完美无缺的
words.ex: Her performance was faultless.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演完美无瑕。
words.en: If you describe something as faultless, you mean that it is perfect and has no mistakes or faults in it.

words.ex: She danced faultlessly across the stage.
words.ex_cn: 她在舞台上完美地跳舞。
words.en: In a manner that is free from fault or error; perfectly.

words.tr: adj. 有缺陷的；有故障的；有错误的；
words.ex: The faulty phone keeps turning off.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺陷的手机总是自动关机。
words.en: If you describe something as faulty, you mean that it is not perfect or it has some weaknesses.

words.ex: The feasibility of the project was checked by experts.
words.ex_cn: 专家们检查了这个项目的可行性。
words.en: Feasibility refers to the state or degree of being easily or conveniently done.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.ex: The ostrich is a large, featherless bird.
words.ex_cn: 鸵鸟是一种体型巨大、无羽毛的鸟。
words.en: Having no feathers; lacking feathers.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.tr: adv. 感动地，充满感情地
words.ex: She spoke so feelingly about her childhood.
words.ex_cn: 她满怀感情地谈起了她的童年。
words.en: In a way that shows strong emotions or sensitivity.

words.tr: adj. 贴切的；恰当的；妥帖的
words.ex: His felicitous remark made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 他得体的言论让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Well chosen or suited to the circumstances.

words.ex: He was arrested for a felony last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月因重罪被逮捕了。
words.en: A felony is a serious crime such as murder or robbery.

words.tr:
n. 发酵；酵素；动乱
v. （使）发酵；动乱
words.ex: The ferment of yeast makes bread rise.
words.ex_cn: 酵母的发酵使面包膨胀。
words.en: If a substance ferments or if it is fermented, it changes chemically because of the action of yeast or bacteria, often producing alcohol.

words.ex: The ferryman rows the boat across the river.
words.ex_cn: 船夫划船过河。
words.en: A ferryman is a person who operates a ferry, transporting people or goods across a body of water.

words.ex: Bees help to fertilize flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵受精。
words.en: To fertilize means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg, female animal, or plant to develop a new individual by introducing male reproductive material.

words.ex: The patient has lung fibrosis from long-term smoking.
words.ex_cn: 这位病人因长期吸烟患有肺纤维化。
words.en: Fibrosis is the thickening and scarring of connective tissue, usually as a result of injury.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.tr: v. 把（历史事件等）编成小说，使小说化
words.ex: He fictionalize the story to make it more exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他把故事虚构化，使其更令人兴奋。
words.en: To fictionalize something means to make it into a fictional story, especially by changing some of the details or adding imaginary elements.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.tr:
adj. 受托的；信托的
n. 受托人
words.ex: He is a fiduciary for his client's money.
words.ex_cn: 他是客户资金的受托人。
words.en: A fiduciary is a person or organization that acts on behalf of another person or persons, putting their clients' interests ahead of their own, with a duty to preserve good faith and trust.

words.ex: The lord ruled his fief with strict laws.
words.ex_cn: 领主用严格的法律统治他的封地。
words.en: A fief is a piece of land that was given to a vassal by a lord in return for military service.

words.tr: v. 拍成电影；“film”的现在分词； n. 拍摄；
words.ex: They started filming the movie last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周开始拍这部电影。
words.en: The process of making a film or movie.

words.ex: He loves filmmaking and makes short movies every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱电影制作，每个周末都拍短片。
words.en: The process or art of making films.

words.ex: She finely chopped the herbs for the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她把香草精细地切碎用于汤中。
words.en: In a fine manner; excellently.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: The firth is a long, narrow sea inlet near the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个峡湾是靠近小镇的一个狭长的海水入口。
words.en: A firth is a long, narrow indentation of the seacoast.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.ex: The flaw in the glass made it break easily.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃上的瑕疵让它很容易碎。
words.en: A flaw is a mistake or weakness in something that makes it less effective or valuable.

words.tr: adj. 无瑕疵的；无缺点的；
words.ex: Her performance was flawless.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演毫无瑕疵。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is flawless, you mean that they are extremely good and that there are no faults or problems with them.

words.ex: He will flee from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 他会从着火的房子里逃走。
words.en: If you flee from something or someone, you leave them quickly because you are afraid of them or because you do not want to be involved with them.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He works on flexitime so he can leave early on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他实行弹性工作时间，所以周五可以早点下班。
words.en: Flexitime is a system of working a set number of hours with the starting and finishing times chosen within agreed limits by the employee.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.ex: She wore a floral dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条有花卉图案的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Relating to flowers; decorated with flowers or a pattern of flowers.

words.tr:
v. 藐视；轻视；嘲笑
n. 嘲弄；轻视
words.ex: He flouts the rules every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都无视规则。
words.en: If you flout something such as a law, an order, or an accepted way of behaving, you deliberately do not obey it or follow it.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: The stock market shows daily fluctuation.
words.ex_cn: 股票市场每天都有波动。
words.en: A fluctuation is a change in something, especially in a continuous process such as temperature, prices, or levels of activity.

words.ex: He passed the test by a fluke.
words.ex_cn: 他靠运气通过了考试。
words.en: A fluke is an unexpected stroke of good luck or a surprising success that happens by chance.

words.ex: Toothpaste contains fluoride to protect teeth.
words.ex_cn: 牙膏含有氟化物以保护牙齿。
words.en: Fluoride is a chemical compound that contains fluorine. It is often added to water and toothpaste to help prevent tooth decay.

words.ex: He flushes the toilet after using it.
words.ex_cn: 他用完厕所后冲水。
words.en: If you flush, your face goes red because you are hot or ill, or because you are feeling a strong emotion such as embarrassment or anger. To flush a toilet means to cause water to pass through it in order to clean it.

words.ex: He saw his neighbor as a foe.
words.ex_cn: 他把邻居看作敌人。
words.en: A foe is someone who opposes or fights against another; an enemy.

words.tr: adj. 有民间风味的；朴素的；友好亲切的
words.ex: The town's main square had a folksy charm with its wooden benches and street musicians.
words.ex_cn: 小镇的主广场以其木制长椅和街头音乐家而具有民间风味的魅力。
words.en: Having the characteristics of traditional rural life, especially in being simple, friendly, and unpretentious.

words.ex: His folly led to the loss of his job.
words.ex_cn: 他的愚蠢导致他丢了工作。
words.en: If you say that a particular action or way of behaving is folly, you mean that it is foolish.

words.ex: This store sells many kinds of foodstuff.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售许多种类的食品。
words.en: Foodstuffs are substances that are used as food.

words.ex: The climbers found a foothold on the rocky wall.
words.ex_cn: 登山者在岩壁上找到了一个立足点。
words.en: A foothold is a secure position from which further progress or development may be made.

words.tr: adj. 无足的，笨拙的，无基础的
words.ex: The doll has footless legs.
words.ex_cn: 这个玩偶的腿没有脚。
words.en: Lacking feet; without a firm foundation; clumsy.

words.ex: The store sells all kinds of footwear.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种鞋类。
words.en: Footwear refers to garments worn on the feet, which typically serve the purpose of protection against adversities of the environment such as ground textures and temperature.

words.ex: This is his first foray into painting.
words.ex_cn: 这是他首次涉足绘画。
words.en: A foray is a sudden and brief incursion or attack into enemy territory, especially to obtain something; a raid. It can also refer to an initial attempt to become involved in a different activity or profession.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave a forceful speech to convince the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一番有力的演讲来说服人群。
words.en: A forceful person expresses their opinions and wishes strongly, and people are easily persuaded by them.

words.ex: The forecaster predicts rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 气象预报员预测明天会下雨。
words.en: A forecaster is someone whose job is to study the weather or other conditions and to say what they are likely to be in the future.

words.ex: Our forefather built this village long ago.
words.ex_cn: 我们的祖先很久以前建造了这个村庄。
words.en: Your forefathers are your ancestors, especially the male ones.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.ex: He can foretell the weather by looking at the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他可以通过观察天空来预知天气。
words.en: To tell or indicate beforehand; predict.

words.ex: I forget where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you forget something, you fail to remember it.

words.ex: He will forgo dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: If you forgo something, you decide to do without it, even though you would like it.

chapters.name: 第2周 高频词汇2500（上）星期日

words.tr: v. 使正式化；使形式化
words.ex: The company decided to formalize the agreement with a written contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定用书面合同使协议正式化。
words.en: To make something official or to give it a definite form.

words.ex: The company used a new formula to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用了一个新方案来解决问题。
words.en: A formula is a plan or method that is used to achieve a particular goal, especially in science or mathematics.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.tr: n. 公式化；阐述方式；规划；配方
words.ex: The formulation of the equation took hours.
words.ex_cn: 这个公式的推导花了好几个小时。
words.en: The act or process of formulating something, especially a systematic statement of principles or a particular method of preparing something.

words.tr: v. 发誓放弃；断然丢弃
words.ex: He forswears lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓不再对朋友撒谎。
words.en: If you forswear something, you promise to stop doing it or having it, especially because you think it is bad or harmful.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.ex: The soldiers defended the fortress from enemy attacks.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们保卫堡垒，抵御敌人的进攻。
words.en: A fortress is a large building or complex of buildings used as a military stronghold.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.ex: The child was placed in fosterage to ensure a stable environment.
words.ex_cn: 为了确保一个稳定的环境，这个孩子被寄养了。
words.en: The act of fostering or the state of being fostered; the care and upbringing of a child by someone other than its natural or adoptive parents.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: n. 脆弱性；脆性；易碎性
words.ex: The fragility of the glass made it easy to break.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃的易碎性让它很容易破碎。
words.en: The quality of being easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The flower has a sweet fragrance.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有一种甜美的香味。
words.en: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, especially that of a flower or perfume.

words.ex: Frankly, I don't like this idea.
words.ex_cn: 坦率地说，我不喜欢这个想法。
words.en: In a frank manner; honestly or directly.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.tr:
n. 怪诞行为；
adj. 不正常的；怪异的；
words.ex: His freak of wearing socks with sandals surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他穿袜子配凉鞋的怪诞行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A freak is a person who is considered to be unusual because of their behaviour or interests, or a sudden and unexpected event or situation.

words.ex: He is a freelance graphic designer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名自由职业的平面设计师。
words.en: A freelance person is someone who does particular pieces of work for different organizations, rather than working all the time for a single organization.

words.ex: He drives on the freeway every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都开上高速公路。
words.en: A freeway is a wide road built for fast travel between cities or towns, with a limited number of places where vehicles can enter and leave it.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.ex: The freight train carried boxes to the city.
words.ex_cn: 货运列车把箱子运到了城市。
words.en: Freight refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also mean the charge for such transportation.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: The fringe of the forest is full of wildflowers.
words.ex_cn: 森林的边缘长满了野花。
words.en: The outer, marginal, or extreme part of an area, group, or sphere of activity.

words.tr: n. <美>（靠近未开发地带的）边远的居民，边远者
words.ex: The frontiersman lived alone in the wild woods.
words.ex_cn: 这位边疆开拓者独自生活在荒野中。
words.en: A frontiersman is a man who lives on the frontier, especially in the early days of the American West, and is involved in settling and developing new areas.

words.tr: adj. 冰冻的；冻结的； v. “freeze”的过去分词；
words.ex: The frozen fish tastes fresh.
words.ex_cn: 冰冻的鱼尝起来很新鲜。
words.en: If something is frozen, it has been turned into ice or has become very hard because of cold temperature.

words.tr: n. 取得成果；实现；完成
words.ex: The project finally came to fruition after years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年的努力，这个项目终于完成了。
words.en: The realization or fulfillment of a plan or project.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.tr: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人泄气的；让人懊恼的； v. “frustrate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The slow internet is frustrating.
words.ex_cn: 网速慢让人沮丧。
words.en: If something is frustrating, it annoys you or makes you angry because you cannot do anything about the problems it causes.

words.ex: He couldn't hide his frustration after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后无法掩饰自己的沮丧。
words.en: The feeling of being upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something.

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: The picture is fuzzy and hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 这张图片很模糊，看不清楚。
words.en: Something that is fuzzy is unclear or indistinct, often because it is out of focus or because it is covered with a soft, fluffy material.

words.tr: adv. 有收入地；有利益地
words.ex: He is gainfully employed at a local store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家本地商店有正当工作。
words.en: In a way that provides gain or profit; profitably.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The gale knocked down several trees.
words.ex_cn: 大风刮倒了几棵树。
words.en: A gale is a very strong wind.

words.ex: The factory galvanize iron sheets to prevent rust.
words.ex_cn: 工厂对铁片进行镀锌以防止生锈。
words.en: To galvanize someone means to cause them to take action, for example by making them feel very excited, afraid, or angry.

words.ex: His opening gambit was a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他的开场白是一个简单的问题。
words.en: A gambit is a clever action in a game or other situation that is intended to achieve an advantage and usually involves taking a risk.

words.ex: The gangster stole money from the bank.
words.ex_cn: 这个黑帮分子偷了银行的钱。
words.en: A gangster is a member of a group of violent criminals.

words.ex: The gardener waters the plants every morning.
words.ex_cn: 园丁每天早上给植物浇水。
words.en: A gardener is someone who takes care of a garden as a job or hobby.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr:
n. 花环
v. 给…戴上花环
words.ex: She put a garland on the door for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对在门上挂了一个花环。
words.en: A garland is a circular decoration made from flowers and leaves, which is worn on the head or hung up as a decoration.

words.ex: He adds garlic to the soup for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 他往汤里加蒜来提味。
words.en: A strong-smelling pungent-tasting bulb, used as a flavoring in cooking and in herbal medicine.

words.ex: The garrison stayed in the fort during the war.
words.ex_cn: 驻军在战争期间留在堡垒里。
words.en: A garrison is a group of soldiers whose job is to guard the town or building where they live.

words.ex: The mechanic opened the gearbox to inspect the gears.
words.ex_cn: 机械师打开变速箱检查齿轮。
words.en: A gearbox is a device that is used to change the speed or the direction of movement of a vehicle by controlling the gears.

words.ex: The old geezer walks his dog every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位老家伙每天早上都遛狗。
words.en: An old man, especially one who is eccentric or amusing.

words.tr: adj. 可概括的，可归纳的
words.ex: This method is generalizable to other cases.
words.ex_cn: 这种方法可以推广到其他情况。
words.en: Capable of being generalized; applicable or adaptable to a wide range of situations or conditions.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He generalized the results from the small group to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他将小群体的结果概括为全体情况。
words.en: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.tr: adj. 生育的；世代的；一代的
words.ex: Each generational shift brings new values.
words.ex_cn: 每一代的生育更替都会带来新的价值观。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of all the people born and living at about the same time, regarded collectively.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The scientist studied genetic traits in plants.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了植物的基因特征。
words.en: relating to genes or heredity

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: Scientists mapped the human genome last year.
words.ex_cn: 科学家们去年绘制了人类基因组。
words.en: The complete set of genes or genetic material present in a cell or organism.

words.tr: n. 吸气剂; 获得者
words.ex: The getter returns the value of the variable.
words.ex_cn: 这个获取器返回变量的值。
words.en: A getter is a person or thing that gets something, or a material used to remove or absorb gases in a vacuum tube.

words.tr: n. 间歇泉；热水炉；热水器
words.ex: The geyser shoots hot water into the air.
words.ex_cn: 间歇泉将热水喷向空中。
words.en: A geyser is a spring characterized by intermittent discharge of water ejected turbulently and accompanied by steam.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The power plant produces one gigawatt of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这座发电厂产生一吉瓦的电力。
words.en: A unit of power equal to one billion watts.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.ex: The gimp walked slowly with a limp.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛脚的人慢慢地走着。
words.en: A gimp is someone who has a limp or walks with difficulty. It can also refer to a decorative trimming used in sewing.

words.tr: n. （鸟的）砂囊; （鸟的）胃; <俗>喉咙; （人的）胃
words.ex: The chicken's gizzard helps grind its food.
words.ex_cn: 鸡的砂囊帮助磨碎它的食物。
words.en: The gizzard is a part of the stomach of some animals, especially birds, that has thick muscular walls and is used for grinding food.

words.ex: The glacial landscape was covered in snow.
words.ex_cn: 冰河地貌被雪覆盖着。
words.en: relating to, resulting from, or denoting the presence or agency of ice, especially in the form of glaciers.

words.ex: The glaciologist studies ice in polar regions.
words.ex_cn: 这位冰川学家研究极地的冰。
words.en: A glaciologist is a scientist who studies glaciers, or more generally ice and natural phenomena that involve ice.

words.tr: v. 使有魅力；美化粉饰；渲染
words.ex: The movie glamorizes crime and violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影美化了犯罪和暴力。
words.en: To make something seem more attractive or exciting than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.tr: n. 吹玻璃的人或机器
words.ex: The glassblower made a beautiful vase.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃吹制工做了一个漂亮的花瓶。
words.en: A glassblower is a person who shapes molten glass into objects by blowing air into it through a tube.

words.ex: Early detection of glaucoma is crucial for preventing vision loss.
words.ex_cn: 青光眼的早期检测对于预防视力丧失至关重要。
words.en: A disease of the eye in which the pressure of fluid inside the eyeball is abnormally high, damaging the optic disc and impairing vision, sometimes progressing to blindness.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.tr:
adj. 辉煌的；成功的；盛大的；华丽的
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）；“glitter”的现在分词
words.ex: The sky was filled with glittering stars.
words.ex_cn: 天空中满是闪闪发光的星星。
words.en: Something that is glittering shines brightly with little flashes of light.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: Globalization helps countries trade more easily.
words.ex_cn: 全球化帮助各国更容易地进行贸易。
words.en: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.

words.tr: vi. 环球旅行；周游世界
words.ex: He globetrots every summer to visit new countries.
words.ex_cn: 他每年夏天都去世界各地旅行。
words.en: To travel widely around the world.

words.tr:
n. 黑暗；忧郁；幽暗
v. 变阴暗；变忧郁
words.ex: The room was filled with gloom after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后，房间里一片黑暗。
words.en: Gloom is a feeling of sadness and lack of hope.

words.tr: adv. 沮丧地；黑暗地；阴沉地
words.ex: She stared gloomily out of the window.
words.ex_cn: 她沮丧地盯着窗外。
words.en: In a manner that shows sadness or depression.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.ex: The movie glorifies violence as heroism.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影美化了暴力，将其视为英雄主义。
words.en: To glorify someone or something means to praise them or make them seem more important or better than they really are.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.ex: The glow of the fire warmed the room.
words.ex_cn: 火的炽热温暖了房间。
words.en: If something glows, it produces a dull, steady light.

words.ex: The doctor checked his glucose level.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的血糖水平。
words.en: A simple sugar which is an important energy source in living organisms and is a component of many carbohydrates.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；傻瓜；蠢人
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；混；打发时间
words.ex: He made a goof when he forgot his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记带作业，犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
words.en: If you call someone a goof, you mean they are silly or stupid. As a verb, to goof means to make a mistake or do something badly.

words.ex: She wore a gorgeous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件华丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you say that something is gorgeous, you mean that it gives you a lot of pleasure or is very attractive.

words.ex: The gossip about the CEO made everyone shocked.
words.ex_cn: 关于CEO的流言蜚语让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: Gossip is informal conversation or reports about other people's private lives, which might be unkind or not true.

words.ex: He suffered from gout and had to limit his diet.
words.ex_cn: 他患有痛风，不得不限制饮食。
words.en: Gout is a medical condition usually characterized by recurrent attacks of acute inflammatory arthritis—a red, tender, hot, swollen joint. The metatarsal-phalangeal joint at the base of the big toe is the most commonly affected (approximately 50% of cases). However, it may also present as tophi, kidney stones, or urate nephropathy. It is caused by elevated levels of uric acid in the blood.

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.tr: adj. 优雅的；优美的；得体的；
words.ex: The dancer moved in a graceful way.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者动作优雅。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as graceful, you mean that they move in a smooth, controlled, and attractive way.

words.tr: n. 倾斜度；坡度；梯度；斜坡
words.ex: The hill has a steep gradient.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个陡峭的坡度。
words.en: A gradient is a slope or a degree of inclination, especially in a road or railway.

words.ex: My family came to my graduation.
words.ex_cn: 我的家人来参加我的毕业典礼。
words.en: Graduation is the successful completion of a course of study at a university, college, or school, often marked by a ceremony.

words.tr: n. 语法专家；文法家；语言学专家；
words.ex: The grammarian corrected the student's sentence.
words.ex_cn: 语法专家纠正了学生的句子。
words.en: A grammarian is a person who studies and writes about grammar.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr: v. 授予；承认；“grant”的过去式和过去分词； conj. 假定；
words.ex: The king granted him land.
words.ex_cn: 国王授予了他一块土地。
words.en: Used to admit that something is true before making another, sometimes contrasting, statement.

words.ex: The medicine comes in small granules.
words.ex_cn: 这种药是小颗粒状的。
words.en: A granule is a small compact particle of a substance.

words.ex: The report shows graphical data to explain trends.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告用图表数据来解释趋势。
words.en: Relating to or involving visual art or computer graphics.

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.ex: She used a grater to chop cheese.
words.ex_cn: 她用擦丝器把奶酪擦碎。
words.en: A grater is a kitchen utensil with sharp edges used for shredding foods into fine pieces.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.tr: adv. 严肃地；庄重地；严重地
words.ex: He looked gravely at the broken glass.
words.ex_cn: 他严肃地看着那块碎玻璃。
words.en: In a serious or solemn manner.

words.tr: n. 雕刻师，雕刻刀; 錾刀; 刻具
words.ex: He made a graver mistake than he admitted.
words.ex_cn: 他犯了一个比他承认的更严重的错误。
words.en: A graver is a tool used in engraving or a person who engraves.

words.tr: n. 墓地；坟场；垃圾场；废物堆积处
words.ex: The old graveyard is quiet at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地晚上很安静。
words.en: A graveyard is an area of land, often near a church, where dead people are buried.

words.ex: The gravitational force pulls the apple to the ground.
words.ex_cn: 引力把苹果拉向地面。
words.en: relating to or resulting from the force of gravity

words.ex: The park is full of greenery.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园里到处都是绿色植物。
words.en: Plants and foliage, especially when used for decoration.

words.ex: He greet his friend with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着向朋友问好。
words.en: To greet someone means to say hello to them or to welcome them.

words.tr: n. 僵局；交通堵塞；交通阻塞
words.ex: The traffic caused a gridlock on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 交通导致了高速公路上的严重堵塞。
words.en: A situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of a disagreement or deadlock.

words.tr: adj. 严厉的；严峻的；冷酷无情的；坚定的；可怕的
words.ex: He had a grim look on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严峻的表情。
words.en: If a situation or piece of news is grim, it is very serious, unpleasant, and depressing.

words.tr: adj. 积满污垢的；肮脏的
words.ex: The boy's hands are grimy from playing in the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 男孩的手因为玩土变得脏兮兮的。
words.en: Something that is grimy is very dirty.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.tr:
n. 紧握；掌握；控制；
v. 紧握；掌握；
words.ex: He has a strong grip on the handle.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握住把手。
words.en: To grip something means to hold it tightly. It can also mean to hold someone's attention completely.

words.ex: The children played in the grit near the road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在路边的沙砾中玩耍。
words.en: Grit is very small pieces of stone. It is often used to make surfaces less slippery. Grit is also a quality of character that enables someone to continue with determination in the face of difficulties.

words.ex: He buys milk and bread at the grocery.
words.ex_cn: 他在杂货店买牛奶和面包。
words.en: A grocery is a store where food and small items for the house are sold.

words.ex: The mother grooms her puppy every morning.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈每天早上给她的小狗梳理毛发。
words.en: A groom is a man who is getting married. Also, to groom means to clean and brush an animal, or to prepare someone for a particular job or position.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；低声吼叫；发出隆隆声
n. 咆哮；怒吼声；轰鸣声
words.ex: The dog growl at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 狗向陌生人咆哮。
words.en: To make a deep, guttural sound of anger or hostility, often by an animal.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
