words.en: To cut or shape something with a tool such as an axe, or to make something by cutting.

words.ex: That park was in its heyday in the 1990s.
words.ex_cn: 那个公园在20世纪90年代是它的鼎盛时期。
words.en: The period of a person's or thing's greatest success, popularity, or vigor.

words.ex: Bears hibernate in winter to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠以保存能量。
words.en: To spend the winter in a dormant state.

words.ex: The book has a thick cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有厚厚的封面。
words.en: Having a large distance between the top and bottom or front and back surfaces; not thin.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.ex: Hilary Clinton is a well-known political figure.
words.ex_cn: 希拉里·克林顿是一位知名的政治人物。
words.en: A female given name, also the name of a former US Secretary of State (Hillary Clinton).

words.ex: He grew up in the mountains and was considered a hillbilly by the city folks.
words.ex_cn: 他在山里长大，被城里人认为是乡巴佬。
words.en: A hillbilly is a person from a remote rural or mountainous area, especially from the southern United States, often characterized by a lack of sophistication or education.

words.ex: The children played on the hillside after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在山坡上玩耍。
words.en: The side of a hill.

words.tr: adj. 喜马拉雅山的；喜马拉雅山脉的；喜马拉雅山脉特有的
words.ex: The Himalayan mountain range is the highest in the world.
words.ex_cn: 喜马拉雅山脉是世界上最高的山脉。
words.en: Of or relating to the Himalayas, the highest mountain range in the world, located in Asia.

words.ex: The rain was a hindrance to the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨水对比赛造成了妨碍。
words.en: A hindrance is a person or thing that makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.ex: He fell and hurt his hip.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒了，伤到了臀部。
words.en: The hip is the area on each side of the body below the waist and above the thigh.

words.ex: Hiroshima is a city in Japan that was devastated by an atomic bomb during World War II.
words.ex_cn: 广岛是日本的一个城市，在第二次世界大战期间遭受了原子弹的毁灭性打击。
words.en: Hiroshima is a city in Japan, which is historically significant as the first city to be targeted by a nuclear weapon when the United States dropped an atomic bomb on it on August 6, 1945.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.ex: The bees built a hive in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在树上建了一个蜂巢。
words.en: A hive is a structure where bees live, consisting of a series of cells in which they store honey and raise their young.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.ex: He reads books as a hobby.
words.ex_cn: 他读书作为一种爱好。
words.en: A hobby is an activity that you enjoy doing in your spare time.

words.tr:
n. 锄头
v. 锄（地）；锄（草）
words.ex: He uses a hoe to dig in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他用锄头在花园里翻土。
words.en: A hoe is a gardening tool consisting of a long handle with a flat metal blade at the end, used for breaking up soil and removing weeds.

words.tr:
n. 猪；贪婪的人
v. 攫取；独占
words.ex: The hog is eating corn in the farm.
words.ex_cn: 这头猪在农场里吃玉米。
words.en: A hog is a domesticated pig, especially one that is raised for its meat. It can also refer to a greedy or selfish person. As a verb, to hog means to take or use more than one's fair share of something.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.ex: He believes in holism, so he treats the whole body, not just the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他相信整体论，因此他治疗整个身体，而不仅仅是疼痛。
words.en: Holism is the idea that systems and their properties should be viewed as wholes, not just as a collection of parts.

words.tr: adj. 整体论的；整体主义的；
words.ex: The doctor takes a holistic approach to health.
words.ex_cn: 这位医生采取整体论的方法来治疗健康问题。
words.en: A holistic approach to something involves considering the whole thing, rather than just a part of it.

words.ex: He lives in Holland with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人住在荷兰。
words.en: Holland is a region and former province on the western coast of the Netherlands. The name Holland is also frequently used informally to refer to the whole of the country of the Netherlands.

words.tr: n. 自酿（啤）酒; 公司自产自用
words.ex: He enjoys making his own homebrew beer.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢自酿啤酒。
words.en: Homebrew refers to beer or other alcoholic beverages that are made at home, rather than commercially. It can also refer to any product or solution that is made by an individual or group for their own use, often implying a DIY or custom approach.

words.tr:
adj. 回家的；回国的
adv. 向家；向本国
words.ex: He walked homeward after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后往家走。
words.en: If you are going homeward, you are going towards your home.

words.ex: He pulled the hood over his head to stay dry.
words.ex_cn: 他把兜帽拉到头上以保持干燥。
words.en: A hood is a part of a coat or jacket that you can pull up to cover your head.

words.tr:
n. （马等动物的）蹄
v.  走；步行；以蹄踢（踏）
words.ex: The horse stepped on the rock with its hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马用蹄子踩在石头上。
words.en: The horny part of the foot of an ungulate animal, especially a horse.

words.tr:
n. 猫头鹰叫声；汽笛响声；叫嚣声
v. 作猫头鹰叫声；汽笛等嘟嘟响；大声叫嚣
words.ex: The hoot of an owl echoed through the night.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰的叫声在夜晚回荡。
words.en: To make the sound that an owl makes, or to make a similar sound as a signal or in disapproval.

words.tr: adj. 荣誉的；名誉的；道义上的
words.ex: He received an honorary degree for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的工作获得了荣誉学位。
words.en: Given as an honor without the usual requirements or duties.

words.ex: The frog hopped over the stone.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙跃过了那块石头。
words.en: To move by jumping on one foot or to move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: He felt hopeless after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到毫无希望。
words.en: If you feel hopeless, you feel very unhappy because there seems to be no possibility of a better situation or success.

words.ex: The boy drew a line horizontally on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在纸上水平地画了一条线。
words.en: In a horizontal direction or position.

words.ex: The movie was horribly scary.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常可怕。
words.en: In a manner that causes horror or is extremely unpleasant.

words.ex: The horseshoe is nailed to a horse's hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马蹄形铁掌被钉在马的蹄子上。
words.en: A horseshoe is a piece of metal shaped like a U, which is fixed with nails to the bottom of a horse's foot in order to protect it.

words.ex: The boy whose bag is red is my brother.
words.ex_cn: 那个书包是红色的男孩是我弟弟。
words.en: You use whose to ask about the person that something belongs to or is associated with.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.ex: The bird hovers above the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在花上空盘旋。
words.en: To remain in one place in the air, or to stay close to someone or something.

words.ex: The wolf howl at the moon.
words.ex_cn: 狼对着月亮嚎叫。
words.en: If a dog or wolf howls, it makes a long, loud, crying sound. If a person howls, they make a long, loud cry expressing pain, anger, or unhappiness.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.ex: The hue of the sky changed at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空的色调发生了变化。
words.en: A hue is a particular shade of a color.

words.ex: He showed humility after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得奖品后表现出了谦逊。
words.en: Humility is the quality of being humble and not thinking that you are better than other people.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.ex: He hurled the ball across the field.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地把球投过球场。
words.en: To throw something with great force; to shout something loudly.

words.ex: The children built a hut in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树林里建了一间小屋。
words.en: A hut is a small, simple building, usually consisting of one room and made of materials such as wood, mud, or grass.

words.ex: The hydrosphere includes all the water on Earth.
words.ex_cn: 水圈包括地球上所有的水。
words.en: The hydrosphere is the combined mass of water found on, under, and above the surface of a planet, minor planet, or natural satellite.

words.ex: Scientists hypothesize that water once existed on Mars.
words.ex_cn: 科学家假设火星上曾经存在水。
words.en: To hypothesize means to suggest a possible explanation for something, which has not yet been proved to be true.

words.ex: His idealism drives him to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的理想主义驱使他帮助穷人。
words.en: Idealism is the belief that your ideals can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others.

words.tr: n. 识别符；检验人；标识符；鉴别器；编号；
words.ex: The system uses an identifier to find your account.
words.ex_cn: 系统使用一个识别符来查找你的账户。
words.en: An identifier is a name or number that is used to recognize something or someone.

words.tr: n. （观赏鱼类）圆腹雅罗鱼（同orfe）; n. （Ide）（爱尔兰、巴西、美）艾德（人名）
words.ex: The ide is a popular ornamental fish in aquariums.
words.ex_cn: 圆腹雅罗鱼是水族馆中受欢迎的观赏鱼。
words.en: A rare or archaic term for a stream or brook, often used in poetic or regional contexts.

words.ex: He used an idiomatic expression in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个惯用表达。
words.en: If you refer to someone's idiomatic use of a language, you mean that they use it in a way that sounds natural and correct to native speakers of that language.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.ex: The car moved rapidly down the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车迅速地沿着道路行驶。
words.en: If something happens rapidly, it happens very quickly.

words.ex: The illegitimate business was shut down by the police.
words.ex_cn: 这个非法的生意被警察关闭了。
words.en: An illegitimate child is one whose parents were not married to each other when the child was born. Something that is illegitimate is not allowed by the rules or laws.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr: adj. 非现金的；无流动资金的
words.ex: The company has illiquid assets that cannot be sold quickly.
words.ex_cn: 该公司拥有无法迅速出售的非现金资产。
words.en: If something is illiquid, it cannot easily be sold or exchanged for cash without a substantial loss in value.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.tr: v. 牺牲；宰杀作祭品；献祭
words.ex: He decided to immolate himself in protest.
words.ex_cn: 他决定自焚以示抗议。
words.en: To kill or offer as a sacrifice, especially by burning.

words.ex: Vaccines help build immunity against diseases.
words.ex_cn: 疫苗有助于增强对疾病的免疫力。
words.en: Immunity is the state of being immune from or insusceptible to a particular disease or the legal status of being exempt from certain obligations or penalties.

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.tr: v. 监禁；禁闭；把...嵌在墙上
words.ex: He was immured in the old tower for years.
words.ex_cn: 他被囚禁在那座旧塔里多年。
words.en: To confine someone within or as if within walls; imprison.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: The judge treated both sides impartially.
words.ex_cn: 法官公平地对待了双方。
words.en: In a way that is not biased or prejudiced; fairly.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.tr: adj. 不能通行的；无路可通的
words.ex: The road became impassable after the heavy snowfall.
words.ex_cn: 大雪过后，这条路变得无法通行。
words.en: If a road or path is impassable, it is impossible to travel along it because it is blocked or in bad condition.

words.ex: The speaker's words impassioned the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者的话语激起了群众的热情。
words.en: To fill someone with passion or enthusiasm; to arouse strong feelings in someone.

words.ex: He is impatient when he waits for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时很不耐烦。
words.en: If you are impatient, you are easily annoyed by delays or by people making mistakes.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.ex: The construction work was impeditive to the flow of traffic.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工程阻碍了交通的流动。
words.en: Serving or tending to impede; obstructive.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.tr: adv. 冷淡地，客观地; 与个人无关地
words.ex: The company responded impersonally to the customer's complaint.
words.ex_cn: 公司对顾客的投诉冷淡回应。
words.en: In a way that does not show or involve personal feelings.

words.ex: He tried to impersonate a police officer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图冒充一名警察。
words.en: To impersonate someone means to pretend to be that person, either to deceive people or to entertain them.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.ex: She solved the math problem impressively.
words.ex_cn: 她令人印象深刻地解出了这道数学题。
words.en: In a manner that attracts attention or admiration through being notable or extraordinary.

words.ex: He faced imprisonment for stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷钱而面临监禁。
words.en: The state of being confined in prison; the act of putting someone in prison or the condition of being kept in prison.

words.ex: The implementation of the new rule took one month.
words.ex_cn: 新规则的履行花了一个月。
words.en: The act of putting a decision or plan into effect; execution.

words.ex: It is improbable that he will arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 他准时到达的可能性很小。
words.en: If you describe something as improbable, you mean it is unlikely to be true or to happen.

words.tr:
adj. 无准备的；即兴的；即席的
adv. 无准备地；即兴地；即席地
words.ex: He gave an impromptu speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: An impromptu action is one that you do without planning or organizing it in advance.

words.tr: v. 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时准备；
words.ex: He improvise a song on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他即兴创作了一首钢琴曲。
words.en: If you improvise, you make or do something using whatever you have or without having planned it in advance.

words.tr: adj. 难以达到的；无法接近的；
words.ex: The mountain peak is inaccessible in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这座山峰在冬天难以到达。
words.en: If a place is inaccessible, it is very difficult or impossible to reach or enter.

words.tr: n. 不准确；不精确；错误
words.ex: The inaccuracy of the clock caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 钟的不准确导致了延误。
words.en: The quality or state of being inaccurate; error.

words.tr: adv. 不精密地，不准确地
words.ex: He described the events inaccurately.
words.ex_cn: 他对事件的描述不准确。
words.en: In a manner that is not accurate; not precisely.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；空洞的；无意义的
words.ex: His inane comments made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他无聊的评论让每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone's comments or ideas as inane, you mean they are very silly or stupid.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.tr:
adj. 就职的；开幕的；创立的
n. 就职演说
words.ex: He gave his inaugural speech last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚发表了就职演讲。
words.en: An inaugural event or speech is the first in a series planned to celebrate or introduce something.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: The incandescent bulb gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 白炽灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

words.ex: His incapability to handle stress led to his resignation.
words.ex_cn: 他应对压力的无能使他辞职了。
words.en: The state of being unable to do something.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: The company will incentivize employees with bonuses.
words.ex_cn: 公司将用奖金激励员工。
words.en: To incentivize someone means to provide them with a good reason for wanting to do something, often by offering a reward.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.ex: He is tapping his pen incessantly.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地敲打钢笔。
words.en: Without interruption; constantly.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.tr: adv. 不替别人考虑地，考虑不周地，轻率地
words.ex: She acted inconsiderately by leaving without saying goodbye.
words.ex_cn: 她没打招呼就离开了，真是考虑不周。
words.en: In a manner that shows a lack of thoughtfulness or consideration for others.

words.ex: His answers were inconsistent.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案不一致。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsistent, you are criticizing them for not behaving in the same way every time a similar situation occurs.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: The road closure caused an inconvenience to commuters.
words.ex_cn: 道路封闭给通勤者带来了不便。
words.en: Inconvenience refers to the state or quality of being inconvenient; trouble or difficulty caused to one's personal requirements or comfort.

words.ex: She arrived inconveniently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 她开会迟到了，很不方便。
words.en: In a manner that causes trouble or difficulty; not conveniently.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.tr: v. 遭受，招致，引起( incur的现在分词 )
words.ex: The company is incurring significant debt to finance the project.
words.ex_cn: 公司为了资助这个项目正在招致大量债务。
words.en: To incur something means to experience it, usually something unpleasant, as a result of actions you have taken.

words.tr: n. 优柔寡断；犹豫不决
words.ex: He showed indecision when choosing between the two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择两份工作时表现出犹豫不决。
words.en: Indecision is the inability to make decisions quickly and effectively.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.tr: adj. 难以形容的；无法描述的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was indescribable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美无法形容。
words.en: If you describe something as indescribable, you mean that it is so extreme, unusual, or shocking that you cannot describe it.

words.ex: The unemployment rate is an economic indicator.
words.ex_cn: 失业率是一个经济指标。
words.en: An indicator is a measurement or value which gives you an idea of what something is like.

words.ex: The prosecutor read the indictment in court.
words.ex_cn: 检察官在法庭上宣读了起诉状。
words.en: An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.

words.ex: He is indisputably the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a manner that is impossible to question or argue about.

words.tr:
adj. 独立制作的
n. （音乐或电影的）独立制作公司
words.ex: She is an indie filmmaker known for her unique style.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位以其独特风格闻名的独立制片人。
words.en: Indie is used to describe something, especially a band, film, or company, that is not part of a large, well-known organization, but is independent.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: The fiber is indigestible for humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种纤维对人类来说不易消化。
words.en: If food is indigestible, it is difficult or impossible for your stomach to break it down and use it.

words.ex: He ate too much and had indigestion.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，导致消化不良。
words.en: Indigestion is pain or discomfort in your stomach, usually after eating, which is caused by difficulty in digesting food.

words.ex: The evidence is indisputable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可争辩的。
words.en: Something that is indisputable is true and cannot be denied or questioned.

words.tr: adj. 不显著的；无特色的
words.ex: The painting was so indistinctive that it blended into the background.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画如此不显著，以至于它与背景融为一体。
words.en: Lacking distinctive qualities or features; not easily distinguishable.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.ex: She lives in Indonesia.
words.ex_cn: 她住在印度尼西亚。
words.en: A country in Southeast Asia, consisting of an archipelago between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean, known for its diverse cultures, languages, and biodiversity.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: The scientist explained the concept inductively, starting from specific examples and leading to a general conclusion.
words.ex_cn: 科学家通过从具体例子开始并引向一般结论的方式，归纳地解释了这个概念。
words.en: In a way that uses particular facts or examples to form a general rule or principle.

words.ex: The old machine causes inefficiency in production.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器导致生产效率低下。
words.en: The lack of ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.tr: n. 不合适；不擅长；笨拙；无能
words.ex: His ineptitude made him unsuitable for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他的不合适让他不适合这份工作。
words.en: Lack of skill or ability; incompetence.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.tr: adv. 不可逆转地；不可阻挡地；冷酷无情地
words.ex: Time moves inexorably forward.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地向前流逝。
words.en: If something happens inexorably, it happens in a way that cannot be prevented or stopped.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.tr: v. 使冲昏头脑；弄糊涂；使着迷
words.ex: He is infatuated with his new classmate.
words.ex_cn: 他迷上了他的新同学。
words.en: To inspire with a foolish or extravagant love or admiration.

words.tr: adv. 无限地；无穷地；极大地；
words.ex: The stars are infinitely far away.
words.ex_cn: 星星离得无限远。
words.en: In a way that is without limits or bounds; extremely or immeasurably.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.tr: n. 刚性; 不屈性，顽固，不变性; 不可弯曲; 非挠性
words.ex: The inflexibility of the metal made it hard to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种金属的刚性使其难以弯曲。
words.en: The quality of being unwilling to change or compromise; rigidity.

words.ex: The rules are inflexible and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则是不灵活的，不能更改。
words.en: If you say that someone is inflexible, you are criticizing them because they refuse to change their mind or alter their way of doing things.

words.ex: The inflow of water filled the tank quickly.
words.ex_cn: 水的流入很快填满了水箱。
words.en: The movement of a substance into a place or system.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The problem was solved ingeniously.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题被巧妙地解决了。
words.en: In a manner showing cleverness or originality in solving problems or in inventing.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.tr: n. 忘恩负义; 得鱼忘荃
words.ex: Her ingratitude after all he'd done for her was painful.
words.ex_cn: 他为她所做的一切换来的却是她的忘恩负义，这让他感到痛苦。
words.en: Lack of gratitude or appreciation.

words.ex: He inhale the fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上吸入新鲜空气。
words.en: To inhale means to breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.ex: The company's policies were inimical to the interests of its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的政策对员工的利益是有害的。
words.en: If one thing is inimical to another, it prevents the second thing from happening or being successful, or it is harmful to it.

words.ex: The small boat docked at the inlet.
words.ex_cn: 小船停靠在小水湾。
words.en: An inlet is a narrow strip of water that leads from a sea or lake into the land or between islands.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: The chef carefully removed the innards of the fish.
words.ex_cn: 厨师小心翼翼地取出了鱼的内脏。
words.en: The internal parts of something, especially a machine or the body.

words.ex: He is an innovator who created a new app.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创造了新应用程序的创新者。
words.en: An innovator is someone who introduces changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.tr: n. [医] 接种；接木；接插芽
words.ex: The child received inoculation against measles last week.
words.ex_cn: 孩子上周接种了麻疹疫苗。
words.en: The act of introducing a vaccine into the body to produce immunity to a specific disease.

words.ex: The police opened an inquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An inquiry is a question which you ask in order to get some information.

words.ex: The inquisitive child asked many questions about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 这个好奇的孩子问了很多关于星星的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as inquisitive, you mean that they are interested in a lot of different things and want to find out more about them.

words.tr: adv. 过分好奇地; 好问地
words.ex: She looked at him inquisitively, trying to read his thoughts.
words.ex_cn: 她好奇地看着他，试图读懂他的心思。
words.en: In a manner showing curiosity or interest in learning about something.

words.ex: The army made an inroad into the enemy's territory.
words.ex_cn: 军队对敌方领土发动了一次袭击。
words.en: An inroad is an advance or penetration often at the expense of someone or something, or a hostile incursion or invasion.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；精神失常；疯狂
words.ex: He was sent to a hospital because of insanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因精神错乱被送进了医院。
words.en: Insanity is the state of being seriously mentally ill; madness.

words.tr: adv. 不知足地；贪得无厌地
words.ex: He read books insatiably, always craving more knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他如饥似渴地读书，总是渴望更多的知识。
words.en: In a way that cannot be satisfied.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr: n. 不敏感；麻木不仁；感觉迟钝
words.ex: His insensitivity hurt his friend's feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的冷漠伤害了朋友的感情。
words.en: The quality of not being aware of or not being able to understand other people's feelings.

words.ex: The insider told the news about the company's plan.
words.ex_cn: 这位局内人透露了公司计划的消息。
words.en: An insider is someone who is a member of a group or organization, and therefore has special knowledge about it.

words.tr: adj. 坚持的；迫切要求的；持续的
words.ex: He is insistent about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: If someone is insistent, they keep demanding something and refuse to accept any opposition or excuses.

words.ex: She tapped her fingers insistently on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她坚持不懈地用手指敲打着桌子。
words.en: If you say something insistently, you say it firmly and repeatedly, especially because you want to make your point clear.

words.ex: The company went bankrupt due to insolvency.
words.ex_cn: 由于资不抵债，这家公司破产了。
words.en: The state of being unable to pay one's debts.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.ex: The installation of the new machine took two days.
words.ex_cn: 新机器的安置花了两天时间。
words.en: The act of installing or the state of being installed.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.ex: She instinctively reached for her phone when it rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，她下意识地伸手去拿手机。
words.en: If you behave instinctively, you do something without thinking about it because it seems natural or the right thing to do.

words.ex: The teacher used an instructional video to explain the lesson.
words.ex_cn: 老师使用了一段教学视频来讲解课程。
words.en: Relating to the process of teaching or providing knowledge.

words.ex: The instructor explained the math problem clearly.
words.ex_cn: 教员清楚地讲解了这道数学题。
words.en: An instructor is someone who teaches a skill or subject, especially in a college or university, or in a specialized field such as driving or skiing.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.ex: The house has good insulation to keep warm in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有良好的绝缘层以在冬天保暖。
words.en: Insulation is a material or substance that is used to stop heat, electricity, or sound from going from one place to another.

words.tr:
v. 侮辱；辱骂
n. 侮辱；辱骂
words.ex: He insulted her with rude words.
words.ex_cn: 他用粗鲁的话侮辱了她。
words.en: To insult someone means to say or do something that is rude or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的； v. “insult”的现在分词；
words.ex: His insulting words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as insulting, you mean they are rude and offensive.

words.ex: The government is struggling to control the ongoing insurgency.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在努力控制持续的叛乱。
words.en: An insurgency is a violent attempt to oppose a country's government carried out by citizens of that country.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.tr:
n. 凹雕
v. 凹雕
words.ex: The artist used intaglio to create a detailed image.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家使用凹雕术创作了一幅细节丰富的图像。
words.en: Intaglio is a technique in art where an image is created by cutting, carving, or engraving into a flat surface, making it a form of printmaking or sculpture.

words.ex: The number 5 is an integer.
words.ex_cn: 数字5是一个整数。
words.en: An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero.

words.ex: He studied the problem intensively.
words.ex_cn: 他集中地研究了这个问题。
words.en: In a way that involves a lot of effort or activity in a short period of time.

words.tr: adv. 互动; 交互式的
words.ex: The software allows users to work interactively with the data.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许用户与数据进行互动操作。
words.en: In a way that involves communication between people or between people and computers, with immediate response and exchange of information.

words.ex: The two cultures have a lot of interchange.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化有很多交流。
words.en: The act or process of exchanging things with each other, especially ideas or information.

words.ex: These two words are interchangeable in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 这两个词在这个句子中可以互换使用。
words.en: If one thing is interchangeable with another, the first can be used instead of the second because it has the same function or meaning.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: The program helps intergenerational families share stories.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目帮助代际家庭分享故事。
words.en: Relating to or involving different generations, especially in families or societies.

words.ex: The agreement was reached through intergovernmental negotiations.
words.ex_cn: 该协议是通过政府间谈判达成的。
words.en: Involving or relating to two or more governments.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.tr:
vt. 连接；把……互相连结
n. 连环
words.ex: The roads interlink the small towns.
words.ex_cn: 这些道路将各个小镇连接在一起。
words.en: to connect or link together

words.ex: The interlocutor asked a series of probing questions.
words.ex_cn: 对话者提出了一系列尖锐的问题。
words.en: An interlocutor is someone who takes part in a conversation or dialogue, often in a formal or official capacity.

words.tr: n. 间歇；插曲；幕间节目
words.ex: He took an interlude to drink water.
words.ex_cn: 他休息了一下喝水。
words.en: An interlude is a short period of time that comes in the middle of something, or a short piece of music, talk, or entertainment that comes between the main parts of a performance or event.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: The company plans internationalization next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划明年进行国际化。
words.en: The process of making something international in scope or application.

words.ex: The teacher gave a simple interpretation of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这首诗做了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An interpretation of something is an explanation or understanding of it.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.ex: She intersperses flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里分散地种着花。
words.en: To place something at intervals among other things.

words.tr: adj. 州与州之间的；州际的；
words.ex: The interstate highway connects many states.
words.ex_cn: 州际公路连接了许多州。
words.en: An interstate is a highway that connects different states within a country.

words.ex: The two stories intertwine in the final chapter.
words.ex_cn: 这两个故事在最后一章交织在一起。
words.en: If two or more things are intertwined, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

words.ex: The intervertebral disc acts as a cushion between the vertebrae.
words.ex_cn: 椎间盘在椎骨之间起到缓冲作用。
words.en: Located or occurring between vertebrae.

words.tr: n. 被面试者；被采访者；
words.ex: The interviewee answered all the questions calmly.
words.ex_cn: 被面试者冷静地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A person who is interviewed.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr: adj. 令人紧张不安的；令人胆怯的；
words.ex: The big dog looked intimidating to the small child.
words.ex_cn: 那只大狗看起来让小孩子感到紧张不安。
words.en: Something that is intimidating makes you feel nervous and frightened because it is very difficult, dangerous, or extreme.

words.ex: His intonation made the sentence sound friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他的语调让这句话听起来很友好。
words.en: Intonation is the way the voice rises and falls in speech, especially the pitch pattern in a sentence.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.tr:
adj. 醉人的
n. 酒精饮料；致醉药物
words.ex: Alcohol is a common intoxicant.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是一种常见的致醉物。
words.en: An intoxicant is a substance that can cause intoxication, such as alcohol or drugs.

words.ex: The company uses an intranet to share files.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用内网来共享文件。
words.en: An intranet is a private network accessible only to an organization's staff, often used to share company information and computing resources among employees.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.ex: She is intrinsically kind.
words.ex_cn: 她本质上是善良的。
words.en: If something is intrinsically good or bad, it is so because of its own nature, and not because of any external circumstances or factors.

words.tr: adv. 好反省的，好内省的
words.ex: She analyzed her feelings introspectively.
words.ex_cn: 她内省地分析了自己的感受。
words.en: In a manner characterized by introspection; examining one's own thoughts and feelings.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: His intrusive questions made her uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他打搅的问题让她感到不舒服。
words.en: Something that is intrusive disturbs your privacy or peace in an unwanted way.

words.ex: She could intuit what her friend was thinking.
words.ex_cn: 她能凭直觉知道她朋友在想什么。
words.en: To know or understand something immediately without conscious reasoning.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.ex: The heavy rain caused an inundation in the village.
words.ex_cn: 大雨导致了村庄的洪水。
words.en: An inundation is a large amount of water covering an area that is usually dry.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The inverse order of the numbers is 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的倒序是5、4、3、2、1。
words.en: If there is an inverse relationship between two things, one of them becomes larger as the other becomes smaller.

words.ex: The speed is inversely proportional to the time.
words.ex_cn: 速度与时间成反比。
words.en: In an inverse manner; in the opposite order, direction, or effect.

words.ex: The police conducted an investigatory search of the premises.
words.ex_cn: 警方对现场进行了调查搜查。
words.en: Relating to or involved in investigation.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.tr: adv. 惹人怨恨地；不公平地
words.ex: He spoke invidiously about his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他惹人怨恨地谈论他的同事。
words.en: In a manner that is likely to arouse resentment or anger in others.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The invoker pleaded for divine intervention.
words.ex_cn: 祈求者恳求神灵的干预。
words.en: An invoker is someone who calls on or appeals to a higher power for help or inspiration, or someone who causes something to happen by mentioning or using it.

words.tr: adv. 非自愿地；非出于本意地；无意地
words.ex: He blinked involuntarily when the light flashed.
words.ex_cn: 当灯光闪现时，他不由自主地眨了眨眼。
words.en: Involuntarily means done without will or conscious control.

words.ex: The process of ionization can be caused by high-energy radiation.
words.ex_cn: 离子化过程可以由高能辐射引起。
words.en: The process by which an atom or a molecule acquires a negative or positive charge by gaining or losing electrons, often in conjunction with other chemical changes.

words.ex: This acid is ionizable in water.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸在水中可以电离。
words.en: Capable of being ionized.

words.ex: The gas ionize when electricity passes through it.
words.ex_cn: 当电流通过时，气体被电离。
words.en: To convert (an atom, molecule, or substance) into an ion or ions, typically by removing one or more electrons.

words.ex: The ionosphere reflects radio waves.
words.ex_cn: 电离层反射无线电波。
words.en: The ionosphere is a layer of the Earth's atmosphere that is ionized by solar and cosmic radiation. It plays a crucial role in atmospheric electricity and forms the inner edge of the magnetosphere. It is important for radio communication as it reflects and modifies radio waves used for communication and navigation.

words.ex: He didn't care about an iota of the details.
words.ex_cn: 他对这些细节的极小量都不在意。
words.en: An iota is an extremely small amount of something.

words.ex: His voice trembled with ire.
words.ex_cn: 他的声音因愤怒而颤抖。
words.en: Anger or wrath.

words.ex: He is careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很谨慎。
words.en: Full of anger; wrathful.

words.tr: adj. 使人厌烦的；令人生气的
words.ex: The irksome noise from the construction site kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的恼人噪音让我整晚都没睡着。
words.en: If something is irksome, it annoys you.

words.ex: Farmers irrigate their fields with water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民用河里的水灌溉他们的田地。
words.en: To supply land or crops with water by means of channels or pipes.

words.ex: She loves Irish music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢爱尔兰音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Irish means belonging or relating to Ireland, or to its people, language, or culture.

words.ex: He said it was 'great' when he was late, in an ironical tone.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，却用反语的语气说这‘太棒了’。
words.en: If you describe something as ironical, you mean that it involves a contrast or a result that is the opposite of what you expected.

words.ex: The process involves the irradiation of seeds to improve germination.
words.ex_cn: 这个过程包括对种子进行照射以提高发芽率。
words.en: The process of exposing something to radiation, especially for the purpose of sterilization or preservation.

words.tr: adj. 无可辩驳的；不能否认的
words.ex: The evidence is irrefutable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If you describe something such as evidence or a fact as irrefutable, you mean that it cannot be denied or disproved.

words.tr: n. 不规则；无规律；不合常规；不整齐
words.ex: The teacher noticed an irregularity in the test scores.
words.ex_cn: 老师注意到考试成绩中有一个异常。
words.en: The state or quality of being irregular; something that is irregular.

words.ex: This photo is irreplaceable.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片是不可替代的。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as irreplaceable, you mean that they are so good or valuable that it would be impossible to replace them.

words.ex: The irresistibility of the chocolate made her eat it all.
words.ex_cn: 巧克力的诱人魅力让她吃光了它。
words.en: The quality of being too attractive or powerful to be resisted.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.tr: adv. 无可挽回地；不可逆转地；无可救药地
words.ex: He irrevocably quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他不可逆转地辞了工作。
words.en: In a way that cannot be changed, reversed, or recovered.

words.ex: His irritability made it hard to talk to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的易怒让他很难沟通。
words.en: Irritability is the quality of being easily annoyed or made angry.

words.tr: n. 欧文（姓氏；地名，位于美国加利福尼亚州）
words.ex: Irvine is a city in California.
words.ex_cn: 尔湾是加利福尼亚的一个城市。
words.en: A city in Orange County, California, USA, known for its business parks and universities.

words.ex: Irving is walking to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 欧文每天早上步行去学校。
words.en: A male given name, also the name of a city in Texas, USA, and a famous author (Washington Irving).

words.tr: adj. 伊斯兰教的；穆斯林的；
words.ex: The Islamic mosque is very old.
words.ex_cn: 这座伊斯兰教清真寺非常古老。
words.en: Relating to Islam or its culture, principles, and practices.

words.ex: He believes in socialism.
words.ex_cn: 他相信社会主义。
words.en: An ism is a belief, theory, or practice that has a name ending in '-ism'.

words.ex: The country follows isolationism to avoid foreign wars.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家奉行孤立主义以避免卷入外国战争。
words.en: A policy of remaining apart from the affairs or interests of other groups, especially the political affairs of other countries.

words.ex: The word 'hello' is written in italic.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'hello' 是用斜体写的。
words.en: Italic refers to a style of printing or writing in which the letters slope to the right.

words.tr: vt. 用斜体字排字，在字下划横线
words.ex: He will italicize the key words in the text.
words.ex_cn: 他将把文本中的关键词用斜体标出。
words.en: To italicize means to print or write in italics, a style of typeface that slants to the right. It is often used for emphasis, to denote titles, or to indicate foreign words.

words.tr: v. 列出清单；逐条列记
words.ex: He will itemize his expenses on the form.
words.ex_cn: 他将在表格上逐项列出他的开支。
words.en: To itemize means to list things separately, often including details about each one.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.tr: n. 象牙；象牙色 adj. 象牙色的
words.ex: The old piano has ivory keys.
words.ex_cn: 这架旧钢琴有象牙键。
words.en: Ivory is a hard, white material from the tusks and teeth of animals, which is used to make or decorate objects.

words.ex: Jacob is my best friend.
words.ex_cn: 雅各布是我最好的朋友。
words.en: A male given name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'supplanter' or 'held by the heel'.

words.tr: n. 牙买加（加勒比海岛国）
words.ex: He is from Jamaica.
words.ex_cn: 他来自牙买加。
words.en: Jamaica is an island country situated in the Caribbean Sea.

words.ex: The janitor cleans the school every night.
words.ex_cn: 门卫每天晚上打扫学校。
words.en: A janitor is a person whose job is to take care of a building, especially by cleaning it.

words.tr: n. 雅努斯（罗马神话中的门神，有两张脸，一张向前看，一张向后看）
words.ex: He is as changeable as Janus.
words.ex_cn: 他像雅努斯一样善变。
words.en: In Roman mythology, Janus is the god of beginnings, gates, transitions, time, duality, doorways, passages, and endings. He is usually depicted as having two faces, since he looks to the future and to the past.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.tr: adj. 爵士乐的; <俚>绚丽的 “jazz”的派生
words.ex: He wears a jazzy hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶花哨的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as jazzy, you mean that it is bright, colorful, and showy, often in a way that is considered to be in the style of jazz music.

words.ex: The fabric is made of thick jean.
words.ex_cn: 这种布料是由厚实的斜纹布制成的。
words.en: Jeans are casual trousers made from denim or dungaree cloth, often called 'blue jeans' or just 'jeans'.

words.ex: Jeff is a common name for a man.
words.ex_cn: 杰夫是一个常见的男子名。
words.en: A common male given name, often a short form of Jeffrey or Geoffrey.

words.tr: n. 耶利米（男子名，源自希伯来语，意为‘耶和华至高’）
words.ex: Jeremiah walks to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 杰里米亚每天早上走路去上学。
words.en: A person who is pessimistic and always predicts bad things will happen.

words.ex: Jeremy is a common English name.
words.ex_cn: 杰里米是一个常见的英文名字。
words.en: jeremy

words.tr: n. 乘喷气式飞机到处旅游的富佬；名流人物
words.ex: He is a jet-setter who travels to Paris every month.
words.ex_cn: 他是个经常飞往巴黎的环球旅行者。
words.en: A jet-setter is a wealthy person who frequently travels by jet to fashionable places for pleasure.

words.ex: He eats jewish food on holidays.
words.ex_cn: 他在节日吃犹太人的食物。
words.en: Jewish means relating to the religion, culture, or people of the Jews.

words.tr: adj. 好开玩笑的，滑稽的
words.ex: He told a jokey story to make us laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个搞笑的故事来让我们笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is jokey, you mean that they are in the habit of making jokes or that they are in a mood to make jokes.

words.tr: adv. 开玩笑地；闹着玩地；戏谑地
words.ex: He said it jokingly, but everyone laughed.
words.ex_cn: 他开玩笑地说了这句话，但大家都笑了。
words.en: In a manner that is intended to be humorous or not serious.

words.ex: He jogs every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上慢跑以保持健康。
words.en: To run at a slow, steady pace, especially as a form of exercise.

words.ex: The sudden jolt woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 突然的震动把我惊醒了。
words.en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

words.ex: The jolty ride made her feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 颠簸的旅程让她感到恶心。
words.en: adj. Characterized by sudden jerks or bumps; causing a feeling of being shaken or jolted.

words.tr:
v. 挤；推；撞；争夺
n. 挤拥；推撞
words.ex: People jostle in the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 人们在拥挤的市场里推挤。
words.en: To jostle someone means to push or knock against them, usually in a crowd.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.tr:
n. 司法部；司法制度；法官（总称）
adj. 司法的；法院的；法官的
words.ex: The judiciary made a fair decision.
words.ex_cn: 司法部做出了公正的裁决。
words.en: The judiciary is the system of courts that interprets and applies the law in the name of the state.

words.ex: He drinks orange juice every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝橙汁。
words.en: The liquid obtained from or present in fruit or vegetables.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

words.ex: The junta seized power in a military coup.
words.ex_cn: 军政府通过军事政变夺取了政权。
words.en: A junta is a military government that has taken power by force, not by election.

words.ex: The junto made decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这个小团体在不征求他人意见的情况下做出了决定。
words.en: A junto is a small group of people who join together to achieve a particular purpose, especially in politics, often secretly.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.ex: The juror voted guilty after listening to the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 这位陪审员在听取证据后投票判定有罪。
words.en: A juror is a member of a jury, which is a group of people in a court of law who listen to the facts of a case and decide whether someone is guilty or not.

words.tr: adv. 言之有理地；无可非议地
words.ex: He justifiably won the award for his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他因努力工作而理所当然地赢得了奖项。
words.en: For actions or beliefs that are justifiably held or done, there are good reasons that support them.

words.tr: adv. 公正地；正当地；应得地
words.ex: He was justly punished for lying.
words.ex_cn: 他因为撒谎而得到了应有的惩罚。
words.en: In a fair and deserved manner; rightly.

words.tr: adv. 仅仅；就；只是；刚刚；恰好；
words.ex: He just wants to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅想睡觉。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is exactly the case or is happening at this moment.

words.tr: n. 烤腌羊肉串；肉串上的肉块
words.ex: He eats a kebab for dinner every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五吃烤肉串当晚餐。
words.en: A dish consisting of small pieces of meat, fish, or vegetables roasted or grilled on a skewer or spit.

words.ex: The zoo keeper feeds the lions every morning.
words.ex_cn: 动物园饲养员每天早上喂狮子。
words.en: A keeper is someone whose job is to look after a particular place or thing.

words.ex: Keith is playing soccer with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 基思正在和朋友们踢足球。
words.en: A male given name, often associated with musicians or athletes.

words.ex: The kidnapper took the boy and demanded money.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪绑架了那个男孩并索要赎金。
words.en: A kidnapper is a person who abducts someone and holds them captive, typically to demand a ransom.

words.ex: He drank water to help his kidney work better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝水以帮助肾脏更好地工作。
words.en: One of the two organs in your lower back that separate waste products from your blood and make urine.

words.tr: adj. 较慈祥的; 较体贴的; 较友好的; 较宽容的
words.ex: He is kinder to his little brother now.
words.ex_cn: 他现在对弟弟更友善了。
words.en: comparative of kind; more kind.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.ex: They felt a strong kinship because they grew up in the same village.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为从小在同一个村庄长大，感到有很强的亲属关系。
words.en: Kinship is the relationship between members of the same family.

words.tr: n. 基辛格（美国前国务卿）
words.ex: Kissinger negotiated peace talks in the 1970s.
words.ex_cn: 基辛格在20世纪70年代谈判了和平会谈。
words.en: A German-born American political scientist and diplomat who served as US Secretary of State.

words.ex: He bought a repair kit for his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套自行车维修工具。
words.en: A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.

words.ex: He turned the knob to adjust the volume.
words.ex_cn: 他转动旋钮来调节音量。
words.en: A knob is a round handle, or a round switch on a piece of equipment.

words.tr:
n. 指关节
v. 用指关节…；屈从
words.ex: He cracked his knuckles before the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛前掰响了指关节。
words.en: The knuckles are the joints of the fingers, especially where they join the hand.

words.ex: He received kudos for winning the science competition.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得科学竞赛而获得荣誉。
words.en: Praise and honor received for an achievement.

words.ex: The laborer works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人每天努力工作。
words.en: A laborer is a person who does unskilled physical work, especially outdoors.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr:
n. 地方；方位；
v. 安放；安置；
words.ex: This is a quiet place to read books.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个安静的地方读书。
words.en: A particular position or point in space.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.ex: The truck is laden with boxes.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车装满了箱子。
words.en: If someone or something is laden with a lot of heavy things, they are holding or carrying them.

words.tr: n. 拉格啤酒；贮藏啤酒
words.ex: He drinks lager at the pub.
words.ex_cn: 他在酒吧喝拉格啤酒。
words.en: A type of beer that is stored at a low temperature for a period of time to allow it to mature and develop its flavor.

words.ex: The children swam in the clear lagoon.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在清澈的潟湖里游泳。
words.en: A lagoon is a body of water separated from larger bodies of water by a natural barrier such as a sandbar, coral reef, or barrier island.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.tr: v. 用薄片覆盖；压成薄片；
words.ex: They laminate the table with plastic to make it waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 他们用塑料薄片覆盖桌子，使其防水。
words.en: To laminate something means to cover it with a layer of plastic or another material for protection or to make it stronger.

words.ex: Greenland is the largest landmass in the world.
words.ex_cn: 格陵兰是世界上最大的陆地。
words.en: A landmass is a large area of land such as a continent that is in one piece and not broken up by oceans.

words.ex: The landowner rented his fields to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 地主把他的田地租给了农民。
words.en: A landowner is a person who owns land, especially a large amount of land.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.ex: He picked up a lapful of leaves.
words.ex_cn: 他捡了一满膝的树叶。
words.en: The amount that can be held in the lap.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr: n. 肥皂泡; 紧张; 激动; （马的）汗沫 vi. （指肥皂）形成泡沫 vt. 用皂沫覆盖; <口
words.ex: The horse was covered in lather after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，马全身都是汗沫。
words.en: Lather is a frothy white mass of bubbles produced by soap or a similar substance when mixed with water.

words.tr: adj. 充满泡沫的；肥皂泡的
words.ex: The sweat on his skin was lathery.
words.ex_cn: 他皮肤上的汗水黏腻。
words.en: Covered with or resembling lather; frothy.

words.tr:
n. 拉美人；拉丁美洲裔
adj. 拉美的；拉丁美洲裔的
words.ex: He is a latino boy who loves soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢足球的拉丁裔男孩。
words.en: A Latino is a man or boy who was born in or is a citizen of a country in Latin America, or a man or boy in the U.S. whose family is originally from Latin America.

words.tr: n. （Latvia）拉脱维亚; n. （Latvia）（俄、泰、加、印、美）劳特维艾（人名）
words.ex: He is from Latvia.
words.ex_cn: 他来自拉脱维亚。
words.en: Latvia is a country in Northern Europe, located in the Baltic region. It is bordered by Estonia, Russia, Belarus, and Lithuania. The capital and largest city is Riga.

words.tr: adj. 赞美的；赞赏的；称赞的
words.ex: The teacher gave a laudatory remark about his effort.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的努力给予了赞扬的评价。
words.en: If something is laudatory, it expresses praise.

words.ex: The elevation of his skills helped him get a better job.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的提升帮助他找到了一份更好的工作。
words.en: The height to which something is elevated or to which it rises.

words.ex: The slave worked in the fields every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个奴隶每天在田地里劳作。
words.en: A slave is someone who is the legal property of another person and is forced to obey them.

words.tr: adv. 浪费地；丰富地；大方地
words.ex: He lavishly spent money on fancy clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他浪费地花钱买昂贵的衣服。
words.en: In a way that is very generous or extravagant.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 法律许可的；守法的；合法的
words.ex: He did a lawful job to help the community.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一份合法的工作来帮助社区。
words.en: If something is lawful, it is allowed by the law.

words.ex: They drove lawlessly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 他们无拘无束地开车穿过城镇。
words.en: In a manner that is without law or control; in a way that disregards laws or rules.

words.ex: The lawmaker wrote a new bill for schools.
words.ex_cn: 这位立法者为学校写了一项新法案。
words.en: A lawmaker is a person who makes laws; a legislator.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.ex: Lawrence is walking to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 劳伦斯每天早上步行去学校。
words.en: A male given name, also the name of a city in Massachusetts, USA, and a famous poet (T.S. Eliot).

words.ex: The laxity in the company's safety regulations led to several accidents.
words.ex_cn: 公司安全规定的松驰导致了几次事故。
words.en: Laxity refers to the quality or state of being lax, which means not strict, severe, or careful enough.

words.ex: He walks through the lea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都穿过这片草地。
words.en: A lea is an open area of grassy or arable land.

words.ex: He handed out a leaflet about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一份关于该活动的传单。
words.en: A leaflet is a small sheet of printed paper that gives you information or advertises something.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.tr: n. 牵狗的链子或皮带；控制；约束
words.ex: He holds the dog's leash tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握着狗的牵引绳。
words.en: A leash is a rope or a strap that you attach to a dog's collar so that you can control the dog.

words.ex: The cat sat on the ledge of the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在窗户的架状突出物上。
words.en: A ledge is a narrow horizontal surface projecting from a wall, cliff, or other surface.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: She wears black legging to the gym.
words.ex_cn: 她穿黑色紧身裤去健身房。
words.en: Leggings are tight-fitting stretch pants, typically worn by women or girls.

words.tr: n. 易读性；易辨认；易理解；
words.ex: The legibility of the sign is important for drivers.
words.ex_cn: 标志的易读性对司机来说很重要。
words.en: The quality of being clear enough to read.

words.ex: There are legion stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A legion is a large group of soldiers who form a section of an army, especially in ancient Rome. It can also refer to a large number of people or things.

words.ex: The handwriting is legible and easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 字迹清晰，容易辨认。
words.en: If writing or print is legible, it is clear enough to read.

words.tr: adj. 很长的；漫长的；冗长的；
words.ex: The meeting was lengthy and tiring.
words.ex_cn: 会议很长，很累人。
words.en: Something that is lengthy lasts for a long time, often longer than you want or expect.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: n. 列宁（Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov的姓氏，苏联共产党的创始人之一）
words.ex: Lenin led the Russian Revolution in 1917.
words.ex_cn: 列宁在1917年领导了俄国革命。
words.en: Lenin was a Russian revolutionary, politician, and political theorist. He served as head of government of Soviet Russia from 1917 to 1924 and of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1924.

words.tr:
n. 女同性恋者
adj. 女同性恋的
words.ex: She is a lesbian and loves her partner.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名女同性恋者，深爱着她的伴侣。
words.en: A lesbian is a woman who is sexually attracted to other women.

words.ex: Try to lessen your sugar intake.
words.ex_cn: 试着减少你的糖摄入量。
words.en: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.ex: There was no letup in the rain all day.
words.ex_cn: 一整天雨都没有停。
words.en: A letup is a pause or reduction in the intensity of something, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 杠杆；杠杆作用；影响力
v. 举债经营；充分利用
words.ex: The mechanic used a lever to lift the car.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用杠杆来抬起汽车。
words.en: Leverage refers to the use of a lever or the mechanical advantage gained by using a lever. In finance, it refers to the use of borrowed capital to increase the potential return of an investment.

words.tr: n. 庞然大物；海中怪兽
words.ex: The leviathan moved slowly through the deep ocean.
words.ex_cn: 那只海中怪兽在深海中缓慢移动。
words.en: A leviathan is something that is extremely large and powerful, often used to describe a very large sea creature or a huge organization.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.ex: The movie was banned for its lewd content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因内容猥亵而被禁播。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as lewd, you are critical of it because it is sexual in a rude and unpleasant way.

words.ex: The movie was banned for its lewdness.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因内容淫秽被禁。
words.en: Lewdness refers to behavior that is sexual in a rude or offensive way.

words.ex: He is the liaison between the two departments.
words.ex_cn: 他是两个部门之间的联络人。
words.en: A liaison is a person who acts as a link to assist communication between different groups or organizations.

words.tr: adv. 大量地；思想开明地
words.ex: He liberally adds salt to his food.
words.ex_cn: 他很慷慨地往食物里加盐。
words.en: In a way that is generous or plentiful; not strictly.

words.ex: The liberation of the city ended the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的解放结束了战争。
words.en: Liberation refers to the act of setting someone free from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression; release.

words.tr:
adj. 自由论者的；自由意志论者的
n. 自由论者
words.ex: He is a libertarian who believes in small government.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个主张小政府的自由论者。
words.en: A libertarian is someone who believes in the doctrine of free will, or in the principle that people should have complete freedom of thought and action.

words.ex: Alice is walking to school with her friend.
words.ex_cn: 爱丽丝正和她的朋友一起去学校。
words.en: A female given name.

words.ex: He needs licensure to practice medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他需要执照才能行医。
words.en: The granting of a license, especially to carry out a trade or profession.

words.tr:
v. 点击；
n. 咔哒声；
words.ex: Click the button to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 点击按钮开始游戏。
words.en: To make a short, sharp sound, or to press a button on a computer mouse or other device to select something on a screen.

words.ex: He put the lid on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他把盖子盖在盒子上。
words.en: A lid is a cover for a container, or the movable cover of the eye, known as the eyelid.

words.tr: adj. 有盖子的，盖着盖子的，覆盖着的
words.ex: The pot has a lidded top to keep the soup warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个锅有盖子，可以保持汤的温度。
words.en: Having a lid or lids; covered with a lid.

words.tr: adj. 无盖的；注视的；无眼睑的
words.ex: The lidless eye of the camera never blinked.
words.ex_cn: 摄像机的无眼睑之眼从未眨动。
words.en: Without a lid or eyelids; open or exposed.

words.ex: The doll has a lifelike face.
words.ex_cn: 这个玩具有一个逼真的脸。
words.en: If something is lifelike, it is very similar to the thing it represents or imitates, especially in a way that is surprising or impressive.

words.ex: The statue has great lifelikeness.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像非常逼真。
words.en: The quality of resembling life or a living being, especially in art or sculpture.

words.ex: He has a lifelong love for reading.
words.ex_cn: 他对阅读有着终身的热爱。
words.en: Lasting or continuing through all or much of one's life.

words.tr: n. 毕生的事业；一生的工作
words.ex: Writing novels is his lifework.
words.ex_cn: 写小说是他的毕生事业。
words.en: The main work or task that someone does throughout their life.

words.ex: The boxer is a lightweight fighter.
words.ex_cn: 这位拳击手是一名轻量级选手。
words.en: Something that is lightweight weighs less than average or is less heavy than usual. It can also refer to someone who is not very important or influential.

words.ex: Farmers spread lime on the soil to make it less acidic.
words.ex_cn: 农民在土壤上撒石灰以降低其酸性。
words.en: Lime is a white substance obtained by heating limestone, used in making cement and in farming to improve soil. It is also a small green fruit that is similar to a lemon.

words.ex: The limner painted small portraits for the king.
words.ex_cn: 这位画师为国王画了小型肖像。
words.en: A limner is someone who paints or draws, especially in a detailed or meticulous manner.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.ex: He traced his lineage back to ancient kings.
words.ex_cn: 他追溯了自己的家系到古代的国王。
words.en: Your lineage is the series of families from which you are directly descended.

words.ex: The graph shows a linear relationship between time and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这张图显示了时间与距离之间的线性关系。
words.en: Linear means involving or relating to a straight line or lines.

words.ex: The lingam is a symbol in Hindu worship.
words.ex_cn: 林伽是印度教崇拜中的一个象征。
words.en: A lingam is a representation of the Hindu deity Shiva used for worship in temples.

words.ex: He found a lint on his black jacket.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的黑色夹克上发现了一根绒毛。
words.en: Lint is small fibers or fluffs of cotton or wool that come off clothes or other materials.

words.tr: adj. 有棉毛的，有棉絮的
words.ex: The dog has linty fur after rolling in the laundry.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗在滚过洗衣堆后，毛上有绒毛。
words.en: Covered with or full of lint.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.ex: He bought a bottle of liquor for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对买了一瓶酒。
words.en: Liquor is an alcoholic drink that is made by distillation rather than by fermentation.

words.tr: n. （意大利和土耳其的货币单位）里拉
words.ex: He paid for the bread with lira.
words.ex_cn: 他用里拉支付了面包的钱。
words.en: The lira was the monetary unit of Italy, Turkey, and other countries, replaced in Italy by the euro in 2002.

words.tr: n. 连祷文；枯燥冗长的陈述
words.ex: The meeting was filled with a litany of complaints.
words.ex_cn: 会议充斥着冗长的抱怨。
words.en: A litany is a form of prayer in which a series of petitions are recited by a leader with responses from the congregation. It can also refer to any long, tedious account or recital.

words.ex: He is literate and can read simple books.
words.ex_cn: 他有读写能力，能读简单的书。
words.en: A literate person is able to read and write, and has a good education.

words.ex: He bought one liter of milk.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一升牛奶。
words.en: A liter is a metric unit of capacity, equal to one cubic decimeter.

words.ex: He is facing litigation over the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他因合同问题面临诉讼。
words.en: Litigation is the process of taking legal action or bringing a lawsuit in a court of law.

words.tr:
v. 生活；居住；活着；
adj. 活的；现场的；实况转播的；
words.ex: They live in a small house near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在公园附近的一所小房子里。
words.en: To live means to be alive, to have your home in a particular place, or to spend your life in a particular way.

words.ex: He eats too much sugar and his liver is hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖，他的肝脏受损了。
words.en: The liver is a large organ in the body that cleans the blood and produces bile, or a person who lives in a particular way.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.ex: The film was shot on location in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是在一个小镇上实地拍摄的。
words.en: A locale is a place where something happens or is set, or that has particular events associated with it.

words.tr: adj. 可以定位的；可使地方化的；可以限制于局部的
words.ex: The app is localizable for different languages.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序可以本地化为多种语言。
words.en: Capable of being adapted or modified to meet the language, cultural, and other requirements of a specific locale or market.

words.ex: The localization of the disease is a key factor in treatment.
words.ex_cn: 疾病的定位是治疗的关键因素。
words.en: The process of adapting a product or content to a specific locale or market.

words.tr: v. 使限制于局部；定位
words.ex: The virus can localize in the lungs.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以限制在肺部。
words.en: To localize something means to adapt it to a particular area or market, often by translating it into the local language or modifying it to suit local customs and preferences.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: They stayed in a small lodge near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小屋里。
