words.en: Obsolescence is the state of being which occurs when an object, service, or practice is no longer wanted even though it may still be in good working order.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: His obtuseness in social situations often led to misunderstandings.
words.ex_cn: 他在社交场合的迟钝经常导致误解。
words.en: The quality or state of being obtuse; lack of sharpness or quickness in perception or understanding.

words.ex: The occupancy of the hotel is high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天酒店的占用率很高。
words.en: The act of occupying or the state of being occupied, especially the condition of being occupied by tenants or the period during which a property is occupied.

words.tr: n. 占有者; 居住人; 占用者
words.ex: The occupier of the apartment was not at home during the inspection.
words.ex_cn: 公寓的居住者在接受检查时不在家。
words.en: An occupier is a person or organization that occupies a particular place or position.

words.ex: The old man is an oddity in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是村里的怪人。
words.en: An oddity is someone or something that is strange or unusual.

words.ex: The rotten food has a bad odor.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odor is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.ex: He went on an odyssey to find his lost brother.
words.ex_cn: 他踏上了一段寻找失散兄弟的漫长旅程。
words.en: An odyssey is a long and eventful or adventurous journey or experience.

words.tr: n. 边角料; （木材等的）斜料，纸边
words.ex: The carpenter used the offcuts to make small decorative items.
words.ex_cn: 木匠用边角料制作了小装饰品。
words.en: An offcut is a piece of material that is left over after the main pieces have been cut off.

words.ex: The officeholder was praised for his dedication and efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 这位公务员因他的奉献精神和效率而受到表扬。
words.en: An officeholder is a person who holds a public office.

words.ex: The ontology of the system is well-defined.
words.ex_cn: 系统的本体论定义得很好。
words.en: Ontology is a branch of metaphysics dealing with the nature of being.

words.tr: n. 全能，万能，无限威力
words.ex: The concept of omnipotence is often associated with deities.
words.ex_cn: 全能的概念通常与神祇联系在一起。
words.en: The state or quality of being all-powerful or having unlimited power.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.ex: The concept of omniscience is often attributed to deities.
words.ex_cn: 全知的概念常常被归因于神灵。
words.en: The state of knowing everything.

words.ex: The onlooker watched the accident quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地看着这起事故。
words.en: A person who watches something happening without taking part in it.

words.tr:
adj. 舞台上的；台上演出的
adv. 在舞台上
words.ex: The actor looked nervous onstage.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在舞台上显得很紧张。
words.en: When someone is onstage, they are performing or speaking in front of an audience in a theatre or concert hall.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: The onus is on you to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 完成这个项目是你的职责。
words.en: The responsibility for something, especially a duty or task.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: His openness helped the team trust him.
words.ex_cn: 他的开放态度让团队信任他。
words.en: The quality or state of being open, especially in terms of being honest and not hiding one's thoughts or feelings.

words.ex: The operational system runs smoothly every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个运作系统每天运行顺畅。
words.en: If a system or service is operational, it is working or able to be used.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.ex: The rain stopped just opportunely for the outdoor wedding.
words.ex_cn: 雨恰好在外面的婚礼开始时停了。
words.en: At an opportune time; timely.

words.tr: n. 压迫；压制；抑制；镇压
words.ex: The people suffered under oppression for years.
words.ex_cn: 人们多年来一直遭受压迫。
words.en: Oppression is the cruel or unfair treatment of a group of people.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；沉重的；难以忍受的；闷热的
words.ex: The oppressive heat made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人窒息的炎热让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people in an unfair and cruel way and prevent them from having opportunities and freedom.

words.ex: The dictator was seen as an oppressor by the people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者被人民视为压迫者。
words.en: An oppressor is a person or group that oppresses people, treating them in a cruel and unfair way.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: He smiled optimistically about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他乐观地微笑着面对未来。
words.en: In an optimistic manner; with optimism.

words.tr: n. 编号作品；乐曲；艺术作品
words.ex: The composer's latest opus has received critical acclaim.
words.ex_cn: 这位作曲家的最新作品获得了评论界的好评。
words.en: An opus is a creative work, especially a musical composition or set of compositions numbered in order of publication.

words.ex: The priest was known as an oracle who spoke for the gods.
words.ex_cn: 这位祭司被称为传达神谕的传神谕者。
words.en: An oracle is a person or thing considered to provide wise and insightful guidance or prophetic predictions, often through divine inspiration.

words.ex: He answered the questions orally.
words.ex_cn: 他口头回答了问题。
words.en: In a spoken rather than written form; by means of speech.

words.ex: The orangutan sits quietly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 猩猩静静地坐在树上。
words.en: A large ape with long reddish hair, found in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.tr: n. 轨道飞行器；航天飞行器；
words.ex: The orbiter circled the planet for months.
words.ex_cn: 轨道飞行器在行星周围环绕了数月。
words.en: An orbiter is a spacecraft designed to go into orbit, especially one that does not also land on a planet or moon.

words.ex: He walks in the orchard every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在果园里散步。
words.en: An orchard is an area of land where fruit trees are grown.

words.tr: v. 改编为管弦乐；策划；精心安排
words.ex: He orchestrated the folk song for a symphony orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他将这首民歌改编为管弦乐。
words.en: To orchestrate something means to organize or arrange it in a very detailed and carefully planned way, especially in order to achieve a particular effect or result.

words.tr: n. 管弦乐编曲，管弦乐作曲法
words.ex: The orchestration of the symphony was praised for its complexity and beauty.
words.ex_cn: 这首交响乐的管弦乐编曲因其复杂性和美感而受到赞扬。
words.en: The arrangement or coordination of elements in a complex situation or activity to produce a desired effect, especially in music or business.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

words.ex: She bought a pink orchid for her mother.
words.ex_cn: 她为母亲买了一朵粉色的兰花。
words.en: A plant with complex flowers that are often brightly coloured, grown especially for its beautiful flowers.

words.ex: The point has an ordinate of 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个点的纵坐标是5。
words.en: In mathematics, an ordinate is the y-coordinate of a point in a two-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system.

words.tr: n. 俄勒冈州（美国州名）
words.ex: He lives in Oregon near the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在俄勒冈州，靠近山区。
words.en: Oregon is a state in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States. It is known for its diverse landscape of forests, mountains, farms, and beaches.

words.ex: The miners dug deep to find iron ore.
words.ex_cn: 矿工们深入地下寻找铁矿石。
words.en: Ore is rock or earth from which metal can be obtained.

words.ex: The organizational structure is clear and simple.
words.ex_cn: 组织结构清晰而简单。
words.en: Relating to the way in which the different parts of something are arranged or organized.

words.ex: He is the organizer of the school fair.
words.ex_cn: 他是学校集市的组织者。
words.en: An organizer is a person who arranges or plans an event or activity.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.tr: n. 创作者；发起人；创始人
words.ex: He is the originator of this idea.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个想法的提出者。
words.en: The person who creates or starts something, especially a new idea or way of doing something.

words.ex: The garden has ornamental flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有装饰性的花卉。
words.en: Something that is ornamental is intended to be attractive and is not necessary or useful.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.ex: The boy lives in an orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩住在孤儿院。
words.en: An orphanage is a place where children who have lost their parents or who have been abandoned by them are cared for and live.

words.tr: n. 奥森（男子名，相当于中文的‘奥尔森’）
words.ex: Orson Welles was a famous American actor and filmmaker.
words.ex_cn: 奥森·威尔斯是一位著名的美国演员和电影制片人。
words.en: A given name, notably associated with Orson Welles, the American actor and filmmaker.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.ex: The pendulum shows a smooth oscillation.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆表现出平稳的振荡。
words.en: Oscillation is the process of moving back and forth or up and down in a regular rhythm.

words.ex: He wore gold chains as a show of ostentation.
words.ex_cn: 他戴金链子是为了炫耀。
words.en: Ostentation is the act of showing off your wealth, possessions, or abilities in a way that is meant to impress others.

words.tr: adv. 铺张地，招摇地，炫耀地
words.ex: She dressed ostentatiously for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为聚会盛装打扮。
words.en: In a way that is characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress or attract notice.

words.ex: Osteoarthritis is a common joint disorder that primarily affects cartilage.
words.ex_cn: 骨关节炎是一种常见的关节疾病，主要影响软骨。
words.en: A type of arthritis that occurs when flexible tissue at the ends of bones wears down.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr: vt. 盯得…局促不安，睥睨
words.ex: She tried to outface her opponent in the debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在辩论中试图让对手局促不安。
words.en: To confront someone or something boldly and without fear.

words.ex: She bought a new outfit for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一套新衣服。
words.en: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose.

words.tr: vt. 武器多于; 火力压过; 在武器上超过
words.ex: The rebels were outgunned by the government forces.
words.ex_cn: 叛军在武器装备上被政府军压倒。
words.en: To surpass in firepower or capability.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.tr: n. 被宣布为非法；非法化；逍遥法外
words.ex: The practice of slavery was once considered lawful, but eventually faced outlawry.
words.ex_cn: 奴隶制的做法曾经被认为是合法的，但最终被宣布为非法。
words.en: The state of being an outlaw; the process of outlawing someone or something.

words.ex: The dogs outnumber the cats in this neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区里的狗比猫多。
words.en: If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.

words.ex: The new car can outpace the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车能超过旧车。
words.en: To outpace someone or something means to perform a particular action faster or better than they do.

words.ex: The soldiers stayed at the remote outpost.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们驻守在偏远的前哨站。
words.en: An outpost is a small military camp or position at some distance from the main army, used especially as a guard against surprise attack.

words.tr: n. 流出物；流出; vt. 流出; vi. 流出
words.ex: There was an outpour of love after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，爱如潮水般涌来。
words.en: An outpour is a large amount of something that is produced or released suddenly and in large quantities.

words.tr: adj. 极无礼的；粗暴的；骇人的；
words.ex: His outrageous behavior made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他极无礼的行为让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as outrageous, you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable because it is extremely bad, immoral, or shocking.

words.ex: He outranks his boss in the military.
words.ex_cn: 他在军队中的军衔比他的老板高。
words.en: If one person outranks another, they have a higher position or rank than the other person.

words.ex: He can outshine others with his bright ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他能用他出色的想法胜过别人。
words.en: If you outshine someone, you are much better at doing something than they are.

words.tr:
adj. 特大的；超大号的
n. 特大号
words.ex: The box is outsize for the truck.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子对卡车来说太大了。
words.en: An outsize object is much larger than usual or much larger than you would expect.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.ex: The company decided to outsource its customer service.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司决定将客户服务外购。
words.en: If a company outsources work or things, it pays workers from outside the company to do the work or supply the things.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.tr: n. 过多；过剩；过于丰富
words.ex: The overabundance of sugar in the diet can lead to health problems.
words.ex_cn: 饮食中糖分过多会导致健康问题。
words.en: An overabundance of something is a larger amount of it than is needed, wanted, or can be dealt with.

words.ex: The table has an oval shape.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是椭圆形的。
words.en: An oval is a shape that is like a circle but is longer in one direction than the other.

words.tr:
v. 对…要价（或收费）过高；装填过量
n. 要价过高；装填过量
words.ex: The shop overcharged me for the water bottle.
words.ex_cn: 商店多收了我买水瓶的钱。
words.en: If someone overcharges you, they charge you too much money for goods or a service.

words.ex: He tends to overcompensate for his shyness by talking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他往往通过说太多话来过度补偿自己的害羞。
words.en: To compensate excessively, often in an attempt to make up for a perceived deficiency or mistake.

words.tr: n. 过度补偿; 过补偿
words.ex: He exhibited overcompensation by working excessively hard to prove himself.
words.ex_cn: 他通过过度努力工作来证明自己，表现出过度补偿。
words.en: Overcompensation refers to the act of compensating excessively, especially in psychology, where it denotes an attempt to overcome a perceived weakness by exaggerating in another area.

words.tr:
n. 服药过量；嗑药过量；过量
v. （使）服药过量；过量…
words.ex: He took an overdose of pills and went to hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他服用了过量的药片，被送到了医院。
words.en: An overdose is the taking of too much of a drug, which can cause serious harm or death.

words.ex: The book is overdue at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆逾期了。
words.en: If you say that a change or an event is overdue, you mean that you think it should have happened before now.

words.tr: v. 暴食；吃得过量；吃撑
words.ex: He overate at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上吃太多了。
words.en: To eat more food than your body needs, especially so that you feel uncomfortably full.

words.ex: He went overdrawn on his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他的银行账户透支了。
words.en: An overdraft occurs when money is withdrawn from a bank account and the available balance goes below zero.

words.tr: v. 过分强调；过分着重
words.ex: He overemphasizes grades too much.
words.ex_cn: 他过于强调成绩。
words.en: To give too much emphasis to something; to stress something more than is necessary or appropriate.

words.ex: He overestimated his ability to finish the task in one day.
words.ex_cn: 他过高估计了自己一天内完成任务的能力。
words.en: If you overestimate something, you think it is greater in amount or more important than it really is.

words.tr: vt. 使过于激动（或兴奋），过度刺激
words.ex: The loud music overexcited the baby.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让婴儿过于兴奋。
words.en: To excite someone or something excessively, often leading to a state of heightened agitation or enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. （对资源等的）过度开采，（对工人等的）过度剥削
words.ex: The overexploitation of natural resources has led to environmental degradation.
words.ex_cn: 自然资源的过度开采导致了环境退化。
words.en: The excessive use of natural resources beyond their capacity to regenerate, leading to environmental degradation and loss of biodiversity.

words.tr: v. 过分扩展；过分扩张
words.ex: He overextends himself by working too many hours.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作时间太长而把自己累垮了。
words.en: To overextend means to make something too long or to make someone do too much work.

words.ex: They overfish the sea every year.
words.ex_cn: 他们每年过度捕捞海洋。
words.en: To deplete the stock of fish in a body of water by excessive fishing.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.ex: The news overjoyed her.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让她欣喜若狂。
words.en: To make someone extremely happy or delighted.

words.ex: He is overly careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱过于谨慎。
words.en: To an excessive degree.

words.ex: The car drove under the overpass.
words.ex_cn: 汽车从立交桥下开过。
words.en: An overpass is a bridge that carries one road or railway line over another.

words.ex: He overprotects his little sister by not letting her go outside alone.
words.ex_cn: 他不让她独自外出，对她太过保护。
words.en: To protect someone, especially a child, too much so that they do not learn to do things for themselves.

words.ex: The project cost overrun the budget.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的成本超过了预算。
words.en: If an army or a group of people overruns a place, they take control of it by force. If something such as a place or a piece of land is overrun by things or people, it is filled with them and they spread everywhere.

words.tr: v. 反应过火；反应过度
words.ex: He overreacts when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到坏消息时，他会反应过度。
words.en: If someone overreacts to something, they have and show more of an emotion than is necessary or appropriate.

words.tr: vt. 使有过多的代表，使代表人数超出比例
words.ex: The survey overrepresented the views of the older generation.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查过多地反映了老一代人的观点。
words.en: To represent in numbers that are disproportionately large compared to the actual population or the whole.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The judge will overrule the objection.
words.ex_cn: 法官将驳回这个异议。
words.en: If someone in authority overrules a decision or order, they officially decide that it is wrong and change it.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.ex: He tries to oversimplify the problem, but it is still hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他试图过分简化这个问题，但仍然很难理解。
words.en: If you say that someone oversimplifies something, you mean that they describe or explain it so simply that what they say is no longer true or reasonable.

words.ex: He will overtake the car ahead soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会超过前面的车。
words.en: If you overtake someone, you go past them because you are moving faster than they are.

words.tr: v. 课税过重；负担过度；使工作过度
words.ex: The high taxes overtax the poor families.
words.ex_cn: 高额税收压垮了贫困家庭。
words.en: To impose too much tax on someone or something, or to make excessive demands on someone's strength or resources.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.ex: He worked overtime to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他加班完成了这个项目。
words.en: Overtime refers to the time worked beyond one's regular working hours, often with additional pay.

words.ex: He overtly expressed his dislike for the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他公然表达了对新政策的不满。
words.en: In an open and observable way; not secretly or covertly.

words.ex: He overvalues his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他高估了自己的旧车。
words.en: To overvalue something is to estimate its value as being higher than it really is, or to consider it more important or better than it actually is.

words.ex: Too much homework can overweigh students.
words.ex_cn: 太多的作业会使学生负担过重。
words.en: To be heavier than; to consider or treat as more important than it really is.

words.tr:
n. 过度工作；过度劳累；滥用
v. 工作过度；劳累过度；对…使用过度
words.ex: He got sick from overwork.
words.ex_cn: 他因过度工作而生病了。
words.en: If you overwork or if someone overworks you, you work too hard, often to the point of exhaustion.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.

words.ex: The owl sleeps in the tree during the day.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰白天在树上睡觉。
words.en: An owl is a bird with a flat face, large eyes, and a small sharp beak. Most owls hunt at night.

words.ex: Rust is an oxide of iron.
words.ex_cn: 铁锈是铁的氧化物。
words.en: An oxide is a chemical compound that contains at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.

words.ex: The iron will oxidize in wet air.
words.ex_cn: 铁在潮湿的空气中会氧化。
words.en: To combine or become combined chemically with oxygen.

words.ex: Iron is easily oxidizable in the presence of moisture.
words.ex_cn: 铁在潮湿环境中容易氧化。
words.en: Capable of being oxidized.

words.tr: n. [化学] 氧化，氧化作用
words.ex: The process of oxidization can lead to rust formation.
words.ex_cn: 氧化过程会导致生锈。
words.en: The process of oxidizing; the addition of oxygen to a compound with a loss of electrons; always occurs accompanied by reduction.

words.ex: The ozone layer protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
words.ex_cn: 臭氧层保护我们免受太阳有害射线的伤害。
words.en: Ozone is a form of oxygen that has three atoms in each molecule, and it is a pale blue gas with a pungent smell. It is found in the Earth's atmosphere and absorbs ultraviolet radiation, which is harmful to living organisms.

words.ex: The two countries made a pact to stop fighting.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家达成了一项停止战斗的协议。
words.en: A pact is a formal agreement between two or more people, organizations, or governments to do a particular thing or to help each other.

words.ex: He filled the pail with water from the well.
words.ex_cn: 他从井里打了一桶水。
words.en: A pail is a bucket, usually made of metal or plastic, with a handle, used for carrying liquids or other substances.

words.ex: The cut on his finger is painful.
words.ex_cn: 他手指上的伤口很疼。
words.en: If something is painful, it causes you a lot of physical or emotional pain.

words.ex: He took a painkiller for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: A painkiller is a drug that reduces or removes physical pain.

words.tr: adj. 无痛苦的；不痛的；无需努力（工作）的
words.ex: The injection was painless.
words.ex_cn: 这次注射没有疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as painless, you mean that it is easy to do or causes you no trouble or suffering.

words.ex: He painstakingly checked every answer before submitting the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在提交试卷前极其仔细地检查了每一个答案。
words.en: With great care and thoroughness.

words.tr:
adj. 巴勒斯坦（人）的
n. 巴勒斯坦人
words.ex: The Palestinian conflict has been ongoing for decades.
words.ex_cn: 巴勒斯坦冲突已经持续了几十年。
words.en: Relating to Palestine or its people.

words.tr: adv. 可触之地; 易觉察地
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpably thick.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张气氛明显到可以触摸。
words.en: In a way that is easily perceived or obvious.

words.ex: He felt a palpitation after running fast.
words.ex_cn: 他快速跑步后感到心跳加速。
words.en: A palpitation is an unusually rapid, strong, or irregular heartbeat that you are aware of, often described as a fluttering or pounding sensation in the chest.

words.ex: Panama is known for its famous canal.
words.ex_cn: 巴拿马以其著名的运河而闻名。
words.en: Panama is a country in Central America, known for the Panama Canal, which connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

words.ex: He has pancreatic cancer.
words.ex_cn: 他患有胰腺癌。
words.en: Relating to the pancreas, a large gland behind the stomach that secretes digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

words.ex: The pancreas makes insulin to control blood sugar.
words.ex_cn: 胰腺分泌胰岛素来控制血糖。
words.en: The pancreas is a large gland behind the stomach which secretes digestive enzymes into the duodenum. Embedded in the pancreas are the islets of Langerhans, which secrete into the blood the hormones insulin and glucagon.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息
n. 气喘；喘息
words.ex: He panted after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: To breathe quickly and loudly through your mouth, usually because you have been doing something energetic.

words.ex: After running, he was panting heavily.
words.ex_cn: 跑步后，他气喘吁吁。
words.en: Breathing with short, quick breaths; out of breath.

words.tr: n. 食品贮藏室；食品贮藏柜
words.ex: She keeps cookies in the pantry.
words.ex_cn: 她把饼干放在食品储藏室里。
words.en: A pantry is a small room or closet in a house, usually near the kitchen, where food, dishes, linens, and provisions are stored.

words.ex: He wears pajamas to bed every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上穿睡衣睡觉。
words.en: Pajamas are loose-fitting clothes worn for sleeping, consisting of trousers and a jacket.

words.tr: adj. 宫殿般的；宏伟的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: He lives in a palatial house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边一座宏伟的房子里。
words.en: If you describe a building or a place as palatial, you mean that it is very large, impressive, or luxurious, like a palace.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.tr: n. 专家咨询组；嵌板；仪器板；
words.ex: The government formed a panel to advise on health policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府组建了一个专家咨询组来就卫生政策提供建议。
words.en: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

words.ex: He bought a paperback novel at the bookstore.
words.ex_cn: 他在书店买了一本平装小说。
words.en: A paperback is a book with a thin cardboard or paper cover, as opposed to a hardback, which has a hard cover.

words.ex: He picked up a paperclip from the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他从桌子上捡起一个回形针。
words.en: A paperclip is a small piece of bent wire or plastic used for holding sheets of paper together.

words.ex: He spent all day doing paperwork.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天都在处理文书工作。
words.en: Paperwork refers to the routine work involving written documents such as forms, reports, and letters, especially in an office setting.

words.ex: Ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人在纸莎草纸上写字。
words.en: Papyrus is a material similar to thick paper that was used in ancient times as a writing surface. It was made from the pith of the papyrus plant, Cyperus papyrus, a wetland sedge.

words.ex: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches compassion and kindness.
words.ex_cn: 好撒玛利亚人的寓言教导了同情和善良。
words.en: A simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, as told by Jesus in the Gospels.

words.tr:
n. 降落伞
v. 跳伞；用降落伞空投
words.ex: He jumped from the plane and opened his parachute.
words.ex_cn: 他从飞机上跳下并打开了降落伞。
words.en: A parachute is a device used to slow the motion of an object through an atmosphere by creating drag.

words.tr:
n. 游行；阅兵；
v. 游行；阅兵；
words.ex: The city held a big parade on Independence Day.
words.ex_cn: 城市在独立日举行了盛大的游行。
words.en: A parade is a procession of people or vehicles moving through a public place in order to celebrate an important day or event.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: n. 游行者，列队行进者
words.ex: The parade included a variety of colorful paraders.
words.ex_cn: 游行队伍中包括了各种色彩鲜艳的游行者。
words.en: A parader is someone who takes part in a parade or who shows off something in a way that attracts attention.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.ex: The parasitic worm lives inside the host.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主体内。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a parasite; living on or in another organism and deriving nutrients at the host's expense.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.tr: n. 削下的皮 v. 削皮( pare的现在分词 ); 削掉; 修剪（指甲等）; 逐步减小（数量或体
words.ex: She carefully collected the parings for compost.
words.ex_cn: 她小心地收集削下的皮用来堆肥。
words.en: The act of cutting off the outer layer of something, especially fruit or vegetables, to remove the skin or peel.

words.tr: n. 公园绿地；公用场地；
words.ex: The children play in the parkland after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在公园绿地里玩耍。
words.en: Parkland refers to land that is designated or used as a park, typically characterized by its green, open spaces and recreational facilities.

words.tr: adj. 小气的；吝啬的；太节省的
words.ex: His parsimonious nature made him unpopular among colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他吝啬的本性使得他在同事中不受欢迎。
words.en: Someone who is parsimonious is very unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adv. 吝啬地；极度俭省地
words.ex: He spent his money parsimoniously, never indulging in luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很吝啬，从不沉迷于奢侈品。
words.en: In a manner that is very unwilling to spend money or use resources.

words.tr: adj. 尚可的；可通行的；（钱币等）可流通的
words.ex: The road was passable but not in good condition.
words.ex_cn: 这条路尚可通行，但状况不佳。
words.en: If something is passable, it is good enough to be accepted or allowed, but not of a very high standard.

words.tr: adv. 尚可地，也还过得去地
words.ex: The food was passably good, but not exceptional.
words.ex_cn: 食物还算不错，但并不出众。
words.en: in a satisfactory or acceptable manner

words.tr: n. 银行存折；南非共和国有色人种的身份证
words.ex: He checked his passbook to see his savings.
words.ex_cn: 他查看了存折来看他的存款。
words.en: A passbook is a small book containing a record of the deposits, withdrawals, and interest of a bank account.

words.ex: He bought a warm pastry from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他从面包店买了一个热乎乎的点心。
words.en: Pastry is a food made from flour, fat, and water that is mixed together, rolled flat, and baked in an oven. It is used as a base or covering for pies, tarts, and other dishes.

words.ex: The cows graze in the pasture.
words.ex_cn: 牛在牧场上吃草。
words.en: Pasture is land covered with grass where animals such as cows and sheep can graze.

words.ex: The quilt is a patchwork of old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 这条被子是用旧衣服拼凑而成的。
words.en: Patchwork is a form of needlework that involves sewing together pieces of fabric into a larger design. The larger design is usually based on repeating patterns built up with different fabric shapes (which can be different colors).

words.tr: adj. 父亲的；父亲般的；父系的
words.ex: His paternal grandfather gave him a watch.
words.ex_cn: 他的父亲的父亲送给他一块表。
words.en: Paternal is used to describe feelings or actions which are typical of those of a kind father towards his child.

words.tr: adv. 父亲似地; 父亲一般地
words.ex: He treated the child paternally.
words.ex_cn: 他像父亲一样对待这个孩子。
words.en: In a manner that is characteristic of a father; fatherly.

words.ex: The dirt pathway led to the small house.
words.ex_cn: 这条土路通向那座小房子。
words.en: A pathway is a track that is made by or for people walking, especially one through a countryside or a park.

words.ex: The patriarch leads his large family with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 这位族长以智慧领导他的大家庭。
words.en: A patriarch is a man who is the head of a family or tribe, or a highly respected man in a particular field.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.tr: n. 赞助人；资助人；老主顾
words.ex: The patron gave money to support the art exhibition.
words.ex_cn: 赞助人捐钱支持了这场艺术展览。
words.en: A patron is a person who supports with money, gifts, efforts, or endorsement an artist, musician, writer, form of art, or charitable cause.

words.tr:
n. 回报；收益
adj. 偿付的；偿还的
words.ex: He got payback for the joke they played on him.
words.ex_cn: 他为他们开的玩笑报复了回来。
words.en: Payback refers to the act of repaying money that has been borrowed or the act of taking revenge on someone for something they have done.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.ex: He ate a ripe peach for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个熟透的桃子。
words.en: A peach is a soft, round, slightly furry fruit with sweet yellow flesh and pinky-orange skin. Peaches grow in warm countries.

words.ex: She ate a ripe pear for snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一个熟透的梨当零食。
words.en: A pear is a sweet, juicy fruit that is narrow at the top and wider at the bottom. It has a thin green or brown skin, and white flesh.

words.ex: She wore a white pearl necklace.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条白色的珍珠项链。
words.en: A pearl is a hard, rounded object formed within the shell of a pearl oyster or similar mollusk, highly prized as a gemstone.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.ex: Pedagogics is the science of teaching and education.
words.ex_cn: 教育学是关于教学和教育的科学。
words.en: Pedagogics refers to the science and art of teaching, encompassing the methods and practices of education.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.ex: He pressed the pedal to speed up the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下踏板让自行车加速。
words.en: A pedal is a lever that you press with your foot in order to control a vehicle or machine.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.tr:
n. 钉；支柱
v. 钉（木桩等）以固定；限定
words.ex: He hung the hat on a peg.
words.ex_cn: 他把帽子挂在了一个钉子上。
words.en: A peg is a small device, usually made of wood or metal, that is used to fasten things or to hang things on.

words.ex: The pendulum swings back and forth in the clock.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆在钟里来回摆动。
words.en: A pendulum is a weight that is hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely, especially a rod with a weight at the end that regulates the mechanism of a clock.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The penguin walks on the ice.
words.ex_cn: 企鹅在冰上行走。
words.en: A penguin is a type of bird that cannot fly, lives in the southern hemisphere, and swims very well.

words.ex: The peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个半岛三面环水。
words.en: A peninsula is a piece of land that is almost entirely surrounded by water but is connected to the mainland on one side.

words.ex: She added pepper to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她往汤里加了胡椒粉。
words.en: Pepper is a hot-tasting powder made from the crushed seeds of certain plants, used to flavor food.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉到的；看得出的；可感知的
words.ex: The change was barely perceptible.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化几乎无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is perceptible can be seen, noticed, or felt.

words.tr: n. 可感知（性）; 可感觉（性）; 可察觉（性）; 可辨（性）
words.ex: The perceptibility of the scent increased as we approached the garden.
words.ex_cn: 随着我们接近花园，气味的可感知性增强了。
words.en: The quality of being perceptible; the ability to be perceived by the senses.

words.tr: n. 香水；香水商店；香水的制造
words.ex: She works in a perfumery that makes luxury scents.
words.ex_cn: 她在一家制作高档香水的香水公司工作。
words.en: The art or business of making perfumes.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.ex: She bought fresh perishables at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了新鲜的易腐食品。
words.en: Perishables are goods, especially foodstuffs, that are liable to decay or spoil.

words.ex: Free lunch is a perk of this job.
words.ex_cn: 免费午餐是这份工作的一个额外补贴。
words.en: If someone perks up or if something perks them up, they become more cheerful or lively.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: The permeability of the soil is crucial for plant growth.
words.ex_cn: 土壤的渗透性对植物生长至关重要。
words.en: The ability of a substance to allow liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: The Permian period is known for its extensive coal deposits.
words.ex_cn: 二叠纪以其丰富的煤炭储量而闻名。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the last period of the Paleozoic era, between the Carboniferous and Triassic periods.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: His perseverance helped him finish the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他的毅力帮助他完成了马拉松。
words.en: Perseverance is the quality of continuing to try to achieve a particular aim despite difficulties.

words.ex: The ancient civilization of Persia is renowned for its rich history and culture.
words.ex_cn: 古波斯文明以其丰富的历史和文化而闻名。
words.en: An ancient empire located in what is now Iran, known for its rich history and culture.

words.tr: n. 人物角色；假面；人格面具；
words.ex: The actor played a new persona in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中扮演了一个新的角色。
words.en: The aspect of someone's character that is presented to or perceived by others.

words.tr: v. 使个人化；使（某事物）针对个人；个性化
words.ex: She can personalize her phone with a new wallpaper.
words.ex_cn: 她可以用新的壁纸来个性化她的手机。
words.en: To make something suitable for the needs of a particular person, often by changing or adding to it.

words.ex: The app offers personalization for each user.
words.ex_cn: 该应用为每位用户提供人性化设置。
words.en: The process of making or modifying something so that it is suited to a particular individual or task.

words.tr: adv. 口才好地；令人信服地
words.ex: He argued persuasively for the adoption of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他令人信服地为新政策的采纳进行了辩论。
words.en: In a way that is convincing or able to persuade.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.ex: She answered the teacher's question pertly.
words.ex_cn: 她冒失地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: In a manner that is boldly forward or brash; impudently.

words.ex: The pertinence of her comments was undeniable.
words.ex_cn: 她评论的针对性是无可否认的。
words.en: The quality of being relevant or applicable to a particular matter.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: Her pertness irritated the interviewer.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢惹恼了面试官。
words.en: Pertness is the quality of being pert, which means being inappropriately forward or bold.

words.tr: n. 轻微扰动；摄动；不安；忧虑
words.ex: The small perturbation changed the system's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 这个小的扰动改变了系统的运行状态。
words.en: A perturbation is a small change in the regular movement or state of something, especially one that is caused by an outside influence.

words.ex: The pervasiveness of social media has changed the way we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 社交媒体的无处不在改变了我们的沟通方式。
words.en: The quality of being present or noticeable in every part of a thing or place.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.

words.tr: n. 任性; 乖僻; 刚愎; 倔强
words.ex: His perversity made him refuse the gift just because he wanted to be different.
words.ex_cn: 他的任性让他拒绝了礼物，只是因为他想与众不同。
words.en: The quality or state of being perverse; a deliberate desire to behave in an unreasonable or unacceptable way; contrariness.

words.tr: n. 颠倒；歪曲；堕落；性欲倒错；（性）变态
words.ex: The perversion of justice led to widespread public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 司法的颠倒导致了公众的广泛愤怒。
words.en: A perversion of something is a change to it that makes it unnatural, wrong, or unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 比索（一种外国货币单位）
words.ex: The exchange rate for the peso has dropped significantly.
words.ex_cn: 比索的汇率已经大幅下降。
words.en: The peso is the unit of money used in several Latin American countries, including Mexico, Argentina, and the Philippines.

words.ex: The farmer tried to kill the pest with a spray.
words.ex_cn: 农民试图用喷雾杀死害虫。
words.en: A pest is an animal or insect that damages crops, food, or livestock, or is generally troublesome. It can also refer to a person or thing that causes annoyance or trouble.

words.ex: The students handed in a petition to the principal.
words.ex_cn: 学生们向校长递交了一份请愿书。
words.en: A petition is a document signed by a lot of people which asks a government or other official group to do a particular thing.

words.tr:
n. 石油化学制品
adj. 石化的
words.ex: The factory makes petrochemicals from oil.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂从石油中生产石油化工产品。
words.en: A petrochemical is a chemical obtained from petroleum and natural gas.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.tr:
adj. 制药的；配药的；
n. 药物；
words.ex: He works at a pharmaceutical company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家制药公司工作。
words.en: relating to the production and sale of medicinal drugs

words.ex: The phantom appeared in the mist near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幻影出现在老房子附近的薄雾中。
words.en: A phantom is a ghost or a figment of the imagination.

words.ex: The drug has strong pharmacological effects.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有很强的药理作用。
words.en: Relating to pharmacology, the branch of medicine concerned with the uses, effects, and modes of action of drugs.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.tr: n. 慈善；博爱；慈善事业
words.ex: He gives money to charity because of his philanthropy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为慈善精神而捐钱给慈善机构。
words.en: Philanthropy is the act of donating money, goods, time, or effort to support a charitable cause, usually over an extended period of time and in regard to a defined objective.

words.tr: vi. 进行哲学探讨，理性地思考; vt. 使哲学化；像哲学家般思考或辩论
words.ex: He likes to philosophize about life and death.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢谈论生与死的哲学。
words.en: To philosophize means to think or reason like a philosopher, or to discuss or explain the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence.

words.ex: The philosophizer pondered deeply about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 这位哲理家深思生命的意义。
words.en: A philosophizer is someone who engages in the study or discussion of philosophy, often in a superficial or impractical manner.

words.ex: The plant needs phosphate to grow well.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要磷酸盐才能良好生长。
words.en: A phosphate is a salt or ester of phosphoric acid, containing the anion PO₄³⁻ or the group —PO₄.

words.ex: The photoconductive material changes its electrical resistance when exposed to light.
words.ex_cn: 这种光电导材料在暴露于光线时会改变其电阻。
words.en: A material is photoconductive if its electrical conductivity increases when it is exposed to light.

words.tr: n. 钢琴家；钢琴弹奏者；
words.ex: The pianist played a beautiful song at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这位钢琴家在音乐会上演奏了一首美妙的曲子。
words.en: A pianist is a person who plays the piano, especially professionally.

words.tr:
n. 尖木桩；警戒哨；纠察队（队员）
v. 进行罢工纠察
words.ex: The fence has wooden pickets to keep animals out.
words.ex_cn: 这个围栏有木制尖木桩，用来防止动物进入。
words.en: A picket is a person or group of people who stand outside a place of work or other venue to protest or to try to persuade others not to enter during a strike. It can also refer to a pointed stake or post driven into the ground, typically to form a fence or to tether a horse.

words.ex: The picketer stood outside the building, holding a sign.
words.ex_cn: 纠察员站在大楼外，举着标语牌。
words.en: A picketer is a person who participates in a picket, especially as a form of protest or to prevent workers from entering a place of work during a strike.

words.tr:
n. 泡菜；腌菜；腌汁；腌制品；困境
v. 腌制（泡菜等）
words.ex: He put a pickle on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上放了一颗酸黄瓜。
words.en: A pickle is a vegetable or fruit that has been preserved in vinegar or salt water, or a difficult situation.

words.ex: The pickup is at 7 PM outside the hotel.
words.ex_cn: 接人时间是晚上7点，在酒店外面。
words.en: A pickup is an improvement or recovery, especially in business or health. It can also refer to the act of collecting someone or something, or a small truck with an open back.

words.tr:
adj. 有图画的；图示的
n. 画报
words.ex: The book has a pictorial guide to plants.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一本植物的图解指南。
words.en: A pictorial representation or image is one that is made using pictures or shows things in a way that pictures do.

words.ex: The fisherman walked to the pier to check his nets.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫走到码头去检查他的渔网。
words.en: A pier is a platform sticking out into water, usually the sea, which people walk along or use when getting onto or off boats.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.tr: n. 背着，肩驮，背负式运输 vt. 背负式装运 adj. 背着的；[航] 在背肩上的 adv. 在
words.ex: He piggybacked his younger sister across the stream.
words.ex_cn: 他背着妹妹过了小溪。
words.en: To carry someone on the back and shoulders; to use something that already exists, such as a system or an idea, in order to do something new or to make progress.

words.tr: n. 女孩垂在头两侧编或不编成辫子的长发，发辫，辫子
words.ex: The girl has two pigtails on her head.
words.ex_cn: 这个女孩头上扎着两条辫子。
words.en: A pigtail is a length of hair that is tied together at the back of the head or at each side of the head so that it hangs down like a tail.

words.ex: She wore a pigtailed hairstyle to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她梳着辫子去参加聚会。
words.en: Having hair that is divided into two sections and tied at the back of the head, resembling a pig's tail.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.ex: The pillager ransacked the village, taking everything of value.
words.ex_cn: 掠夺者洗劫了村庄，拿走了所有有价值的东西。
words.en: A pillager is someone who steals things by force, especially in a time of war or unrest.

words.ex: He put his head on the pillow and fell asleep.
words.ex_cn: 他把头放在枕头上，睡着了。
words.en: A pillow is a cushion that you rest your head on when you are in bed.

words.ex: The GPS can pinpoint your exact location.
words.ex_cn: GPS可以精准定位你的准确位置。
words.en: To pinpoint something means to locate or identify it precisely.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.tr: n. 海盗行为；侵犯版权；
words.ex: The ship was attacked because of piracy near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 船在海岸附近因海盗行为遭到袭击。
words.en: The act of illegally copying and selling someone else's work, especially books, videos, or computer programs, or the act of attacking and stealing from ships at sea.

words.ex: The pirate sailed the sea with a black flag.
words.ex_cn: 海盗带着黑旗在海上航行。
words.en: A pirate is someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. The term can also refer to someone who illegally copies and distributes software, music, or films.

words.ex: He held a pistol in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他手里拿着一把手枪。
words.en: A pistol is a small gun.

words.tr:
n. 音高；球场；程度（最高点）；宣传论点；
v. 扎营；
words.ex: The singer changed the pitch of her voice.
words.ex_cn: 歌手改变了她声音的音高。
words.en: Pitch can refer to the highness or lowness of a sound, the act of throwing something, or a thick, black, sticky substance used for paving roads or waterproofing.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.tr: adj. 令人怜悯的；使人同情的；可怜的
words.ex: The dog looked pitiful in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe something as pitiful, you mean that it is inadequate or disappointing.

words.tr: n. 匹兹堡（美国宾夕法尼亚州西南部城市）
words.ex: Pittsburgh is known for its steel industry.
words.ex_cn: 匹兹堡以其钢铁工业闻名。
words.en: A city in southwestern Pennsylvania, USA, known for its steel industry and cultural institutions.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.ex: She sat placidly by the window, watching the rain.
words.ex_cn: 她平静地坐在窗边，看着雨。
words.en: In a calm and peaceful manner; without disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: The placidity of the lake was disturbed by a sudden gust of wind.
words.ex_cn: 湖面的平静被一阵突如其来的风打破了。
words.en: Placidity refers to the state or quality of being calm and peaceful.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.ex: The plagiarizer was caught red-handed copying someone else's work.
words.ex_cn: 那个剽窃者被当场抓住抄袭别人的作品。
words.en: A plagiarizer is someone who uses another person's ideas or work and pretends that it is their own.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.tr: adv. 清楚地；明显地；明白地
words.ex: She spoke plainly, without any attempt to hide her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她直率地说话，毫不掩饰自己的感情。
words.en: In a manner that is easy to perceive or understand; clearly.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 刨工，刨机; 刨路机; 水榆; 平刨
words.ex: He uses a planer to smooth the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用刨子把木头磨平。
words.en: A planer is a tool or machine used for smoothing or shaping wood or other materials by removing thin layers from the surface.

words.ex: He nailed the wooden plank to the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把木板钉在了地板上。
words.en: A plank is a long, flat piece of wood, often used in building or as part of a structure.

words.tr: n. 匾额；饰板；薄金属板；齿菌斑
words.ex: The plaque on the wall honors the founder of the school.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的匾额纪念这所学校的创始人。
words.en: A plaque is a flat piece of metal or stone with writing on it that is fixed to a wall or other structure to remind people of an important person or event.

words.ex: The artist presented a plaquette to the museum as a gift.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将一个小匾作为礼物赠予博物馆。
words.en: A small, decorative metal plaque, often used for commemorative or artistic purposes.

words.tr:
n. 灰泥；
v. 涂以灰泥；敷以膏药；
words.ex: The wall was covered with white plaster.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁上覆盖着白色灰泥。
words.en: A substance applied to walls or ceilings to smooth or decorate them, or a medical dressing used to cover wounds.

words.ex: The sheep graze on a high plateau.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在高高原上吃草。
words.en: A plateau is a large area of high and fairly flat land. It can also refer to a period during which there are no large changes.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.ex: He put the food on a large platter.
words.ex_cn: 他把食物放在一个大盘子上。
words.en: A large flat dish or plate, typically used for serving food.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: The playful puppy chased its tail.
words.ex_cn: 那只爱玩耍的小狗追着自己的尾巴跑。
words.en: Someone who is playful is full of fun and likes to play.

words.ex: He plays with his playmate every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午和玩伴一起玩。
words.en: A playmate is a child's friend with whom they play.

words.tr: n. 延长赛；季后赛；最后决赛
words.ex: The two teams competed in a playoff to decide the champion.
words.ex_cn: 这两支球队在延长赛中竞争冠军。
words.en: A playoff is a series of games played after the regular season in order to determine the champion or to qualify for a higher level of competition.

words.tr: n. 玩物，供消遣的东西; <正>玩具
words.ex: She treated him like a plaything.
words.ex_cn: 她把他当作玩物。
words.en: A plaything is an object that a child plays with, such as a toy, or someone who is treated as if they have no feelings and is used for someone else's amusement.

words.tr: n. 游戏时间，娱乐时间
words.ex: The children are having playtime in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在公园里玩耍。
words.en: The time allowed for children to play.

words.ex: The pleasantness of the weather made the outing enjoyable.
words.ex_cn: 宜人的天气使得郊游非常愉快。
words.en: The quality of being pleasant; agreeableness.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.tr:
n. 犁；犁形器具
v. 犁；耕；艰苦前进
words.ex: The farmer uses a plow to turn the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用犁翻土。
words.en: A plow is a farm tool with one or more heavy blades that breaks the soil and cuts a furrow for sowing seeds.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.tr:
v. 摘；拔；猛拉；拨弹
n. 胆识；胆量；快而猛地拉
words.ex: He plucked a flower from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他从花园里摘了一朵花。
words.en: To pluck means to pull something quickly to remove it or to play a musical instrument by pulling the strings with your fingers. As a noun, it refers to the quality of being brave and determined.

words.tr: n. 抓棉机; 拔毛机
words.ex: The plucker is used to remove feathers from poultry.
words.ex_cn: 拔毛机用于去除家禽的羽毛。
words.en: A plucker is someone who removes feathers from birds or picks fruits or vegetables.

words.ex: The builder used a plumb to check if the wall was straight.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人用铅锤检查墙是否垂直。
words.en: To measure the depth of water with a plumb line; to explore or understand something deeply; exactly vertical; completely or directly.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: He used a plunger to unclog the sink.
words.ex_cn: 他用活塞来疏通水槽。
words.en: A plunger is a device consisting of a rubber cup on the end of a stick, used to clear blocked pipes by means of suction.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.tr: adj. 财阀的；富豪的；有钱有势的
words.ex: The government was criticized for being too plutocratic.
words.ex_cn: 该政府因过于富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the rule of the wealthy.

words.ex: The plutocrat's vast wealth allowed him to influence political decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位富豪的巨额财富使他能够影响政治决策。
words.en: A plutocrat is someone who uses their wealth to control a country or area, especially in a way that is considered unfair or selfish.

words.tr: n. 小笔记本；钱夹；袖珍本；财力
words.ex: He wrote the phone number in his pocketbook.
words.ex_cn: 他把电话号码写在了他的小笔记本里。
words.en: A pocketbook is a small book, especially one that can be carried in a pocket, or a woman's handbag.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；捅
n. 戳；刺；捅
words.ex: He poked the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke means to prod or jab someone or something with a finger or a pointed object, or to move something in a particular direction with a sharp movement. It can also refer to the act of making a hole or opening in something by pushing a pointed object into it.

words.ex: The poignancy of the moment was not lost on anyone.
words.ex_cn: 那一刻的辛酸没有被任何人忽略。
words.en: The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.tr: adv. 尖锐地；明确地；直言不讳地
words.ex: She looked at him pointedly.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐地看着他。
words.en: In a way that is clearly directed and makes a specific point or meaning obvious.

words.ex: The polarity of the magnet is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个磁铁的极性很清晰。
words.en: Polarity refers to the state of having two opposite or contradictory tendencies, opinions, or aspects.

words.tr: n. 决策者；政策制定者
words.ex: The policymaker made a new rule for schools.
words.ex_cn: 这位政策制定者为学校制定了一项新规定。
words.en: A policymaker is a person responsible for or involved in formulating policies, especially in government.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: The North Pole is covered with ice all year round.
words.ex_cn: 北极全年都被冰雪覆盖。
words.en: A pole is a long, thin, rounded piece of wood or metal, used especially for supporting things.

chapters.name: 第4周 认知词汇2000 星期六

words.ex: The factory releases a pollutant into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向河里排放一种污染物。
words.en: A pollutant is a substance that pollutes something, especially air, water, or soil.

words.ex: The factory is a big polluter.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂是一个严重的污染源。
words.en: A polluter is a person or organization that causes pollution, especially one that releases harmful substances into the environment.

words.tr: n. 工艺专科学院；理工专科学院；
words.ex: He enrolled in a polytechnic to learn engineering.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所工艺专科学院学习工程。
words.en: A polytechnic is an institution of higher education offering courses in many subjects, especially vocational or technical subjects.

words.ex: He put the food in a polythene bag.
words.ex_cn: 他把食物放在一个聚乙烯袋里。
words.en: Polythene is a type of plastic made in thin sheets, used especially for keeping things dry or for wrapping things.

words.tr: n. 庞贝（意大利古罗马城市，公元79年因维苏威火山爆发而被埋没）
words.ex: Pompeii was buried by a volcano long ago.
words.ex_cn: 庞贝古城很久以前被火山掩埋了。
words.en: An ancient Roman city near modern Naples, Italy, which was buried under volcanic ash in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79.

words.ex: The child rides a pony in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在公园里骑小马。
words.en: A pony is a small horse.

words.ex: The red poppy grows in the field.
words.ex_cn: 红罂粟生长在田地里。
words.en: A poppy is a plant with large, delicate, red flowers. The seeds of the poppy are used in cooking and for producing oil.

words.ex: The popularization of the internet has revolutionized communication.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的普及彻底改变了通信方式。
words.en: The act of making something widely known and accepted by the general public.

words.ex: This song is popularly played on the radio.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌普遍地在收音机里播放。
words.en: If something is popularly known as a particular thing, most people know it by that name.

words.ex: He bought a porcelain cup at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个瓷杯。
words.en: A hard, white, translucent ceramic that is made by firing a pure clay and then glazing it.

words.ex: He sits on the porch and drinks coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在门廊上喝咖啡。
words.en: A porch is a covered shelter projecting in front of the entrance of a building.

words.tr:
n. 毛孔；小孔
v. 细看；钻研；凝视
words.ex: Sweat comes out through the pores of the skin.
words.ex_cn: 汗水通过皮肤上的毛孔排出。
words.en: A pore is a tiny opening in a surface that allows liquids or gases to pass through. As a verb, to pore means to read or study something very carefully.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.tr: n. 朴茨茅斯（英国城市）
words.ex: Portsmouth is a major port city in Hampshire, England.
words.ex_cn: 朴茨茅斯是英格兰汉普郡的一个主要港口城市。
words.en: Portsmouth is a city in the south of England, known for its historic dockyard and naval base.

words.tr:
n. 葡萄牙人；葡萄牙语；
adj. 葡萄牙的；葡萄牙人的；葡萄牙语的；
words.ex: He is a Portuguese from Lisbon.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位来自里斯本的葡萄牙人。
words.en: Portuguese refers to something that is related to Portugal, its people, or its language. It can also denote the people of Portugal or the Portuguese language itself.

words.ex: Postsecondary education focuses on specialized knowledge and skills.
words.ex_cn: 高等教育侧重于专业知识和技能。
words.en: Postsecondary education refers to education beyond the secondary level, especially education at the college or university level.

words.ex: The postwar economy grew quickly.
words.ex_cn: 战后经济迅速增长。
words.en: occurring or existing after a war

words.ex: Farmers use potash to make soil better for crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用钾肥来改善土壤以利于作物生长。
words.en: Potash is a potassium compound, often used in fertilizers to improve plant growth and soil quality.

words.tr: n. 效力; 力量，权力，能力
words.ex: The potence of his argument convinced everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点的力量说服了房间里的每个人。
words.en: The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way; effectiveness.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: The potentate ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者以铁腕统治。
words.en: A potentate is a ruler who has great power, especially one who rules over a large area or empire.

words.ex: The child has great potentiality to learn quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子有很强的学习能力潜力。
words.en: Potentiality refers to the inherent capacity or ability for growth, development, or coming into existence.

words.ex: The potter made a clay bowl by hand.
words.ex_cn: 陶工用手制作了一个陶碗。
words.en: A potter is someone who makes pottery, and to potter means to busy oneself in a desultory but pleasant manner.

words.ex: He buys poultry at the local market.
words.ex_cn: 他在当地市场买家禽。
words.en: Poultry refers to domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat, or feathers.

words.ex: He felt powerlessness when he couldn't help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 当他无法帮助朋友时，他感到无能为力。
words.en: The state or condition of being powerless; lack of power or ability to act or influence.

words.ex: Smallpox is a highly contagious pox.
words.ex_cn: 天花是一种高度传染性的痘症。
words.en: A pox is a disease characterized by pustules or eruptions on the skin, often associated with viruses.

words.tr: n. 波兹南（波兰中西部城市）
words.ex: Poznań is a major city in western Poland.
words.ex_cn: 波兹南是波兰西部的一座重要城市。
words.en: A city in western Poland, known for its historic market square and cultural events.

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.ex: He is a pragmatist who solves problems with real solutions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个注重实际解决方案的实用主义者。
words.en: A pragmatist is someone who is pragmatic, that is, someone who is practical and focused on reaching a goal. Pragmatists are results-oriented and often have a no-nonsense approach to solving problems.

words.ex: The cows graze on the prairie.
words.ex_cn: 牛在草原上吃草。
words.en: A prairie is a large area of flat, grassy land, especially in North America.

words.tr: n. 开玩笑者；恶作剧者；顽皮的人
words.ex: The prankster was known for his elaborate practical jokes.
words.ex_cn: 这个爱开玩笑的人以他精心策划的恶作剧而闻名。
words.en: A prankster is someone who plays tricks on people or causes mischief in a playful way.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: n. 事先形成的看法；先入之见；成见
words.ex: He had a preconception that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: An idea or opinion that is formed before you have enough information or experience, or a bias that prevents objective consideration of an issue.

words.ex: The cave paintings predate written history.
words.ex_cn: 这些洞穴壁画早于文字历史。
words.en: To exist or occur at a date earlier than something else.

words.ex: The lion's predation helps control the deer population.
words.ex_cn: 狮子的捕食有助于控制鹿群的数量。
words.en: The act of preying by a predator, especially the killing and eating of an animal by another animal.

words.ex: The lion is a predatory animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Predatory animals live by killing and eating other animals. Predatory people or organizations are eager to gain something out of someone else's weakness or suffering.

words.tr: adv. 可预见地；可预言地
words.ex: He arrives late, predictably.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，这很可预见。
words.en: In a way that can be expected or foreseen.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: He has a predisposition to catch colds easily.
words.ex_cn: 他容易感冒的倾向。
words.en: A predisposition is a tendency to behave in a particular way or to suffer from a particular condition.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: You can take the bus, preferably early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 你可以坐公交车，最好是在早上早些时候。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferably to another, you mean that the first thing is more desirable or suitable than the second.

words.tr: n. 史前史学家，史前学家
words.ex: The prehistorian studied the artifacts to understand ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 这位史前史学家研究文物以了解古代文明。
words.en: A prehistorian is a specialist in prehistoric archaeology, focusing on the study of human history before written records.

words.ex: Prehistory is the time before writing was invented.
words.ex_cn: 史前是文字发明之前的时代。
words.en: The period of time before written records began, studied through archaeology and anthropology.

words.ex: He preliminarily checked the data before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前初步检查了数据。
words.en: In a preliminary manner; as a preliminary step or measure.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.tr: v. 先占；使全神贯注；占据…的思想
words.ex: The old man preoccupies the best seat in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人先占了公园里最好的座位。
words.en: If something is preoccupying you, you are thinking about it a lot or it is occupying your attention.

words.ex: The preponderance of evidence shows he is guilty.
words.ex_cn: 大多数证据表明他有罪。
words.en: If there is a preponderance of one type of thing or person in a group, there are more of that type than of any other.

words.ex: In the sentence, 'on the table' is a prepositional phrase.
words.ex_cn: 在句子中，'on the table' 是一个介词短语。
words.en: Relating to or functioning as a preposition.

words.tr: n. 演讲人；节目主持人；发言人；呈献者；
words.ex: The presenter told a funny story to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 演讲人给观众讲了一个有趣的故事。
words.en: A presenter is a person who introduces or hosts a television or radio program, or who introduces a speaker or performer at a public event.

words.ex: Bread often contains a preservative to last longer.
words.ex_cn: 面包中常含有防腐剂以延长保质期。
words.en: A preservative is a chemical that is added to substances such as food, wood, or medicine to prevent them from decaying or spoiling.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.tr: v. 预先假定；预料；以…为先决条件
words.ex: He presupposes that everyone likes coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他假设每个人都喜欢咖啡。
words.en: If one thing presupposes another, the first thing cannot be true or exist unless the second thing is true or exists.

words.tr: adj. 可以预防的；可以防止的；
words.ex: This disease is preventable with clean water.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病通过干净的水是可以预防的。
words.en: Capable of being prevented; able to be stopped or avoided.

words.ex: The priest said a prayer for the sick.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为病人祈祷。
words.en: A priest is a person who is qualified to perform religious duties and ceremonies in a Christian church.

words.ex: This phone is pricey, so I bought a cheaper one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机价格很高，所以我买了一个便宜的。
words.en: If you describe something as pricey, you mean that it is expensive.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.ex: He tries to procure food for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力为家人获取食物。
words.en: To obtain something, especially with care or effort.

words.tr: n. 受公众注意的程度；简介；轮廓；
words.ex: The celebrity's profile rose after the TV interview.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人经过电视采访后，受公众注意的程度提高了。
words.en: A profile is a side view of something, especially a person's face, or a brief description of someone or something.

words.tr: n. 放荡；不检点；肆意挥霍
words.ex: His profligacy led to the loss of all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他的放荡导致他失去了所有的钱。
words.en: Profligacy refers to reckless extravagance or wastefulness in the use of resources, or to licentiousness or dissoluteness in behavior.

words.ex: The proliferation of bacteria causes the infection to spread.
words.ex_cn: 细菌的增殖导致感染扩散。
words.en: The rapid increase in the number or amount of something.

words.tr: n. 促进者；发起者；倡导者；支持者
words.ex: He is a promoter of healthy eating.
words.ex_cn: 他是健康饮食的倡导者。
words.en: A promoter is a person or organization that helps to organize and finance an event, such as a concert or sports match.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.ex: The government used propaganda to influence people's opinions.
words.ex_cn: 政府使用宣传来影响人们的观点。
words.en: Information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view.

words.ex: The poster is propagandistic and tries to control people's thoughts.
