words.ex: The forest is full of tall spruce trees.
words.ex_cn: 森林里长满了高大的云杉树。
words.en: A spruce is a type of evergreen tree with needle-like leaves. As an adjective, it describes something neat and trim in appearance. As a verb, it means to make someone or something neat and smart in appearance.

words.ex: She added cinnamon spice to the cake.
words.ex_cn: 她往蛋糕里加了肉桂香料。
words.en: Spice refers to a substance used to flavor food, which is usually made from parts of plants, especially their seeds, fruits, or roots. It can also mean something that adds interest or excitement.

words.ex: He hurt his spinal cord in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中伤到了脊髓。
words.en: Relating to the spine or the spinal cord.

words.ex: The boy hurt his spine when he fell from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 他从树上摔下来时伤到了脊柱。
words.en: The spine is the row of bones down the center of your back that supports your body and protects your spinal cord.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.ex: He did it out of spite.
words.ex_cn: 他出于恶意做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.

words.ex: He ran a 100-meter sprint in under 11 seconds.
words.ex_cn: 他在100米冲刺中跑出了不到11秒的成绩。
words.en: If you sprint, you run or ride as fast as you can over a short distance.

words.ex: The squad practices every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个小组每天早上训练。
words.en: A squad is a small group of people organized for a particular purpose or task.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.tr:
n. 刺；戳
v. 刺；戳
words.ex: He felt a sharp stab in his side.
words.ex_cn: 他感到侧腹一阵刺痛。
words.en: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.ex: The results were statistically significant.
words.ex_cn: 这些结果在统计上是显著的。
words.en: In a way that relates to statistics or the use of statistics.

words.tr: n. 小雕像，小塑像，小铸像
words.ex: She received a beautifully crafted statuette as a gift.
words.ex_cn: 她收到了一个精美的小雕像作为礼物。
words.en: A statuette is a small statue, often one that is used for decoration.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；
n. 五线谱；
words.ex: He staved off the angry dog with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子挡开了那只发怒的狗。
words.en: A stave is a narrow strip of wood, especially one that is part of a barrel or a ladder. It can also refer to a verse or stanza in poetry. As a verb, to stave means to break something by forcing it inward or to delay something.

words.ex: His steeliness helped him stay calm during the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚毅帮助他在危机中保持冷静。
words.en: The quality of being like steel in hardness or strength; also, the quality of being unyielding or resolute.

words.tr: adj. 似钢的；钢色的；坚硬如钢的
words.ex: She had steely determination to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 她有着钢铁般的决心要成功。
words.en: Resembling steel in color, brightness, or strength; hard and unyielding.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.ex: The church's steeple was visible from miles away.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔在数英里外就能看到。
words.en: A steeple is a tall pointed structure on the top of a building, especially a church.

words.ex: His neck was stiff after sleeping wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他睡姿不对，脖子变得僵硬。
words.en: If something is stiff, it is firm and does not bend easily. It can also describe a person who is not relaxed or friendly.

words.ex: The wind stiffened the cloth on the line.
words.ex_cn: 风把晾衣绳上的布吹硬了。
words.en: to make or become stiff or rigid; to make or become more severe or strict

words.tr: n. 使僵硬的人（或物）; 扶强材
words.ex: The metal stiffener makes the box stronger.
words.ex_cn: 金属加强筋使箱子更坚固。
words.en: A stiffener is a device or substance used to make something rigid or stiff.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.ex: The stillness of the night was broken by a sudden cry.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的沉静被一声突如其来的叫喊打破。
words.en: The absence of movement or sound; quietness and calm.

words.ex: Caffeine is a common stimulant.
words.ex_cn: 咖啡因是一种常见的兴奋剂。
words.en: A stimulant is a substance that raises levels of physiological or nervous activity in the body.

words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.ex: The contract has a stipulation about payment dates.
words.ex_cn: 合同中有关于付款日期的规定。
words.en: A stipulation is a condition or requirement that is specified as part of an agreement or contract.

words.ex: He works as a stockbroker in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约做股票经纪人。
words.en: A stockbroker is a person whose job is to buy and sell stocks and shares for other people.

words.ex: He is a stockholding shareholder in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家公司的持股股东。
words.en: The ownership of shares in a company.

words.tr:
n. 大量贮备；囤积
v. 大量储备；囤积
words.ex: The government built a stockpile of food for emergencies.
words.ex_cn: 政府为紧急情况储备了大量食物。
words.en: A stockpile is a large supply of something that is kept to be used in the future.

words.ex: The worker walks to the stockroom to get more boxes.
words.ex_cn: 工人走到仓库去拿更多的箱子。
words.en: A stockroom is a room where goods are stored, especially in a shop or factory.

words.tr: n. 盘点; 估计，估量
words.ex: The shop does a stocktake every month.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店每个月进行一次盘点。
words.en: A stocktake is the process of counting all the goods that a shop or business has at a particular time.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.tr:
n. 跺脚；顿足爵士舞乐曲
v. 迈着重重的步子走（或跳舞、移动）
words.ex: The baby made a stomp with his foot when he was angry.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝生气时用脚跺了一下。
words.en: To stomp means to walk heavily or noisily, often because you are angry.

words.tr:
v. 弯腰；俯身；卑屈；俯冲
n. 弯腰；屈背；屈服；俯冲
words.ex: He must stoop to enter the small door.
words.ex_cn: 他必须弯腰才能进入那扇小门。
words.en: If someone stoops, they bend their body forwards and downwards.

words.ex: The stormy sea crashed against the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海浪拍打着岩石。
words.en: Characterized by strong winds and usually rain, thunder, lightning, or snow.

words.ex: The old tree has a stout trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个粗壮的树干。
words.en: Someone who is stout is rather fat or heavy.

words.tr: v. 蔓延；散乱地分布；落伍
words.ex: Weeds straggle across the garden.
words.ex_cn: 杂草蔓延在整个花园里。
words.en: If people straggle, they move along slowly, spread out over a wide area, and are not in a group.

words.tr: adj. 散乱的; 蔓延的; 落后的; 脱离行列的
words.ex: The straggly hair made her look unkempt.
words.ex_cn: 散乱的头发让她看起来不修边幅。
words.en: Growing or spreading out in a scattered or irregular way.

words.tr: n. 落伍者；掉队者；落在最后的人（或动物）
words.ex: The straggler arrived late to the group.
words.ex_cn: 那个落伍者迟到了，没跟上队伍。
words.en: A straggler is a person or thing that is late or slow in comparison with others in a group, often because they are moving more slowly or are less organized.

words.ex: The ship sailed through the strait at night.
words.ex_cn: 船在夜间通过了海峡。
words.en: A strait is a narrow passage of water connecting two seas or two large areas of water.

words.ex: He has a streak of kindness that makes everyone like him.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种善良的性情，让每个人都喜欢他。
words.en: A streak is a long thin mark that is a different colour from the surfaces next to it. It can also refer to a period of time during which a particular kind of behaviour or activity is consistently shown.

words.tr: n. 英国货币；英镑；标准纯银；银制品；
words.ex: He paid for the book with sterling.
words.ex_cn: 他用英镑支付了这本书的费用。
words.en: Sterling is used to describe something of very high quality or value. It can also refer to British money or a standard of purity for silver.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.tr: n. 应激物；压力源；紧张性刺激
words.ex: Lack of sleep is a common stressor.
words.ex_cn: 睡眠不足是一种常见的压力源。
words.en: A stressor is a chemical or biological agent, environmental condition, external stimulus or an event that causes stress to an organism.

words.ex: She tied the box with a thin string.
words.ex_cn: 她用一根细线把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A string is a thin piece of rope or cord, or a series of things connected together.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.ex: The tiger has black stripes on its orange fur.
words.ex_cn: 老虎的橙色皮毛上有黑色条纹。
words.en: A stripe is a long, narrow band or strip differing in color or texture from the surface on either side of it.

words.tr:
n. 种马；钉状首饰；饰钮；性欲旺盛的男子；风流男子
v. 打上装饰钉；镶嵌；布满颗粒
words.ex: The farmer owns a strong stud for breeding horses.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民养了一匹强壮的种马用于配种。
words.en: A stud is a male animal, especially a horse, that is kept for breeding. As a verb, it means to decorate or cover something with many small objects.

words.tr: n. 使无效；使显得愚笨
words.ex: The boring rules caused stultification in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 枯燥的规则导致了课堂上的呆滞。
words.en: The act of making someone or something seem foolish or ineffective.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.tr: adv. 无比地；令人震惊地
words.ex: She is stunningly beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 她美得惊人。
words.en: In a way that is extremely impressive or attractive.

words.tr:
n. 树桩；残段；残根
v. 难倒；重步走
words.ex: The tree stump is still in the yard.
words.ex_cn: 树桩还在院子里。
words.en: A stump is the base part of a tree that remains after the rest of the tree has been cut down. It can also refer to a difficult problem or to the act of walking heavily.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.tr: n. 昏迷；不省人事；恍惚
words.ex: He fell into a stupor after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他陷入了昏迷状态。
words.en: A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷的，不省人事的；无感觉的
words.ex: He became stuporous after taking too much medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他服药过多后变得昏昏沉沉。
words.en: In a state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.

words.tr: adv. 坚强地，刚强地，坚毅地
words.ex: He built the table sturdily.
words.ex_cn: 他结实牢固地建造了这张桌子。
words.en: In a manner that shows physical strength or determination.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.ex: The stygian cave was dark and cold.
words.ex_cn: 那个阴森的洞穴又黑又冷。
words.en: extremely dark, gloomy, or forbidding

words.ex: He loves the punk subculture.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢朋克亚文化。
words.en: A subculture is a group of people within a culture that differentiates itself from the parent culture to which it belongs, often maintaining some of its founding principles.

words.tr: n. 学科的分支；分科；子域
words.ex: Algebra is a subfield of mathematics.
words.ex_cn: 代数是数学的一个子领域。
words.en: A subfield is a specific area of study or research within a broader field.

words.tr: adv. 主观地；臆想地；内省地
words.ex: The judge considered the evidence subjectively.
words.ex_cn: 法官主观地考虑了证据。
words.en: In a way that is based on personal feelings, tastes, or opinions rather than on facts.

words.tr:
adj. 虚拟语气的
n. 虚拟语气；虚拟式
words.ex: In English, the subjunctive mood is often used to express hypothetical situations.
words.ex_cn: 在英语中，虚拟语气常用于表达假设的情况。
words.en: The subjunctive is a verb form or mood used to express hypothetical or non-real actions, events, or situations.

words.tr: vt. 给……发从属证书（或执照、许可证等）; n. （证书持有者发给其他人的）从属证书（（或执照、...
words.ex: He can sublicense the software to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他可以把这个软件再许可给他的朋友们。
words.en: A sublicense is a license granted by a licensee to a third party, under the authority of the original licensor, to perform acts covered by the original license.

words.tr:
v. （使）升华；使净化
adj. 升华的；纯化的
words.ex: He tries to sublimate his anger into art.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把愤怒升华成艺术。
words.en: To sublimate means to transform something, especially a strong emotion or desire, into a more positive or acceptable form, often through a process of refinement or elevation.

words.ex: The process of sublimation can be used to purify substances.
words.ex_cn: 升华过程可以用来提纯物质。
words.en: The process by which a substance changes directly from a solid to a gas without becoming a liquid first.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: He got a subprime loan because his credit was poor.
words.ex_cn: 因为他的信用不好，他获得了一笔次要贷款。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a loan, typically a mortgage, offered to a borrower with a poor credit history.

words.ex: The set {1, 2} is a subset of {1, 2, 3}.
words.en: A subset of a group of things is a smaller group of those things.

words.tr: v. 维持生活；生存下去
words.ex: They subsist on rice and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 他们靠米饭和蔬菜维持生活。
words.en: If people subsist, they are just able to obtain the food or money that they need in order to stay alive.

words.ex: They live in a subsistent way, growing their own food.
words.ex_cn: 他们以自给自足的方式生活，自己种粮食。
words.en: Subsistent refers to something that exists or is capable of existing, especially in terms of sustaining life or maintaining a certain state.

words.tr: adj. 未达到标准的；不达标的；不合格的
words.ex: The food was substandard and made us sick.
words.ex_cn: 这些食物质量低劣，让我们生病了。
words.en: Below the usual or required standard.

words.tr: n. 底层；下层土壤地基
words.ex: The rock layer is the substratum of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 岩石层是土壤的基底。
words.en: A substratum is an underlying layer or substance, especially one that forms a foundation or basis.

words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.ex: The rule is a subsumption of the earlier law.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则是早期法律的包含。
words.en: The act of including or absorbing something within a larger or more general category or principle.

words.tr: n. 说明或对白的字幕；副标题；
words.ex: The movie has English subtitles for the dialogue.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影为对白提供了英文字幕。
words.en: A subtitle is a secondary or explanatory title, or a translation of the dialogue in a film or television program, displayed at the bottom of the screen.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.ex: The plot involved subversion of the government.
words.ex_cn: 这个情节涉及对政府的颠覆。
words.en: Subversion is the act of trying to destroy or damage an established system or government.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: He explained the idea succinctly.
words.ex_cn: 他简洁地解释了这个想法。
words.en: In a manner that is expressed in a few words; concisely.

words.ex: The report's succinctness made it easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 报告的简洁性使其易于理解。
words.en: The quality of being expressed clearly and in a few words.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The water is sufficiently warm to swim.
words.ex_cn: 水温足够暖和，可以游泳。
words.en: To an adequate degree; enough.

words.ex: He packed his clothes into a suitcase.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服装进了行李箱。
words.en: A suitcase is a case with a handle and often with wheels, used for carrying clothes and possessions when travelling.

words.ex: They booked a hotel suite for their honeymoon.
words.ex_cn: 他们为蜜月预订了一间酒店套房。
words.en: A set of rooms designated for use together, especially in a hotel; a set of musical compositions designed to be performed in a sequence.

words.tr: n. 苏丹（某些穆斯林国家统治者的称号）
words.ex: The sultan ruled the land with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 苏丹以智慧统治着这片土地。
words.en: A sultan is a ruler in some Muslim countries.

words.tr: n. 概括; 摘要，概要
words.ex: He wrote a summarization of the book in one page.
words.ex_cn: 他用一页纸写了一个这本书的摘要。
words.en: The act of making a summary or the process of summarizing.

words.ex: We watched the sundown from the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海滩上观看了日落。
words.en: The time in the evening when the sun disappears or daylight fades.

words.ex: The sunken ship lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 沉没的船位于海底。
words.en: Having descended below the surface; submerged or depressed.

words.ex: We woke up early to see the sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 我们早起看日出。
words.en: The time in the morning when the sun appears or full daylight arrives.

words.ex: The food at this restaurant is superb.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅的食物极佳。
words.en: If something is superb, its quality is very good indeed.

words.tr: adj. 闷热的；性感的；撩人的
words.ex: The sultry weather made everyone feel tired.
words.ex_cn: 闷热的天气让每个人都感到疲惫。
words.en: Sultry weather is hot and damp in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable.

words.tr: adv. 雄伟地；壮丽地；极好地
words.ex: The castle stands superbly on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡雄伟地矗立在山上。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely good or excellent.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: She is a supermodel who walks on runways.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位走T台的超级模特。
words.en: A supermodel is a highly paid fashion model who usually has a worldwide reputation and often a background in haute couture and commercial modeling.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 代谢; 取代，废弃
words.ex: The new law causes the supersession of the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律导致了旧法律的取代。
words.en: The act of replacing someone or something with another person or thing.

words.ex: The jet flies at supersonic speed.
words.ex_cn: 这架喷气式飞机以超音速飞行。
words.en: relating to speeds that are faster than the speed of sound

words.tr: n. 镇压者，抑制物，干扰抑制器
words.ex: The gun has a suppressor to reduce the noise.
words.ex_cn: 这把枪装有消音器以降低噪音。
words.en: A suppressor is a device or person that suppresses something, especially something undesirable.

words.tr:
n. 额外费用；附加费
v. 额外索价；附加罚款
words.ex: He paid a surcharge for extra baggage.
words.ex_cn: 他为额外行李支付了附加费。
words.en: An additional charge or payment.

words.tr:
n. 激浪；拍岸浪花；
v. 冲浪；（互联网上）冲浪；
words.ex: He bought a new surf for the beach trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为海滩之旅买了一块新的激浪。
words.en: To surf means to ride on the crest of a wave towards the shore, typically on a surfboard. It can also mean to browse the internet.

words.ex: The volcano released sulfur into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山向空气中释放了硫。
words.en: Sulfur is a pale yellow, odorless, brittle solid, which is insoluble in water but soluble in carbon disulfide.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: adv. 偷偷摸摸地；暗中进行地
words.ex: He surreptitiously took the cookie from the jar.
words.ex_cn: 他偷偷地从罐子里拿走了饼干。
words.en: If you do something surreptitiously, you do it secretly, often because you do not want people to notice it.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: Children have higher susceptibility to colds.
words.ex_cn: 儿童更容易感冒。
words.en: The condition of being susceptible; the state of being easily affected, influenced, or harmed by something.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.tr: n. 悬浮；暂时停职（停学、停赛）；
words.ex: The suspension of dust in the air made the sky look gray.
words.ex_cn: 空气中的尘埃悬浮使天空看起来灰蒙蒙的。
words.en: The act of temporarily stopping something from happening or being in effect, or the state of being stopped in this way.

words.tr:
v. 交换；
n. 交换；
words.ex: They swap books every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周交换书籍。
words.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动；
n. 影响；支配；
words.ex: The tree branches sway in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树的枝条在风中摇摆。
words.en: To sway means to move slowly or rhythmically backwards and forwards or from side to side. It can also mean to influence someone or something.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.ex: The butterfly is symmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶是对称的。
words.en: Something that is symmetrical has parts that are equal in size, shape, and position, and that are arranged in a balanced way.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.tr: n. 专题讨论会；研讨会
words.ex: He spoke at a symposium about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个关于气候变化的研讨会上发言。
words.en: A symposium is a conference or meeting to discuss a particular subject.

words.ex: The two teams showed synergy when they finished the project early.
words.ex_cn: 当这两个团队提前完成项目时，展现了协同效应。
words.en: The interaction or cooperation of two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.tr: adv. 依照句法地，在语句构成上
words.ex: He speaks syntactically correct English.
words.ex_cn: 他讲的英语在语法上是正确的。
words.en: In a way that relates to the rules of grammar that are used for ordering and connecting words to form phrases and sentences.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.ex: He tries to synthesize ideas from different books.
words.ex_cn: 他试图综合来自不同书籍的想法。
words.en: To synthesize means to combine different ideas, influences, or objects into a new whole, or to produce a substance by a chemical reaction in plants or animals.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.tr: v. 使系统化；使成体系；使条理化
words.ex: He tries to systematize his notes before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前试图系统化他的笔记。
words.en: To systematize means to arrange according to an organized system; make systematic.

words.tr: n. 系统化，组织化，分类
words.ex: The systematization of rules made the game easier to understand.
words.ex_cn: 规则的系统化使这个游戏更容易理解。
words.en: The act of arranging or organizing something according to a system or method.

words.tr: n. 分类者；组织者；使体系化的人
words.ex: He is a systematizer who organizes every detail.
words.ex_cn: 他是个系统化者，能整理每一个细节。
words.en: A systematizer is someone who organizes things according to a system or plan.

words.ex: The government made systemic changes to improve education.
words.ex_cn: 政府进行了系统的改革以改善教育。
words.en: Systemic means affecting the whole of something rather than just part of it.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.tr:
n. 晒成棕褐色的肤色
adj. 棕褐色的；棕黄色的
v. 将皮肤晒成棕褐色
words.ex: He has a deep tan after spending the week at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩度过一周后，皮肤晒成了深棕色。
words.en: If you tan, or if the sun tans you, your skin becomes darker because you spend time in the sun.

words.ex: The line touches the circle at one point and is a tangent.
words.ex_cn: 这条线与圆在一个点相切，是一条切线。
words.en: A tangent is a straight line or plane that touches a curve or curved surface at a point, but if extended does not cross it at that point. In a more general sense, it can also refer to a sudden digression or change of course.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.ex: Add a teaspoon of sugar to the tea.
words.ex_cn: 给茶里加一茶匙糖。
words.en: A teaspoon is a small spoon that you use to put sugar into tea or coffee.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.tr:
v. 治疗；对待；
n. 款待；
words.ex: The doctor will treat his fever with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生会用药物治疗他的发烧。
words.en: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave towards them or deal with them in that way.

words.tr: n. 技术性问题；技术细节
words.ex: He won the case because of a technicality.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个技术性细节赢得了诉讼。
words.en: A technicality is a small detail in a law or a set of rules, especially one that forces a particular result.

words.ex: The technician fixed the broken machine.
words.ex_cn: 技术员修好了坏掉的机器。
words.en: A technician is a worker trained with special skills, especially in science or engineering.

words.ex: The child hugged his teddy before sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 孩子睡觉前抱着他的泰迪玩具熊。
words.en: A teddy is a child's toy bear, which is usually made of soft furry material.

words.tr: n. 电讯家庭办公；在家办公；
words.ex: He likes telecommuting because he can work from home.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢电讯家庭办公，因为他可以在家工作。
words.en: Telecommuting refers to the practice of working from home or another remote location, using the internet, email, and the telephone to communicate with the office.

words.tr: n. 讲词提示机; 讲词提示器
words.ex: The speaker read the speech from a teleprompter.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者从提词器上读演讲稿。
words.en: A teleprompter is a device used in television and video production to display a script or speech for a presenter or actor to read while appearing to look directly into the camera.

words.ex: He practices temperance by drinking little alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他通过少喝酒来节制。
words.en: Temperance is the practice of moderation or self-restraint, especially in the consumption of alcohol.

words.ex: He tenaciously practiced piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天坚持不懈地练习钢琴。
words.en: In a manner that shows determination or persistence in holding onto something or in pursuing a goal.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: He held her tenderly in his arms.
words.ex_cn: 他温柔地把她抱在怀里。
words.en: In a gentle, loving, or kind manner.

words.tr: n. 温柔；柔情；压痛；柔和
words.ex: Her tenderness made the child feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 她的温柔让孩子感到安全。
words.en: The quality of being kind, gentle, and affectionate.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: The tenuousness of his argument made it easy to refute.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的脆弱性使它很容易被驳倒。
words.en: The quality of being very thin or slender; lack of density or substance.

words.ex: He held the rope tenuously.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧地握着绳子。
words.en: In a manner that is very weak or slight and likely to change or fail.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. 微温，微热; 温热
words.ex: The tepidity of his reply surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷淡的回复让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality or state of being tepid; lukewarmness.

words.ex: The terminator kills robots in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 终结者在电影里杀死机器人。
words.en: A terminator is someone or something that terminates, ends, or concludes something.

words.tr: adj. 术语的；术语学的；专门名词的
words.ex: The terminological error confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个术语错误让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Relating to the study or use of terms and their definitions.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr: n. 土地；地球；陆地（拉丁语）
words.ex: The terra is dry and cracked after the long summer.
words.ex_cn: 经过漫长的夏天，土地干裂了。
words.en: The term 'terra' refers to the land or earth, often used in scientific or poetic contexts to denote the planet Earth or its surface.

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.ex: The two countries argued over territorial rights.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家就领土权利发生了争执。
words.en: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea.

words.tr: v. 恐吓；恫吓；实施恐怖统治
words.ex: The bully tries to terrorize the new student.
words.ex_cn: 这个霸凌者试图恐吓新学生。
words.en: To terrorize someone means to make them very frightened by using violence or threats.

words.tr: n. 恐怖，畏惧; 恐怖手段抑制
words.ex: The group used terrorization to scare the villagers.
words.ex_cn: 这个组织通过恐吓来吓唬村民。
words.en: The act of terrorizing or the state of being terrorized; the use of terror as a means of coercion.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.ex: His terseness made the message hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的简洁让这个信息难以理解。
words.en: The quality or state of being terse; concise and pithy expression.

words.ex: He answered tersely, 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：'是的。'
words.en: In a brief and concise manner; without unnecessary details.

words.tr:
n. 证明书；推荐书
adj. 证明书的；表扬的
words.ex: She received a glowing testimonial from her former employer.
words.ex_cn: 她收到了前雇主的表扬推荐信。
words.en: A testimonial is a written statement about someone's character or abilities, or a thing given in recognition of service or achievement.

words.ex: The textual evidence supports the author's argument.
words.ex_cn: 文本证据支持作者的观点。
words.en: Relating to or based on a text.

words.ex: The thalamus sends signals to the brain.
words.ex_cn: 丘脑向大脑发送信号。
words.en: The thalamus is a large mass of gray matter in the diencephalon of the brain with several functions such as relaying of sensory signals, including motor signals, to the cerebral cortex, and the regulation of consciousness, sleep, and alertness.

words.tr: n. 神学家；神学研究者
words.ex: The theologian wrote a book about God.
words.ex_cn: 这位神学家写了一本关于上帝的书。
words.en: A theologian is someone who studies the nature of God, religion, and religious beliefs.

words.ex: Theoretically, the plan should work.
words.ex_cn: 理论上，这个计划应该可行。
words.en: In a way that relates to the theory of a subject or area of study rather than its practical application.

words.tr: v. 建立理论；建立学说；推论；推理
words.ex: Scientists theorize that black holes exist.
words.ex_cn: 科学家们建立理论认为黑洞存在。
words.en: To theorize means to form a theory or conjecture about a subject without firm evidence.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: He checked the thermometer to see the temperature.
words.ex_cn: 他看了温度计来查看温度。
words.en: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring and indicating temperature.

words.ex: He poured hot tea into the thermos.
words.ex_cn: 他把热茶倒进了保温瓶。
words.en: A thermos is a container which is used to keep hot drinks hot or cold drinks cold. It has two thin shiny glass walls with no air between them.

words.ex: The doctor examined his thorax with a stethoscope.
words.ex_cn: 医生用听诊器检查了他的胸腔。
words.en: The thorax is the part of the body between the neck and the abdomen, including the rib cage and the organs within it.

words.ex: His thoroughness in checking the answers ensured no mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他检查答案时的彻底确保了没有错误。
words.en: The quality of being complete with regard to every detail; exactness.

words.tr: adv. 若有所思地；沉思地；意味深长地；体贴地；关心地；
words.ex: He sat thoughtfully by the window, staring at the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他若有所思地坐在窗边，凝视着雨。
words.en: In a way that shows careful consideration or attention.

words.tr: adj. 色雷斯的；色雷斯人的；n. 色雷斯人
words.ex: The Thracian man sang an old folk song.
words.ex_cn: 那位色雷斯人唱了一首古老的民歌。
words.en: Relating to ancient Thrace, its people, or their language.

words.tr: n. 束缚；奴役；奴隶的身分
words.ex: He escaped from thralldom after many years.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年，他从奴役中逃脱了。
words.en: The state of being under the control of another person or of a powerful influence.

words.ex: She picked up a thread from the fabric.
words.ex_cn: 她从布料上捡起一根线。
words.en: A thread is a long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing or weaving. It can also refer to a theme or idea that connects parts of a story or discussion.

words.ex: He had a sore throat after singing all night.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一整晚后喉咙疼。
words.en: Your throat is the back part of your mouth, where it connects to your neck. It includes the passage that leads from your mouth to your stomach and lungs.

words.tr:
v. 跳动；悸动；颤动
n. 跳动；搏动；悸动
words.ex: His heart throbbed with fear.
words.ex_cn: 他的心脏因恐惧而跳动。
words.en: If part of your body throbs, you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.

words.tr:
adj. 跳动的；悸动的
n. 跳动
v. 抽痛;（心脏、脉搏等）跳动；“throb”的现在分词
words.ex: His head is throbbing after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的头在跳痛。
words.en: If part of your body throbs, you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.

words.ex: He was in the throes of a difficult decision.
words.ex_cn: 他正处在艰难抉择的痛苦中。
words.en: If someone is experiencing something very unpleasant or emotionally painful, you can say that they are in the throes of it.

words.ex: The thrombus blocked the artery.
words.ex_cn: 血栓阻塞了动脉。
words.en: A thrombus is a blood clot that forms in a blood vessel and remains there.

words.ex: The king sat on the throne.
words.ex_cn: 国王坐在王位上。
words.en: The throne is the special chair used by a king, queen, or emperor during ceremonies, or the position of being a ruler.

words.ex: The rocket's thrust lifted it into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 火箭的推力将它送上了天空。
words.en: To thrust something somewhere means to push it there quickly and forcefully. A thrust is also a powerful push or movement.

words.ex: The mechanic checked the throttle on the car engine.
words.ex_cn: 机械师检查了汽车发动机的节流阀。
words.en: To throttle someone means to kill or injure them by squeezing their throat or tightening something around it and preventing them from breathing. A throttle is a device that controls the amount of fuel going into an engine.

words.tr:
v. 发出砰的一声
n. 重击声；砰的一声
words.ex: The book fell to the floor with a thud.
words.ex_cn: 书掉到地板上，发出一声闷响。
words.en: A thud is a dull sound, such as that which a heavy object makes when it hits something soft.

words.ex: The thunderstorm woke us up at night.
words.ex_cn: 雷雨在夜里把我们吵醒了。
words.en: A thunderstorm is a storm with thunder and lightning and typically also heavy rain or hail.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr:
v. 给…打钩；发出滴嗒声；
n. 钩号；
words.ex: Please tick the box if you agree.
words.ex_cn: 如果你同意，请在方框里打钩。
words.en: The word 'tick' can refer to the sound a clock makes, a very short period of time, a mark used to indicate something, or a type of small insect. As a verb, it can mean to make a ticking sound or to mark something with a tick.

words.tr:
v. （使）发痒；胳肢；逗乐
n. 痒；胳肢；呵痒
words.ex: The feather tickles my arm.
words.ex_cn: 羽毛挠得我手臂发痒。
words.en: If something tickles you, it touches you in a way that makes you laugh or feel slightly uncomfortable, usually because it is touching a sensitive part of your body. If something tickles you, it also makes you feel amused or pleased.

words.ex: He eats tilapia for dinner every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五晚餐吃罗非鱼。
words.en: Tilapia is a type of freshwater fish that is commonly farmed and eaten around the world. It is known for its mild flavor and firm texture.

words.ex: They laid new tile in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们在厨房铺了新的瓷砖。
words.en: A tile is a flat piece of baked clay, carpet, cork, or other material, used especially for covering roofs and floors.

words.tr:
adv. 仍然；还是；
adj. 静止的；
words.ex: He is still waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然在等公交车。
words.en: If a situation that used to exist still exists, it has continued and exists now.

words.tr:
v. （使）倾斜；（使）偏向
n. 倾斜；企图
words.ex: The boy tilt the cup and spill the water.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把杯子倾斜，水洒了出来。
words.en: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.tr:
n. 时间；时期；次数；
v. 计时；安排时间；
words.ex: I don't have time to finish my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我没有时间完成作业。
words.en: Time is the ongoing sequence of existence and events that occurs in an apparently irreversible succession from the past, through the present, into the future.

words.tr:
v. （使）发出叮当声
n. 丁零声；当啷响
words.ex: The wind made the bells tinkle softly.
words.ex_cn: 风使铃铛发出轻轻的叮当声。
words.en: To make a light, clear, ringing sound; a series of such sounds.

words.ex: The wind made the tinkly bells ring softly.
words.ex_cn: 风使那些叮当作响的铃子轻轻响起。
words.en: Making a light, clear, metallic sound; tinkling.

words.ex: He felt tiredness after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一小时后感到疲惫。
words.en: The state of feeling tired or weary.

words.ex: The kids got into a tizzy when the lights went out.
words.ex_cn: 当灯熄灭时，孩子们变得慌乱不安。
words.en: A tizzy is a state of nervous excitement or confusion.

words.ex: He uses a toaster to make toast every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上用烤面包机烤面包。
words.en: A toaster is an electric device for making toast by heating slices of bread on both sides.

words.tr:
v. （幼儿学步时）摇摇摆摆地走；步行；去
n. 晃晃荡荡的步子；刚学走步的小孩；悠闲地走；遛达
words.ex: The baby toddle across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝摇摇摆摆地穿过地板。
words.en: To toddle means to walk with short, unsteady steps, as a very young child does.

words.ex: The family felt togetherness during the holiday dinner.
words.ex_cn: 家人在节日晚餐时感受到了团聚的温暖。
words.en: Togetherness is the feeling of being close to other people, especially because you are sharing experiences or working with them towards the same aim.

words.ex: She packed her toiletries in a small bag.
words.ex_cn: 她把化妆用具装在一个小包里。
words.en: Articles or preparations used in washing, grooming, or personal care, such as soap, shampoo, and toothpaste.

words.ex: The weather was tolerably warm yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的天气还算暖和。
words.en: In a manner that is fairly good or acceptable; to a moderate degree.

words.ex: The government showed toleration for different religions.
words.ex_cn: 政府对不同的宗教表现出容忍。
words.en: The willingness to allow something that one does not necessarily agree with or like.

words.ex: The tombstone was engraved with the deceased's name and date of birth and death.
words.ex_cn: 墓碑上刻着死者的名字和出生及死亡日期。
words.en: A tombstone is a large stone with words carved into it, which is placed on a grave.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.tr: n. 象征物；标志；代金券；代币；
words.ex: The dove is a token of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征物。
words.en: A token is something that represents or stands for something else, especially a piece of metal or plastic that you can use instead of money in some machines or as a symbol of a particular feeling or event.

words.ex: The topmast broke in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 在强风中，顶桅杆折断了。
words.en: A topmast is a mast on a ship above the lower mast and below the topgallant mast.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr: n. 拷打者；拷问者；虐待者
words.ex: The torturer hurt the prisoner badly.
words.ex_cn: 施刑者严重伤害了囚犯。
words.en: A torturer is someone who inflicts severe physical or mental pain on someone as a punishment or in order to force them to do or say something.

words.tr:
n. 小孩；一小杯液体
v. 合计
words.ex: The tot was playing with his toys.
words.ex_cn: 那个小孩正在玩他的玩具。
words.en: A tot can refer to a very young child or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to add up numbers or amounts to reach a total.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.tr: v. 变坚韧；变顽强；变强硬；变困难
words.ex: The leather will toughen as it dries.
words.ex_cn: 皮革干燥后会变得坚韧。
words.en: To toughen someone or something means to make them stronger or more able to deal with difficult conditions or situations.

words.ex: This material is a toughener for the plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这种材料是塑料的增韧剂。
words.en: A substance that is added to a material to make it tougher or more resistant to damage.

words.ex: The boy showed toughness when he kept running despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管疼痛，这个男孩仍然坚持跑步，展现了坚韧。
words.en: The quality of being strong and not easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He won the chess tournament last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周赢得了国际象棋锦标赛。
words.en: A tournament is a competition in which players who win a match continue to play further matches in the competition until just one person or team is left.

words.tr:
v. 牵引；拖
n. 牵引；拖
words.ex: He tows his broken car to the garage.
words.ex_cn: 他把坏掉的车拖到修理厂。
words.en: To pull a vehicle or boat along behind another vehicle, using a rope or chain.

words.ex: The townspeople gathered at the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 村民们聚集在广场上参加节日。
words.en: The people living in a particular town or city.

words.tr: adj. 可追踪的；可追溯的；
words.ex: The package is traceable using the tracking number.
words.ex_cn: 使用跟踪号码可以追踪这个包裹。
words.en: If something is traceable, it can be tracked or followed back to its source or origin.

words.tr: adj. 可贸易的，可买卖的
words.ex: These coins are tradable on the market.
words.ex_cn: 这些硬币可以在市场上交易。
words.en: Capable of being traded or exchanged.

words.tr: n. 权衡；折衷；（公平）交易（同 trade-off）
words.ex: There is a tradeoff between speed and accuracy.
words.ex_cn: 速度和准确性之间存在权衡。
words.en: A tradeoff is a situation where you must accept something you do not like or want in order to get something that you do like or want.

words.ex: The truck pulled a heavy trailer full of boxes.
words.ex_cn: 卡车拖着一辆装满箱子的重型拖车。
words.en: A trailer is a vehicle that is pulled by a car or truck and is used for carrying things. It can also refer to a short promotional film composed of scenes from a movie, television show, or video game.

words.ex: He takes the tram to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上乘电车上班。
words.en: A tram is a vehicle that is used for public transportation in cities and towns, running on tracks laid in the streets.

words.ex: The trainee is learning how to use the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这位受训者正在学习如何使用这台机器。
words.en: A trainee is someone who is being taught how to do a particular job.

words.tr: adj. 安静的；平静的；宁静的；
words.ex: The lake was tranquil in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很安静。
words.en: If a place or situation is tranquil, it is calm, peaceful, and quiet, with no disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: The lake offers tranquillity after a long day.
words.ex_cn: 湖水在漫长的一天后带来宁静。
words.en: Tranquillity refers to a state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: She slept tranquilly through the night.
words.ex_cn: 她整晚都平静地睡着了。
words.en: In a manner that is free from disturbance or turmoil; calmly and peacefully.

words.ex: The doctor tried to tranquilize the anxious patient.
words.ex_cn: 医生试图让焦虑的病人平静下来。
words.en: To tranquilize someone or an animal means to make them calm or unconscious, especially by giving them a drug.

words.tr: adj. 反式的；跨性别的；（有机体）异型结合的; abbr. 交易；交易行为；交流；事务（tran...
words.ex: The trans isomer has the groups on opposite sides.
words.ex_cn: 反式异构体的基团在相对的两侧。
words.en: A prefix meaning "across," "through," "beyond," "over," or "on the other side of," as in transatlantic, transcontinental, or transport.

words.ex: The transcontinental railway was a monumental engineering achievement.
words.ex_cn: 横贯大陆的铁路是一项伟大的工程成就。
words.en: Extending or going across a continent.

words.ex: The transducer converts sound into electric signals.
words.ex_cn: 这个传感器将声音转换为电信号。
words.en: A transducer is a device that converts variations in a physical quantity, such as pressure or brightness, into an electrical signal, or vice versa.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.ex: He committed a transgression by stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷钱犯了过错。
words.en: A transgression is an act that goes against a law, rule, or code of conduct; an offense.

words.ex: The transgressor was punished for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 违反规则的违法者受到了惩罚。
words.en: A transgressor is someone who breaks a law or moral rule.

words.ex: The translator helped him understand the French book.
words.ex_cn: 这位翻译员帮他理解了这本法语书。
words.en: A translator is a person whose job is translating writing or speech from one language to another.

words.tr: n. 可透性; 可传送性，可遗传性，变速性; 可传性
words.ex: The transmissibility of the virus is high.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒的传播性很高。
words.en: The ability of a disease or a virus to be transmitted from one person or organism to another.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.tr: adv. 明亮地，显然地，易觉察地
words.ex: The truth became transparently clear to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 真相对每个人来说都变得显而易见。
words.en: In a way that is easily seen through or detected; without concealment or deception.

words.ex: The trapper caught a fox in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 捕兽者在树林里抓到了一只狐狸。
words.en: A trapper is a person who traps wild animals, especially for their fur.

words.ex: The accident traumatized him for life.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他终生受创。
words.en: If someone is traumatized by an event or situation, it shocks or upsets them very much, and may cause them psychological damage.

words.ex: The accident caused his traumatization.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故导致了他创伤。
words.en: The process or fact of causing severe and lasting emotional shock and pain.

words.ex: The fishermen trawl the sea for fish.
words.ex_cn: 渔民们用拖网在海里捕鱼。
words.en: To trawl means to fish with a trawl net or to search through something thoroughly.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.ex: Two countries signed a treaty to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家签署了一项条约以停止战争。
words.en: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more countries or groups, especially one that is written down and signed by their leaders.

words.ex: The treeless landscape was barren and desolate.
words.ex_cn: 这片无树木的景观荒凉而凄凉。
words.en: An area of land that has no trees.

words.tr: adv. 非常；极其地；极大地
words.ex: She improved tremendously after practicing every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天练习后进步巨大。
words.en: To a very great extent or degree; extremely.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.ex: The workers dug a trench to lay the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 工人们挖了一条沟来铺设管道。
words.en: A trench is a long, narrow ditch. In warfare, trenches are dug by troops to provide shelter from enemy fire.

words.tr: n. 分类；伤员验伤分类
words.ex: The hospital implemented a triage system to prioritize patients.
words.ex_cn: 医院实施了分类系统以优先处理患者。
words.en: The process of determining the priority of patients' treatments based on the severity of their condition.

words.ex: The tribunal decided the case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 法庭迅速作出了裁决。
words.en: A tribunal is a special court or committee that is officially chosen to examine a particular problem or situation.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He has high triglyceride levels in his blood.
words.ex_cn: 他的血液中甘油三酯水平很高。
words.en: A triglyceride is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids. Triglycerides are the main constituents of body fat in humans and other animals, as well as vegetable fat.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The trombonist plays in a jazz band.
words.ex_cn: 这位长号手在一个爵士乐队里演奏。
words.en: A trombonist is a musician who plays the trombone.

words.tr: n. 惹事生非者；麻烦制造者；捣乱者
words.ex: He was known as a troublemaker in the neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 他在邻里间以捣乱者著称。
words.en: A troublemaker is someone who deliberately causes problems or difficulties for others.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；讨厌的；
words.ex: The noisy neighbors are troublesome.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的邻居令人烦恼。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as troublesome, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or worries.

words.ex: The team trounced their rivals in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在决赛中大胜对手。
words.en: To defeat someone decisively in a competition or fight.

words.tr: n. 停战（协定）；休战（协定）
words.ex: The two sides agreed to a truce.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意停火。
words.en: A truce is an agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting or arguing for a certain time.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；正确的；
words.ex: The story is true.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是真实的。
words.en: in accordance with fact or reality

words.tr:
v. 缓慢或吃力地走
n. 长途跋涉
words.ex: He trudges through the snow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跋涉穿过雪地。
words.en: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically because of exhaustion or harsh conditions.

words.ex: He plays the trumpet in the school band.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校乐队里吹喇叭。
words.en: A trumpet is a brass musical instrument with a flared bell and three valves, producing a bright, penetrating tone.

words.tr: v. 缓慢滚动；缓缓行进；艰难移动
words.ex: The boy trundles his toy car down the hallway.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把他的玩具车在走廊里推着走。
words.en: To move slowly and noisily, especially of a wheeled vehicle or object.

words.ex: The trustee manages the money for the children.
words.ex_cn: 受托人管理孩子们的钱。
words.en: A trustee is a person or firm that holds and administers property or assets for the benefit of a third party.

words.tr: adj. （太）相信别人的，充满信任的，无疑心的 adv. 充满信任地
words.ex: He is a trustful friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: A trustful person is someone who is willing to believe that other people are good and honest.

words.tr: n. 信任; 相信，信赖
words.ex: His trustfulness makes people feel safe around him.
words.ex_cn: 他的诚实可信让人们在他身边感到安心。
words.en: The quality of being trustful; the state of being inclined to believe or trust others.

words.tr: adv. 深信不疑地；信任地
words.ex: He trustfully accepted the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他满怀信任地接受了这份礼物。
words.en: In a manner that shows a willingness to trust others; with trust.

words.ex: The tsunami destroyed the village near the sea.
words.ex_cn: 海啸摧毁了海边的村庄。
words.en: A tsunami is a very large ocean wave caused by an underwater earthquake or volcanic eruption.

words.ex: He poured water into the tub.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进了桶里。
words.en: A tub is a large, open container that you fill with water and use to wash yourself or to wash clothes.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with tuberculosis last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有结核病。
words.en: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.

words.tr:
v. 把…塞进狭窄的空间；把…藏入
n. 褶皱；零食
words.ex: He tucked the letter into his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他把信塞进了口袋里。
words.en: If you tuck something somewhere, you put it there so that it is safe, comfortable, or neat.

words.tr:
n. 用力拉；拖拽；拖船
v. 用力拉；使劲拖；拖拽
words.ex: He gave a strong tug on the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他用力拉了绳子一下。
words.en: If you tug something or tug at it, you give it a quick and usually strong pull.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.ex: The doctor found a tumor in his lung.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的肺里发现了一个肿瘤。
words.en: A tumor is a mass of tissue that's formed by an accumulation of abnormal cells. Normally, the cells in your body age, die, and are replaced by new cells. With cancer and other tumors, something disrupts this cycle. Tumor cells grow, even though the body does not need them, and unlike normal old cells, they don't die. As this process goes on, the tumor continues to grow as more and more cells are added to the mass.

words.ex: Reindeer live in the tundra near the North Pole.
words.ex_cn: 驯鹿生活在北极附近的苔原上。
words.en: A tundra is a vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.

words.ex: He lives in Turin with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人住在都灵。
words.en: Turin is a city in northern Italy, known for its rich history, culture, and as a major business and cultural centre in Europe.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.tr: adj. 翻下的，翻折的 n. 低落; 拒绝; 谢绝; 可翻下部分
words.ex: He wore a shirt with a turndown collar.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件翻领衬衫。
words.en: A refusal or rejection of an offer, proposal, or request.

words.ex: Please turn off the light before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 离开前请关灯。
words.en: If you turn off a device or machine, you stop it from operating by pressing a button or moving a switch.

words.ex: The castle has a small turret on each corner.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡的每个角落都有一个小塔。
words.en: A turret is a small tower on top of a building, especially a castle, or a structure on a military vehicle that can turn around and from which guns are fired.

words.tr: adj. 有角塔的; 角塔状的
words.ex: The old castle has turreted towers.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡有带塔楼的塔。
words.en: Having turrets or resembling a turret.

words.ex: He twitched the rope to pull the box closer.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把箱子拉近了些。
words.en: To make a sudden, small movement with a part of your body, especially because you are nervous or in pain.

words.tr: n. 大亨；巨头；大企业家；
words.ex: He became a tycoon after building a big oil company.
words.ex_cn: 他在建立了一家大型石油公司后成为了一位大亨。
words.en: A tycoon is a person who is successful in business or industry and has become rich and powerful.

words.tr: n. 打字; 打字稿; 打字术 v. 打字，用打字机打( typewrite的现在分词 )
words.ex: He is practicing typewriting every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都在练习打字。
words.en: The activity or skill of writing with a typewriter.

words.ex: Typhus is a serious infectious disease caused by bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 斑疹伤寒是一种由细菌引起的严重传染病。
words.en: Typhus is a group of infectious diseases that are caused by rickettsial bacteria and are transmitted by arthropods such as fleas, lice, and ticks.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.ex: The tyrannous king ruled with fear.
words.ex_cn: 这位暴虐的国王用恐惧统治。
words.en: Using or exercising power in a cruel or arbitrary way.

words.tr: adv. 压制地；暴虐地，残暴地
words.ex: The king ruled tyrannously, ignoring the needs of his people.
words.ex_cn: 国王暴虐地统治，无视人民的需要。
words.en: In a manner characteristic of a tyrant; oppressively or despotically.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: He has an ulcer from eating too much spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多辣食而得了溃疡。
words.en: An ulcer is a sore area on the skin or inside the body that is very painful and may bleed or produce a poisonous substance.

words.tr: n. 紫外线辐射；紫外光；
words.ex: The ultraviolet from the sun can hurt your skin.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的紫外线会伤害你的皮肤。
words.en: Ultraviolet light or radiation has a wavelength shorter than that of visible light but longer than X-rays.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；不能理解的；无责任的
words.ex: The manager made unaccountable decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理做出了无法解释的决定。
words.en: If someone or something is unaccountable, there is no way of explaining why they behave in a particular way, and it is often strange or surprising.

words.ex: He is unafraid to speak his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他不怕表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you are unafraid, you are not afraid of doing something or of something happening.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.tr: adj. 未经许可的；未经授权的；
words.ex: He entered the building through an unauthorized door.
words.ex_cn: 他通过一扇未经许可的门进入了大楼。
words.en: If something is unauthorized, it has been done without the official permission of someone in authority.

words.tr: adj. 不相信的；怀疑的；不信教的
words.ex: His unbelieving attitude towards the new project was evident.
words.ex_cn: 他对新项目的怀疑态度显而易见。
words.en: Refusing to accept something as true or real; skeptical.

words.tr: adj. 不可战胜的；坚不可摧的
words.ex: He had an unconquerable spirit.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种不可战胜的精神。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unconquerable, you mean that they cannot be defeated or overcome.

words.ex: The teacher noticed a pattern of underachievement in some students.
words.ex_cn: 老师注意到一些学生中存在低成就的模式。
words.en: The failure to achieve as much as one is capable of.

words.tr: v. 对……重视不够，对……强调不够
words.ex: The report underemphasizes the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 报告对定期锻炼的重要性强调不够。
words.en: To give insufficient emphasis to something; to not emphasize something enough.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 保守的说法；不充分的叙述；掩饰；低调
words.ex: His description of the accident was an understatement.
words.ex_cn: 他对事故的描述是轻描淡写的。
words.en: If you say that a statement is an understatement, you mean that it does not fully express the extent to which something is true.

words.ex: She unbuttoned her coat and stepped inside.
words.ex_cn: 她解开外套的扣子，走进了屋内。
words.en: to unfasten the buttons of a piece of clothing

words.tr: adj. 不关心的；漠视的；不相干的
words.ex: He was unconcerned about the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他对噪音毫不在意。
words.en: If you are unconcerned about something, you are not interested in it or worried about it.

words.tr: adj. 不分心的；注意力集中的；
words.ex: He stayed undistracted while studying for the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在备考时保持不分心。
words.en: If you are undistracted, you are able to concentrate on something without being diverted or interrupted by other things.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.ex: Strong foundations underpin the building.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基支撑着这栋建筑。
words.en: To support, strengthen, or provide a foundation for something.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.ex: It is unethical to lie to customers.
words.ex_cn: 对顾客撒谎是不道德的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as unethical, you think it is wrong and unacceptable according to a society's rules or people's beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 不平坦的；不均匀的；
words.ex: The road is uneven and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路不平坦，很难开车。
words.en: Something that is uneven is not regular, consistent, or equal.

words.tr: adv. 可靠地；无穷尽地；不倦地
words.ex: She unfailingly arrives on time.
words.ex_cn: 她总是准时到达。
words.en: If you say that someone does something unfailingly, you are emphasizing that they always do it and never let anyone down.

words.ex: The photo was unflattering and made her look older than she really was.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片不讨好，让她看起来比实际年龄大。
words.en: If you describe something as unflattering, you mean that it makes someone or something seem less attractive or appealing than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 不可原谅的，难以饶恕的
words.ex: He made an unforgivable mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他犯了一个不可原谅的错误。
words.en: If you say that something is unforgivable, you mean that it is very bad or cruel, and completely unacceptable.

words.ex: It was unfortunate that he missed the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他没赶上公交车，真是不幸。
words.en: If you describe someone as unfortunate, you mean that something unpleasant or unlucky has happened to them. You can also describe the unpleasant things that happen to them as unfortunate.

words.tr: adj. 不顺从的；未尽职的；不孝的
words.ex: Her undutiful behavior towards her parents was widely criticized.
words.ex_cn: 她对父母的不孝行为广受批评。
words.en: If you describe someone as undutiful, you mean that they are not doing what they are expected to do or are not behaving in the way they are expected to behave.

words.ex: He ate unhealthily and rarely exercised.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食不健康，很少锻炼。
words.en: In a way that is harmful to health.

words.ex: She answered the question unhesitatingly.
words.ex_cn: 她毫不犹豫地回答了问题。
words.en: If you say that someone does something unhesitatingly, you mean that they do it immediately and confidently, without any doubt or hesitation.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.tr: adj. 不受约束的；无拘无束的
words.ex: He sang uninhibited at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上毫无拘束地唱歌。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as uninhibited, you mean that they express their opinions and feelings openly, and behave as they want to, without worrying what other people think.

words.ex: He did an unlawful act and was arrested.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一件非法的事，被逮捕了。
words.en: If something is unlawful, it is against the law.

words.tr: adj. 不能证明为正当的；无可辩解的；没有道理的
words.ex: The price increase was deemed unjustifiable by the consumers.
words.ex_cn: 消费者认为价格上涨是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unjustifiable, you mean that it cannot be justified because it is wrong or unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 不可知的；无法知道的
words.ex: The mysteries of space are unknowable to us.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙的奥秘对我们来说是不可知的。
words.en: If something is unknowable, it is impossible for anyone to understand or know about it.

words.tr: adj. 未满足的，未相遇的，未应付的
words.ex: The unmet needs of children must be addressed.
words.ex_cn: 儿童未满足的需求必须得到解决。
words.en: If a need, demand, or expectation is unmet, it has not been satisfied or fulfilled.

words.ex: He is unprejudiced and treats everyone fairly.
words.ex_cn: 他没有偏见，公平对待每个人。
words.en: If you describe someone as unprejudiced, you mean that they are not influenced by an unreasonable dislike of or preference for a person, group, or thing.

words.ex: The remote village is unreachable by road during the rainy season.
words.ex_cn: 这个偏远村庄在雨季期间无法通过道路到达。
words.en: If you describe something as unreachable, you mean that it cannot be reached, accessed, or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 未实现；没有实现的；没能实现的；
words.ex: He still has unrealized dreams of becoming a painter.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然有未实现的成为画家的梦想。
words.en: If something is unrealized, it has not been achieved or made to happen.

words.tr: adj. 寻常的；不值得注意的
words.ex: The landscape was unremarkable, just a stretch of flat fields.
words.ex_cn: 这片风景很平凡，只是一片平坦的田野。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unremarkable, you mean that they are very ordinary, without many exciting, original, or attractive qualities.

words.tr: adj. 不够好的；不能令人满意的；
words.ex: The food was unsatisfactory.
words.ex_cn: 食物不够好。
words.en: If you describe something as unsatisfactory, you mean that it is not as good as it should be, and cannot be considered acceptable.

words.ex: The table is unstable and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子不稳，可能会倒。
words.en: Something that is unstable is not firm and therefore not safe, or is likely to change suddenly and become worse.

words.tr: adv. 不稳定地；摇摆地（unsteady 的副词）; vt. 使不稳定
words.ex: He walked unsteadily after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他走路摇摇晃晃。
words.en: In a manner that is not steady or stable; with a tendency to wobble or shake.

words.tr: adj. 不适宜的；不合适的；
words.ex: This shirt is unsuitable for the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫不适合寒冷的天气。
words.en: If someone or something is unsuitable for a particular purpose or situation, they are not appropriate for it.

words.ex: The unsuitability of the candidate for the position was evident during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 面试过程中，候选人对于该职位的不适合显而易见。
words.en: The quality or state of being unsuitable or inappropriate for a particular purpose or situation.

words.tr: prep. 直到; 对，向; 在…旁边
words.ex: He waited unto nightfall.
words.ex_cn: 他一直等到天黑。
words.en: Unto is an old-fashioned or literary word that means 'to' or 'until'.

words.ex: He is upbeat about his new job.
words.ex_cn: 他对新工作感到乐观。
words.en: If people or their opinions are upbeat, they are cheerful and full of hope.

words.tr:
adj. 漫长而艰难的；
adv. 朝上坡方向；
words.ex: Losing weight is an uphill task for many people.
words.ex_cn: 对许多人来说，减肥是一项漫长而艰难的任务。
words.en: If something is uphill, it is going up a slope or hill. If you say that something is uphill, you mean that it is difficult and requires effort.

words.tr:
adj. 高档的；高级的
adv. 高档地；高级地
words.ex: This shop sells up-market clothes.
words.ex_cn: 这家店出售高档服装。
words.en: Up-market refers to goods, services, or areas that are designed to appeal to or are used by people who have a lot of money and like to spend it on expensive, high-quality things.

words.ex: They eat at an upscale restaurant every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在一家高档餐厅吃饭。
words.en: If you describe something as upscale, you mean it is of high quality or intended for people who are wealthy.

words.ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 会议的结果是一个新计划。
words.en: The final result or outcome of a situation or event.

words.ex: He found uranium in the old rock sample.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧岩石样本中发现了铀。
words.en: A heavy, silvery-white metallic element, radioactive and toxic, used as a fuel in nuclear reactors and in the manufacture of nuclear weapons.

words.tr:
n. 带位员；接待员；门房
v. 引领；招待；做招待员
words.ex: The usher showed us to our seats in the theater.
words.ex_cn: 带位员带我们到了剧院的座位。
words.en: An usher is someone who shows people where to sit, especially at a formal event such as a wedding or a concert. As a verb, to usher means to show someone where to go or to lead them somewhere.

words.ex: He dreams of a perfect utopia where everyone is happy.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想一个每个人都很幸福的完美乌托邦。
words.en: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.

words.ex: The beach was crowded with vacationers enjoying the sun.
words.ex_cn: 海滩上挤满了享受阳光的度假者。
words.en: A vacationer is someone who is on vacation, especially someone who is traveling or staying somewhere for pleasure.

words.tr: v. 接种疫苗；预防接种
words.ex: The doctor will vaccinate the child tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 医生明天会给这个孩子接种疫苗。
words.en: To vaccinate someone is to give them a vaccine, usually by injection, to prevent them from getting a disease.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.ex: The water valve is broken and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这个水阀坏了，需要修理。
words.en: A valve is a device attached to a pipe or a tube which controls the flow of air or liquid through it.

words.tr:
n. 香草；香草精
adj. 香草味的；寻常的；无特色的
words.ex: He likes vanilla ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢香草冰淇淋。
words.en: Vanilla is a flavoring derived from orchids of the genus Vanilla, primarily from the Mexican species, flat-leaved vanilla (V. planifolia). The word vanilla, derived from the diminutive of the Spanish word vaina (vaina itself meaning sheath or pod), is translated simply as 'little pod'.

words.ex: The desert has little vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠植被很少。
words.en: Vegetation refers to plants in general, or the plants that are found in a particular area. It can also refer to a life that is dull or inactive, often due to illness or lack of exercise.

words.ex: The doctor checked the vein in his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他手臂上的静脉。
words.en: A vein is a tube in your body that carries blood towards your heart. It can also refer to a thin layer of a mineral in rock, or a particular style or mood in writing or speech.

words.tr: n. 威尼斯（意大利东北部城市）
words.ex: We visited Venice last summer.
words.ex_cn: 我们去年夏天去了威尼斯。
words.en: Venice is a city in northeastern Italy and the capital of the Veneto region. It is situated across a group of 118 small islands that are separated by canals and linked by over 400 bridges.

words.ex: The car's velocity increased on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在高速公路上的速度增加了。
words.en: Velocity is the speed at which something moves in a particular direction.

words.ex: The shop specializes in the vendition of handmade crafts.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店专门销售手工工艺品。
words.en: The act of selling or the state of being sold.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: Open the window to ventilate the room.
words.ex_cn: 打开窗户给房间通风。
words.en: To ventilate means to cause fresh air to enter and move around a room, building, etc., or to express your opinions or feelings about something openly.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.ex: He writes a verse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上写一首诗。
words.en: A verse is one of the parts into which a poem, a song, or a chapter of the Bible or the Koran is divided.

words.ex: The red team played versus the blue team.
words.ex_cn: 红队与蓝队比赛。
words.en: Used to indicate the two sides in a competition or conflict.

words.tr:
n. 背心；马甲；汗衫
v. 授予；使穿衣
words.ex: He wears a black vest over his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件黑色背心，上面是衬衫。
words.en: A vest is a piece of clothing without sleeves that you wear over a shirt.

words.ex: He is a veteran player with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的老练球员。
words.en: A veteran is someone who has a lot of experience in a particular field or activity, especially in the armed forces.

words.tr: n. 代理；副职；恶习；缺点；
words.ex: He acted as vice for the manager during her absence.
words.ex_cn: 在经理缺席期间，他担任代理。
words.en: A vice is a moral fault or weakness in someone's character.

words.tr:
n. （葡萄酒）制造年份；
adj. 古老的；
words.ex: This wine is from a vintage of 2015.
words.ex_cn: 这款葡萄酒产自2015年的酿造年份。
words.en: Vintage is used to describe something that is not just old, but is also of high quality and typical of the best of its kind.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.tr: adj. 发声的；嗓音的；直言不讳的；
words.ex: He made a vocal sound to get attention.
words.ex_cn: 他发出声音来引起注意。
words.en: If you are vocal about something, you express your opinions or feelings about it in a strong and public way.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.ex: He signed a waiver before the ride.
words.ex_cn: 他在坐过山车前签了免责协议。
words.en: A waiver is an official document or statement that gives up a right or claim, especially in legal contexts.

words.ex: The boxes are stored in the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 这些箱子存放在仓库里。
words.en: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before their export or distribution for sale.

words.ex: The warrior fought bravely to protect his village.
words.ex_cn: 这位战士勇敢地战斗以保护他的村庄。
words.en: A warrior is a person who is engaged in or experienced in battle, or who shows or has shown great vigor, courage, or aggressiveness, as in politics or athletics.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: The old factory became a wasteland after it closed.
words.ex_cn: 工厂关闭后，它变成了一片荒地。
words.en: A wasteland is an area of land that is uncultivated or uninhabited, often because it is barren or devastated.

words.ex: Mr. Watkins is a renowned historian.
words.ex_cn: 沃特金斯先生是一位著名的历史学家。
words.en: A surname, commonly associated with individuals like the American actor and comedian.

words.ex: He uses wavelet to analyze sound signals.
words.ex_cn: 他使用小波来分析声音信号。
words.en: A wavelet is a small wave; a ripple.

words.tr: n. 幸福; 鞭痕; <书>福利; 杖痕 vt. 在…上抽打出条状鞭痕
words.ex: The weal on his back was a reminder of his harsh treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他背上的鞭痕是他遭受严酷对待的提醒。
words.en: Weal refers to the well-being, happiness, or prosperity of a person or group, or a mark on the skin made by a blow from a whip or similar instrument.

words.tr:
n. 楔子；三角木；楔形物
v. 把…楔住 ；将…挤入（或塞进、插入）
words.ex: He used a wedge to split the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用楔子把木头劈开。
words.en: A wedge is a piece of wood, metal, or other material with one thick end and one thin edge, used to keep something in position or to split something apart.

words.ex: The company charges a fee for wharfage.
words.ex_cn: 公司对码头使用收取费用。
words.en: Wharfage refers to the charge made for the use of a wharf, especially for loading or unloading goods.

words.ex: His whine about the food made everyone annoyed.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物的抱怨让所有人都感到厌烦。
words.en: If someone or something whines, they make a long, high-pitched noise, especially one which sounds sad or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 哀诉者；悲嗥者；啜泣者
words.ex: He was always the first to complain, a true whiner.
words.ex_cn: 他总是第一个抱怨，真是个十足的哀诉者。
